001.title: Introduction to Aerospace Science Engineering
001.description: Description of the field of aerospace engineering with examples from industry, government, and research. Aerospace engineering principles, ethics, and responsibilities.

127.title: Applied Aircraft Aerodynamics
127.description: Principles, governing equations, and predictive theories for aircraft aerodynamics. Lift and drag of 2D airfoils, 3D wings, and high-lift devices.

133.title: Finite Element Methods in Structures
133.description: Introduction to the aerospace structural design process. History of aircraft and spacecraft materials. Effects of loading beyond elastic limit. Deflections and stresses due to combined loading. Virtual work principles, and finite element methods. Applications to aerospace structures.
133.prereq_text: ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better.

140.title: Rocket Propulsion
140.description: Fluid and thermodynamics of rocket engines, liquid and solid rocket propulsion. Space propulsion concepts and space mission requirements.
140.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken identical EAE 189A prior to Fall Quarter 2013.

010.title: African-American Culture & Society
010.description: Critical examination of the historical, political, social, and economic factors that have affected the development and status of African-American people in contemporary society.

050.title: Black Popular Culture
050.description: Survey of the African American images in popular culture (film, television, comedy, sports and music).

107D.title: African Descent Communities & Cultures in Europe
107D.description: Study of the origin and development of African Descent communities and cultures in Europe.

123.title: Black Female Experience in Contemporary Society
123.description: Black female social, intellectual, and psychological development. Black women's contributions in history, literature, and social science; life experiences of Black women and philosophical underpinnings of the feminist movement.
123.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

130.title: Education in the African-American Community
130.description: Examination of the history of the education of African Americans in the United States. Examination and critique of contemporary theories concerning the schooling of African Americans. (Former AAS 140.)

136.title: Black Women & Food
136.description: Black women’s relationships with food. Historical and contemporary representations, self-representations, and misrepresentations in popular culture. Images of African American women in their roles as providers, producers, preparers and consumers of food in both domestic and public arenas from the periods of Black people’s enslavement up through the 21st century.

138.title: AIDS, Race, Gender & Sexuality in Black Communities
138.description: Critical examination of how the intersections of gender, religion, race, sexuality, and socioeconomic status have perpetuated the marginalization of African Americans in public health. Focus on vulnerabilities to HIV/AIDS in Black communities.

152.title: Major Voices in Black World Literature
152.description: Recurrence of cultural tropes in the works of major black world authors and formation of an African-oriented canon. Principal activities include critical reading and discovery of literature as a cultural resource.

181.title: Hip Hop in Urban America
181.description: History, aesthetics, urban context, and economics of hip-hop in the US, and its globalization. Hip-hop's four artistic elements-rap, deejaying, breakdance, and aerosol art-allow the examination of issues of race, ethnicity, and gender in youth culture and American society.
181.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in African-American & African Studies
192.description: Supervised internship in community, government, or private institutions, in all subject areas offered by the African American & African Studies Program.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 12 units of upper division study in African American & African Studies (AAS) courses; upper division standing.

197T.title: Tutoring in Afro-American Studies
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of major committee; upper division standing with major in African American & African Studies.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

298A.title: Directed Group Study in African American & African Diaspora Studies

298B.title: Directed Group Study in African Studies
298B.description: Directed group study in African Studies.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Selected topics in agricultural and environmental chemistry, presented by students.

010.title: Introduction to Agricultural & Environmental Technologies
010.description: Technologies of agriculture and the environmental sciences. History & revolution of industrial technology and its impacts on agriculture, environment, energy, and bioproducts; types of sensing technologies; communication and information transfer technologies; artificial intelligence, technologies for control of automatic processes; technologies for the production of food, bioproducts, clean energy and water purification; gene-editing technology; wearable technologies.

121.title: Controlled Environments for Plants & Animals
121.description: Principles of environmental control (temperature, humidity, lighting, CO2, air circulation, air quality) for plants and animals. Psychrometrics and applications. Energy-efficient building envelopes for greenhouses, vertical farmings, and animal barns. Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, lighting and CO2 enrichment systems, growing substrates, and irrigation systems. Control systems (sensors and sensing for automated control). Visiting controlled environment facilities.
121.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Agricultural & Environmental Technology; or consent of instructor.

018.title: Business Law
018.description: General principles of business law in the areas of contracts, business organization, real property, uniform commercial code, sales, commercial paper, employment relations, and creditor-debtor against a background of the history and functioning of our present legal system.

100A.title: Intermediate Microeconomics: Theory of Production & Consumption
100A.description: Theory of individual consumer and market demand; theory of production and supply of agricultural products, with particular reference to the individual firm; price determination, and employment of resources under pure competition.
100A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECN 100.
100A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 019A C- or better,  MAT 019B C- or better,  MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better,  MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better,  MAT 021B C- or better)).

100B.title: Intermediate Microeconomics: Imperfect Competition, Markets & Welfare Economics
100B.description: Price determination, and employment of resources under conditions of monopoly, oligopoly, and monopolistic competition.
100B.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; ((ECN 001A C-  or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better,  MAT 016B C- or better,  MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better,  MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better,  MAT 021B C- or better)); ARE 018 C- or better.

106.title: Econometric Theory & Applications
106.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data to solve problems in managerial economics. Topics include the linear regression model, methods to resolve data problems, and the economic interpretation of results.
106.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have enrolled in or completed ECN 140.
106.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better); STA 103 C- or better.

112.title: Fundamentals of Organization Management
112.description: Role of organizational design and behavior in business and public agencies. Principles of planning, decision making, individual behavior, management, leadership, informal groups, conflict and change in the organization.

115A.title: Economic Development
115A.description:
Major issues encountered in emerging from international poverty, problems of growth and structural change, human welfare, population
growth and health, labor markets and internal migration. Important issues of policy concerning international trade and industrialization.
115A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

115BY.title: Economic Development
115BY.description: Macroeconomic issues of developing countries. Problems in generating capital, conduct of monetary and fiscal policies, foreign aid and investment.  Issues of policy concerning international borrowing and external debt of developing countries.
115BY.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

118.title: Tax Accounting
118.description: Development and application of a framework to understand the tax effects of typical management decisions on both entities and their owners. Impacts that different methods of taxation have on business entities with emphasis on tax planning, using income and deduction strategies, retirement plans, and choice of business entity for tax minimization. Irregularly offered.
118.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better; ARE 018 recommended.

132.title: Cooperative Business Enterprises
132.description: Study of cooperative business enterprise in the United States and elsewhere; economic theories of behavior, principles of operation, finance, decision-making, and taxation.
132.prereq_text: ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better.

133.title: Introduction to Behavioral Economics
133.description: Inclusion of non-economic factors such as psychological principles in economic decisions and model predictions. Emphasis on behavioral principles, resulting strategies and implications for diverse market settings.
133.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better).

138.title: International Commodity & Resource Markets
138.description: Basic nature and scope of international trade in agricultural commodities, agricultural inputs, and natural resources. Market dimensions and policy institutions. Case studies to illustrate import and export problems associated with different regions and commodities.
138.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; ARE 100B C- or better.

142.title: Personal Finance
142.description: Management of income and expenditures by the household. Use of consumer credit, savings, and insurance by households. Principles of tax, retirement, and estate planning.

143.title: Basics of Investing
143.description: Survey of investment institutions, sources of investment information, and portfolio theory. Analysis of the stock, bond and real estate markets from the perspective of the investor.
143.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students concurrently enrolled in or who have completed ARE 171 or ARE 171A.

144.title: Real Estate Economics
144.description: Economic theory, analysis, and institutions of real estate markets and related financial markets. Techniques for appraising property values. Cases drawn from the raw land, single family, multifamily, industrial and office real estate markets.

155.title: Operations Research & Management Science
155.description: Introduction to quantitative methods used to analyze business and economic processes: decision analysis for management, mathematical programming, competitive analysis, and other methods.
155.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better); STA 103 C- or better.

171.title: Principles of Finance
171.description: Principles of corporate financial management. Time value of money, interest rates, principles of valuation, NPV, risk and return, and cost of capital.
171.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECN 134 or ECN 134Y.
171.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; ARE 106 C- or better; (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better.

176.title: Environmental Economics
176.description:
Role of the environment in economic activity and methods for protecting
and enhancing environmental quality; implications of market failures for public policy; design of environmental policy; theory of welfare measurement; measuring the benefits of environmental improvement.
176.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better or ECN 100A C- or better or ECN 100AV C- or better or ECN 100 C- or better.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Internship experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Agricultural & Resource Economics. Internships are supervised by a member of the staff.

194HA.title: Senior Research Thesis
194HA.description: Independent study program and seminar on research methods in applied economics. Supervised completion of a first draft of a research thesis.
194HA.prereq_text: ARE 100B C- or better; ARE 106 C- or better; ARE 155 C- or better; consent of instructor; application required.

197T.title: Tutoring in Managerial Economics
197T.description: Undergraduates assist the instructor by tutoring students in one of the department's regularly scheduled courses.
197T.prereq_text: Senior standing in Managerial Economics and consent of Department Chairperson.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200A.title: Microeconomic Theory
200A.description: Linear and non-linear optimization theory applied to develop the theory of the profit-maximizing firm and the utility-maximizing consumer.

202A.title: Introduction to Applied Research Methods
202A.description: Study of philosophy and methodology of applied research in agricultural economics. Methods of conceptualization of researchable topics. Method of communication and constructive criticism.

204A.title: Microeconomic Analysis I
204A.description: Behavior of consumers and producers and their interactions; tools and methods needed to analyze economic behavior in the marketplace.  Application of those methods to real-world problems.
204A.prereq_text: ARE 100B or ECN 100; advanced undergraduates with consent of instructor.

215C.title: Microdevelopment Theory & Methods II
215C.description: Extension of development theory and microeconomic methods. Agricultural growth and technological change; poverty and income inequality; multisectoral, including village and regional models. Computable general equilibrium methods and applications.

231.title: Supply & Demand for Agricultural Products
231.description: Analysis of supply and demand for agricultural commodities emphasizing the effective use of microeconomic theory with econometric methods, and other empirical procedures, in conducting applied analysis of supply and demand at the firm and industry level.
231.prereq_text: ARE 200A; ARE 202A; ARE 240A; or consent of instructor.

239.title: Econometric Foundations
239.description: Prepares students for econometric theory and empirical work by examining the statistical foundation of econometrics. Special attention is paid to problems specific to non-experimental data common to social sciences. Topics from matrix algebra are also covered.
239.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

240D.title: Cross Section Econometrics
240D.description: Estimation and inference for nonlinear regression models for cross-section data; models for discrete data and for limited dependent variables; models for  panel data; additional topics such as bootstrap and semiparametric regression.

256A.title: Applied Econometrics I
256A.description: First of two courses in the Masters-level econometrics sequence. The linear regression model and generalizations are applied to topics in applied economics. Tools for empirical research for problems requiring more sophisticated tools than standard regression models are emphasized.
256A.prereq_text: ARE 106 or ECN 140; or consent of instructor.

277.title: Natural Resource Economics
277.description: Application of capital theory and dynamic methods to issues of optimal use of renewable and nonrenewable resources. Examination of policy issues associated with forests, fisheries, groundwater, energy resources, watersheds, soil, global climate, and wildlife.

298.title: Directed Group Study
298.description: Advanced study through special seminars, informal group studies, or group research on problems for analysis and experimentation. Sections:(1) Managerial Economics; (2) Agricultural Policy; (3) Community & Regional Development; (4) Natural Resources; (5) Human Resources; (6) Research Methods & Quantitative Analysis.

299.title: Individual Study
299.description: Sections: (1) Managerial Economics; (2) Agricultural Policy; (3) Community & Regional Development; (4) Natural Resources; (5) Human Resources; (6) Research Methods & Quantitative Analysis; and (7) Dissertation Research Prospectus.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship off and on campus in areas of agricultural education.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.description: AED support moved to ANS, informed July 2018 by Lisa Holmes. Subject moved in ICMS, took some time.

160.title: Vocational Education
160.description: Philosophy and organization of vocational education, with particular reference to educational principles for agriculture commerce, home economics, and industry.

172.title: Multimedia Productions
172.description: Design and production of educational, technical, and professional multimedia presentations. Instructional or professional presentations using a variety of media, including slides, video, transparencies, and computer-generated graphics.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship off and on campus in areas of agricultural education.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

010.title: Introduction to American Studies
010.description: Ideals, conflicts, and realities defining American Cultures through study of popular music, advertising, and other media. Themes include Imagining America, Citizenship and Belonging, and Cultural/Spatial Practices.

025V.title: United States as a Business Culture
025V.description: Business as a cultural system and its relation to religion, politics, arts, science, technology, and material culture; business themes of success, creativity, invention, and competition in American autobiographies, fiction, advice literature, film, and television; cultures of the workplace; multinational business.

030.title: Images of America & Americans in Popular Culture
030.description: Investigation of verbal and visual discourses about American identity in various popular culture products, including film, television, radio, music, fiction, art, advertising, and commercial experiences; discourses about the United States in the popular culture of other societies.

059.title: Music & American Culture
059.description: Examination of music and American culture. Studies will explore music in its cultural contexts, which may include examinations of recording and broadcasting, of race, class, and gender, the role of technology, and relationships between musical production, consumption and listening.

095.title: Careers & Identity in American Culture
095.description: Defining one's identity through the career. Life course, preparation, and choices. Personality and career. Ethics. Gender, ethnicity, sexuality, and social class in the workplace. Transnational workplace. Conflicts between the career and other social roles.

100.title: Methods in American Studies
100.description: Design and implementation of interdisciplinary research, analysis and writing for American Studies and other cultural studies fields. Library and Internet research skills, project/problem definition, methods for study of texts, individuals, communities. Hand-on, skill-building, focused reading, discussion.

101C.title: Special Topics: Material Aspects of American Culture
101C.description: Intensive reading, writing, and special projects. Interdisciplinary group study of special topics in American Culture Studies, designed for non-majors as well as majors.

110.title: A Decade in American Civilization
110.description: Close examination of a single decade in American civilization; the connections between the history, literature, arts, customs, and ideas of Americans living in the decade. Issues and representations of race, class, gender, age, and sexuality in the decade.

152.title: The Lives of Children in America
152.description: Multiple histories and cultural specificity of childhood and adolescence in the United States.

155.title: Eating in America
155.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the culture of food in America. Exploration of eating as a richly symbolic event integral to how Americans express and negotiate values, politics and identity.

156.title: Race, Culture & Society in the United States
156.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the significance of race in the making of America; how race shapes culture, identities and social processes in the United States; the interweaving of race with gender, class and nationhood in self and community.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and chairperson of American Studies Program.

100.title: Comparative Vertebrate Organology
100.description: Functional anatomy of major organ systems in vertebrates. Each system examined from cellular to gross level in fish, birds, and mammals. Emphasis on how differentiated cell types are integrated into tissues and organs to perform diverse physiological functions.
100.prereq_text: (BIS 001A,  BIS 001B) or (BIS 002A,  BIS 002B).

192.title: Internship in Anesthesiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in anesthesia and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

218A.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
218A.description: Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.
218A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division undergraduate introduction to the biology of behavior, such as PSC 101, PSC 122, PSC 123, NPB 102, NPB 150, NPB 152, WFC 141, ENT 104, or ANS 105.

290.title: Seminar in Animal Behavior
290.description: Selected topics in animal behavior.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Lectures and/or discussion of current issues, problems, or techniques in animal behavior.

299.title: Research
299.description: Advanced research in one of the specialty areas in animal behavior

050A.title: Animal Biology Laboratory
050A.description: Scientific methods for answering questions in animal biology by doing exercises to demonstrate hypothesis testing and reporting, short laboratory, population and field experiments. Maintain notebooks, analyze data, interpret results and write reports.

092.title: Internship in Animal Biology
092.description: Office, laboratory or fieldwork off or on campus in research, governmental regulation, policy making, and private enterprise dealing with animal related issues of production, welfare, pest management, biodiversity and the environment. All requirements of Internship Approval Request form must be met.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

102.title: Animal Biochemistry & Metabolism
102.description: Water and biological buffers; thermodynamics of metabolism; structure and function of biomolecules; enzyme kinetics and function; membrane biology; digestion and absorption; carbohydrate metabolism.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 102.

189.title: Senior Practicum
189.description: Practicum may be an experimental research project, a library research project or some other creative activity that will serve as a capstone experience for the Animal Biology major.
189.prereq_text: ABI 050A; ABI 050B; ABI 050C; ABI 187; Junior standing.

192.title: Internship in Animal Biology
192.description: Office, laboratory or fieldwork off or on campus in research, governmental regulations, policy making, and private enterprise dealing with animal related issues of production, welfare, pest management, biodiversity and the environment. All requirements of Internship Approval Request form must be met.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

200A.title: Integrated Animal Biology I
200A.description: Natural history, management, historical and current uses, and specialized disciplinary features of model and novel animal systems used in research. Development of conceptual approaches in organismal biology to improve experimental design and interpretation of interdisciplinary research studies.
200A.prereq_text: BIS 101 or BIS 101V;  or consent of instructor, or equivalent course; graduate standing.

201.title: Mastering Your Masters
201.description: Guided and mentored development of scientific, professional skills and personal development for masters candidates in the Animal Biology Graduate Group.

202.title: Grant Procurement & Administration
202.description: Topics include: structure of grants, attention to specifications, concise persuasive writing, and grant budgeting. Identify grant opportunities, write a persuasive research grant proposal, and administer grants.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research with a faculty member in Animal Biology Graduate Group.

300.title: Methods in Teaching Animal Biology
300.description: Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching animal biology. Includes analysis of laboratory exercises, discussion of teaching techniques, grading scientific essays, preparing for and conducting discussion or laboratory sections, formulating quiz and exam questions under instructor supervision.

401.title: Ethics & Professionalism in Animal Biology
401.description: Case studies and discussion of ethical and professional issues for animal biologists, including the use of animals in research and teaching, patenting and intellectual property, consulting and conflict of interest, scientific integrity, dealing with the media, and mentoring relationships.

107.title: Genetics & Animal Breeding
107.description: Principles of quantitative genetics applied to improvement of livestock and poultry. Effects of mating systems and selection methods are emphasized with illustration from current breeding practices.

111.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory Techniques
111.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in molecular biology; the role of this technology in both basic and applied animal research, and participation in laboratories using some of the most common techniques in molecular biology.
111.prereq_text: BIS 002C; (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V or ABI 102); (BIS 103 or ABI 103).

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Selected topics relating to animal genetics.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Lectures and discussions of advanced topics in animal genetics.

001.title: Domestic Animals & People
001.description: Animal domestication and factors affecting their characteristics and distribution. Animal use for food, fiber, work, drugs, research and recreation; present and future roles in society. Laboratory exercises with beef and dairy cattle, poultry, sheep, swine, laboratory animals, fish, horses, meat and dairy products.

018.title: Introductory Aquaculture
018.description: Historical and contemporary aquacultural practices. Interaction between the aqueous culture environment and the biology of aquatic animals. Impact of economics and governmental policies on the development of aquaculture. Interaction of aquacultural practices with larger societal goals.

041.title: Domestic Animal Production
041.description: Principles of farm animal management, including dairy and beef cattle, sheep, and swine. Industry trends, care and management, nutrition, and reproduction.

041L.title: Domestic Animal Production Laboratory
041L.description: Animal production principles and practices, including five field trips to dairy cattle, beef cattle, sheep, and swine operations and campus labs.

049B.title: Animal Management Practices: Beef
049B.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049C.title: Animal Management Practices: Dairy
049C.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049D.title: Animal Management Practices: Goats
049D.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049E.title: Animal Management Practices: Horses
049E.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049G.title: Animal Management Practices: Meats
049G.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049H.title: Animal Management Practices: Poultry
049H.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049I.title: Animal Management Practices: Sheep
049I.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049J.title: Animal Management Practices: Swine
049J.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049K.title: Animal Management Practices: Captive & Companion Avian
049K.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

090C.title: Research Group Conference
090C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

092.title: Internship in Animal Science
092.description: Internship off and on campus in dairy, livestock, and aquaculture production, research and management; or in a business, industry, or agency associated with these or other animal enterprises. All requirements of Internship Approval form must be met.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

104.title: Principles & Applications of Domestic Animal Behavior
104.description: Basic principles of animal behavior as applied to domesticated species. Emphasis placed on application of the principles of animal behavior.

113.title: Meat Safety & Hazard Analysis & Critical Control Points
113.description: Fundamentals of meat safety and Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP). Principles, development, implementation of HACCP. Control of physical, chemical, biological hazards assuring meat/food safety via programs (Good Manufacturing Practices, Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures), hazard analysis critical control points. Regulations, focusing on HACCP implementation in meat & seafood products. Value, shortcomings of sampling, and microbial testing in meat safety assurance programs.

115.title: Advanced Horse Production
115.description: Feeding, breeding, and management of horses; application of the basic principles of animal science to problems of production of all types of horses. Designed for students who wish to become professionally involved in the horse industry.
115.prereq_text: ANS 015; (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); NUT 115; (ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V); or consent of instructor.

132.title: Microbiology of Animal Systems Laboratory
132.description: Basic microbiology techniques and the ability to produce recombinant proteins from genomic information. Importance of carbohydrate degrading enzymes in animal systems. Animal systems of interest range from the digestive tract of animals (e.g. rumen) to animal waste (e.g. manure).

134.title: Animal Nutrition Laboratory
134.description: Animal nutrition research experience for senior-level students. Forming a valid hypothesis, designing treatments, preparing for experiments, recording measurements in the field, summarizing results. Emphasis on developing essential research skills & proper techniques for collecting, summarizing, and presenting data.
134.prereq_text: ABI 103 (can be concurrent); (ANS 100 (can be concurrent) or NPB 101 (can be concurrent) or NPB 101V (can be concurrent)); (STA 100 or PLS 120).

135.title: Production Animal Laboratory
135.description: Biochemical methods for developing and conducting research with production animals, and interpreting and presenting data. Laboratory focus course which uses sheep as model. There may be one or two mandatory all day Saturday field trips.
135.prereq_text: ABI 102; ABI 103; (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or ANS 100).

136.title: Techniques & Practices of Fish Culture
136.description: Daily care and maintenance of fish in residential aquariums, research and commercial facilities. Biological and environmental factors important to sound management of fish. Laboratories focus on fish culture including growth trials and biochemical assays.
136.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed ANS 136A or ANS 137.
136.prereq_text: ANS 002; BIS 002A; BIS 002B; BIS 002C; ((CHE 008A,  CHE 008B) or (CHE 118A,  CHE 118B)).

142.title: Companion Animal Care & Management
142.description: Management and production of companion animals. Integration of the disciplinary principles of behavior, genetics, nutrition, and physiology as related to the care of companion animals.
142.prereq_text: ANS 042; (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or ANS 100); ((ABI 102 or BIS 102) and (ABI 103 or BIS 103)) recommended.

170.title: Ethics of Animal Use
170.description: Ethical issues relating to animal use in contemporary society. Integration of philosophical theories with scientific evidence relating to animal behavior, mentality, and welfare. Uses of animals in agriculture, research, and as companions. Ethical responsibilities regarding wildlife and the environment.
170.prereq_text: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or CMN 001 or CMN 001V or COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003 or COM 004 or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or NAS 005 or NAS 005V.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

192.title: Internship in Animal Science
192.description: Internship off and on campus in dairy, livestock and aquaculture production, research and management; or in a business, industry, or agency associated with these or other animal enterprises. All requirements of Internship Approval Form must be met.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194.title: Research in Animal Science
194.description: Research with a faculty mentor. Weekly discussion and laboratory on specific research topic. May include a seminar to research group. Choose from sections: (1) Animal Behavior; (2) Animal Genetics; (3) Animal Nutrition; (4) Animal Physiology.
194.prereq_text: ANS 106 or ANS 135 or ANS 136 or ANS 137 or ANS 139 or ANG 111; or ANS 133; and consent of instructor.

194HA.title: Undergraduate Honors Thesis in Animal Science
194HA.description: Carry out a research project (chosen from faculty-suggested or approved proposals) during the academic year under the guidance of a faculty member. Upon completion, write a thesis and present a public seminar describing his/her research.
194HA.prereq_text: (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or ANS 100); (ABI 103 or BIS 103); and consent of instructor; minimum cumulative GPA of 3.200 and selection by the Honors Selection Committee.

197T.title: Tutoring in Animal Science
197T.description: Tutoring of students in courses taught by instructors in the Department of Animal Science; weekly conference with instructor(s) in charge of the course; written critiques of teaching procedures; assist in preparation and development of instructional materials.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; animal Science or related major; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Selected topics relating to the animal sciences.

290C.title: Research Group Conference
290C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

297.title: Supervised Teaching in Animal Science
297.description: Practical experience in teaching Animal Science at University level; curriculum design and evaluation; preparation and presentation of material. Assistance in laboratories, discussion sections, and evaluation of student work. Evaluation letter sent to the graduate advisor with copy to the student.

298.title: Group Study
298.description:
Lectures and discussions of advanced topics in the animal sciences.

(Sect. 1, 2, 3-letter grading; from Sect. 4 on-S/U grading only.)

001.title: Human Evolutionary Biology
001.description: Evolutionary theory and mechanisms of evolution; basic population and quantitative genetics; primatology; biological and cultural diversity within Homo sapiens; paleoanthropology.

002.title: Cultural Anthropology
002.description: Introduction to cultural diversity in its many forms and methods used by anthropologists to account for it. Relational dynamic of culture, history, and power in constituting "social facts" and "realities." Critical thinking of contemporary concerns.

003.title: Introduction to Archaeology
003.description:
Development of archaeology as an anthropological study; objectives
and methods of modern archaeology.

015.title: From Birth to Death: The Evolution of the Human Life Cycle
015.description: Introduction to the biology of birth, childhood, marriage, the family, old age, and death. Examines comparative characteristics of nonhuman primates and other animals as well as cross-cultural variation in humans by study of selected cases.

025.title: Ancient Animals & People
025.description: History of human and animal relationships and how animals have influenced social and economic structures of past societies. Why, when and how humans used animals in the context of hunting, domestication, secondary products, ritual, companionship, and conservation.

032.title: Drugs, Science & Culture
032.description: Drugs, politics, science, society in a cultural perspective: emphasis on roles of science, government and the media in shifting attitudes toward alcohol, marijuana, Prozac and other pharmaceuticals; drug laws, war on drugs and global trade in sugar, opium, cocaine.

100.title: Theory in Social-Cultural Anthropology
100.description: Discussion of the theoretical and philosophical developments in cultural anthropology from the 19th century to the present.
100.prereq_text: ANT 002 recommended.

101.title: Ecology, Nature, & Society
101.description: Interdisciplinary study of diversity and change in human societies, using frameworks from anthropology, evolutionary ecology, history, archaeology, psychology, and other fields. Topics include population dynamics, subsistence transitions, family organization, disease, economics, warfare, politics, and resource conservation.
101.prereq_text: ANT 001 or ANT 002 or ESP 030 or EVE 100 or BIS 101 recommended.

109.title: Visualization in Science: A Critical Introduction
109.description: Anthropological approaches to scientific visualization techniques, informatics, simulations. Examination of different visualization techniques toward understanding the work involved in producing them, critical assessment of their power and limits, especially when visualizations are used socially to make claims.
109.prereq_text: ANT 002 or STS 001 or STS 020 recommended.

111.title: Science & Race
111.description: Race and racial formations in science, technology, and medicine. History of racial thought in scientific and medical research; colonial and decolonial modes of knowledge production; the racialization of technology; intersectional approaches to technoscience, social justice, environmental justice, and health care equity.

120.title: Language & Culture
120.description: Culture, cognition, meaning, and interpretation; language and the classification of experience; communication and learning in crosscultural perspective.
120.prereq_text: ANT 004 or LIN 001 recommended; ANT 002 recommended.

123AN.title: Resistance, Rebellion, & Popular Movements
123AN.description: Analysis of popular protest in Third World and indigenous societies ranging from covert resistance to national revolts. Comparative case studies and theories of peasant rebellions, millenarian movements, social bandits, Indian "wars", ethnic and regional conflicts, gender and class conflicts.
123AN.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 123B. (Former ANT 123B.)

133.title: Anthropology of Ocean Worlds
133.description: Exploration of various oceanic cultures and their engagement with the sea. Piracy, smuggling, exchange, maritime legal regimes, offshore policing, media infrastructures, and ocean ecologies.

137.title: Meditation & Culture
137.description: Study and practice of the relation between meditation and cultural conditioning; comparison of Buddhist practice with other cultural constructions of mind, body, brain, thought, emotion, and self.

141.title: Indigenous Peoples of the Arctic
141.description: Comparative history of Indigenous peoples across the circumpolar arctic. Arctic ecosystems, language, social structure, subsistence, gender, religion, art, health, colonialism, contemporary issues, climate change, and resilience.

147.title: Modern South Asia Cinema
147.description: South Asian cinema of last 100 years in the context of cultural, social, and political changes. South Asian history, Independence, Partition, urban life, class, migration, postcolonial identity, diaspora, gender, sexuality, religion, sport, performance, etc.
147.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

156A.title: Human Osteology
156A.description: Human skeleton from archaeological, forensic, and paleontological perspectives, including anatomical nomenclature, variation with sex and age, function, evolution, growth, and development of bones and teeth. Hands-on study and identification of human skeletal remains.

172.title: Ice-Age Settlement of the Americas
172.description: Critical evaluation of evidence related to human settlement of the Americas in the late Pleistocene/early Holocene (~40,000–8,000 years ago). Examines archaeological, genetic, biological, and paleoenvironmental data concerning early migrations.

187.title: Cultural Resource Management in Archaeology
187.description: Examination of legal foundations and goals of cultural resource management in the United States, with a focus on archaeological resources. Review of state and federal regulations, guidelines for assessing eligibility for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, professional practices to preserve and mitigate damage to resources, and public outreach practices.
187.prereq_text: ANT 003; or consent of instructor; ANT 170 recommended.

191.title: Topics in Anthropology
191.description: Intensive treatment of a special anthropological topic or problem.

192.title: Internship in Anthropology
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Anthropology under the supervision of a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description: Independent study of an anthropological problem involving the writing of an honors thesis.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open only to majors of senior standing who qualify for honors program.

197T.title: Tutoring in Anthropology
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Upper division standing with major in Anthropology and consent of Department Chairperson.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed reading and group discussion of selected anthropological problems.

201.title: Critical Readings in Ethnography
201.description: Critical readings of selected ethnographies that examine a wide range of important topics and analytical issues in social and cultural anthropology. Emphasis on how and why ethnographic writing has changed over time and its relationship with contemporary theoretical explorations.
201.prereq_text: Graduate student in Anthropology or consent of instructor.

202.title: History & Theory of Biological Anthropology
202.description: History of thought in biological anthropology and analysis of major theoretical problems in the field. Suggested for all first-year graduate students lacking intensive preparation in biological anthropology.

210.title: Aspects of Culture Structure
210.description: Analysis of various phases of culture, such as religion, economics, law, and folklore.

216.title: Problems in Archeological Method
216.description: Techniques for analyzing archeological data; application to various prehistoric cultures.

270.title: Anthropology Colloquium Seminar
270.description: Reports and discussions of recent advances in the four subfields of anthropology. Presented by guest speakers.

016.title: Metal Properties & Fabrication
016.description: Study of metal properties and of techniques for fabricating in metal. Physical principles, design considerations, effects of techniques on quality and appearance, and evaluation procedures. Experience in working with metal.

049.title: Field Equipment Operation
049.description: Operation, adjustment, and troubleshooting of farm tractors and field equipment. Principles of operation, equipment terminology and uses of tilling, cultivating, thinning, and planting equipment. Typical sequences in cropping practices.

060.title: Introduction to Unmanned Aerial Systems for Agriculture & Environmental Science
060.description: Operation, use and impact of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) for applications in agriculture and environmental assessment.  Principles of unmanned flight, vehicle systems, safety, and airspace regulations for communicating spatial relationships. UAS sensors, data acquisition, management, processing, visualization and analysis. Ethics and professional responsibilities in operations and public communication, and potential impacts for agricultural and environmental policy.

150.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
150.description: Basic concepts, principles, and methods of GIS are presented. Data structures, database design, GIS data creation, GPS, and spatial analysis. May be taught abroad.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ABT 180/PLS 180, ABT 181N; LDA 150, LED 150, ABT 150.

190C.title: Research Conference for Advanced Undergraduates
190C.description: Research conferences for specialized study in applied biological systems technology.

197T.title: Tutoring in Applied Biological Systems Technology
197T.description: Tutoring individual students, leading small voluntary discussion groups, or assisting the instructor in laboratories affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference
290C.description: Research problems, progress, and techniques in applied biological systems technology.

001.title: Elementary Arabic 1
001.description: Introduction to basic Arabic. Interactive and integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, including the alphabet and basic syntax. Focus on standard Arabic with basic skills in spoken Egyptian and/or one other colloquial dialect.

021.title: Intermediate Arabic 21
021.description: Builds on courses ARB 001, ARB 002, and ARB 003. Interactive and integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, including idiomatic expression. Focus on standard Arabic with limited use of Egyptian and/or one other colloquial dialect.

121.title: Advanced Arabic
121.description: Review, refinement, and development of skills learned in intermediate Arabic through work with texts, video, and audio on cultural and social issues. Integrated approach to reading, writing, listening, speaking primarily standard Arabic, with limited use of one colloquial dialect.

001A.title: Ancient Mediterranean Art
001A.description: Introduction to the art and architecture of the ancient Mediterranean world, including Mesopotamia, Egypt, Greece, and Rome.

100.title: Methods of Art History
100.description: Methods of art historical research and analysis, and general issues in critical thought. Writing skills appropriate to a range of art-historical exposition.
100.prereq_text: Prior completion of two upper-division Art History (AHI) courses recommended.

102.title: Exhibition Practicum
102.description: Curate an exhibition. Development of exhibition proposal, object selection and installation, design, lighting, creation of exhibition text and promotional material. Production of a public display for a campus museum or elsewhere.

123.title: The Museum in the Age of Spectacle
123.description: The institution of the museum in the context of modernity, nationalism, (post) colonialism, and the society of spectacle. Designed to bring art objects of the Manetti Shrem collection, global art history, and foundational critical theory together in a meaningful and experimental way.

157.title: Buddhist Art
157.description: A historical survey of Buddhist art in relation to the development of Buddhist doctrine and philosophy.

172A.title: Early Greek Art & Architecture
172A.description: Examination of the origin and development of the major monuments of Greek art and architecture from the 8th century to the mid-5th century B.C.

175.title: Architecture & Urbanism in Mediterranean Antiquity
175.description: Architecture and urban development in the ancient Near East, Greece, and Rome. Special emphasis on the social structure of the ancient city as expressed in its architecture, and on the interaction between local traditions and the impact of Greco-Roman urbanism.

176A.title: Art of the Middle Ages: Early Christian & Byzantine Art
176A.description: Term paper or gallery studies and review. Painting, sculpture and architecture of the early Christian era and Byzantine Empire: through the later Roman Empire in the West and to the final capture of Constantinople in the East.

190A.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Art History: Mediterranean Antiquity
190A.description: Study of a broad problem or theoretical issue in art, architecture, or material culture. Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing.
190A.prereq_text: Upper division standing; significant training in Art History recommended; or consent of instructor.

190H.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Art History: Modern-Contemporary
190H.description: Study of a broad problem or theoretical issue in art, architecture, or material culture. Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing.
190H.prereq_text: Upper division standing; significant training in Art History recommended; or consent of instructor.

200A.title: Visual Theory & Interpretive Methods
200A.description: Close study of selected recent developments in interpretive methodology used by art historians and other analysts of visual culture and the place of those developments within art history's history and in the larger field of social, cultural and historical analysis.

290.title: Special topics in Art History
290.description: Special research seminar in the theory or methods of Art History, or in a period of Art History. Topic varies depending on the interests of the instructor or students.

001.title: Introduction to Studio Art Practice
001.description: Introduction to studio art practice. Overview and practice of artists’ creative process including hands-on visual exercises, reading, writing, presentation, and critique.

002.title: Beginning Drawing
002.description: Introduction to drawing using various black and white media to articulate forms and organize space, with reference to historical and contemporary works. May be taught abroad.

005.title: Beginning Sculpture
005.description: Basic sculpture techniques using a variety of media. Form in space using cardboard, plaster, and/or cement, wood and/or metal and other media.

007.title: Beginning Painting
007.description: Introduction to techniques and concepts in the practice of painting.

008.title: Beginning Ceramic Sculpture
008.description: Introduction to ceramic sculpture construction and processes. Large scale hand-building, glazing, kilns and kiln firing technology.

009.title: Beginning Photography
009.description: Introduction to visual language of photographic art and technique. Manual camera operation and printing techniques. Concept and practice of photography as an art form and creating photographic projects.

012.title: Beginning Video
012.description: Production techniques of video shooting, editing, lighting, sound and effects.  A conceptual framework for video-art techniques.

101A.title: Intermediate Painting
101A.description: Individualized projects exploring color and space in a variety of subject matter and approaches. Builds on basic skills and concepts from beginning drawing and painting courses. Study of historical and contemporary art in relation to studio practice.

101B.title: Intermediate Painting: Figure
101B.description: Study of the human figure through the medium of painting with emphasis on development of skill and conceptual awareness.

103AN.title: Intermediate Drawing
103AN.description: Study of drawing composition using charcoal and ink.

103C.title: Intermediate Drawing: 3 Dimensions
103C.description: Study of drawing composition using three dimensional media.

110A.title: Intermediate Photography: Black & White Analog
110A.description: Introduction to analog black-and-white film photography. Technical instruction in 35mm film camera operation, developing film, making prints in the dark-room. Critical exploration of great works of photography and peer critique. Development of photographic project.

113.title: Interdisciplinary Art
113.description: Experimental interdisciplinary strategies. Use of various media in creation of collaborative or independent works. Production of participatory audio-visual works, installations, or two dimensional explorations.
113.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Art Studio, Theater and Dance, Design, Technocultural Studies, or Music.

125B.title: Intermediate Printmaking: Intaglio
125B.description: Intaglio printmaking techniques including copper-plate drypoint, engraving, etching, aquatint. Development of on soft-ground, spit bite and chine-collé. Development of conceptual and technical progress.

151.title: Intermediate Sculpture
151.description: Individualized explorations through multiple projects in a variety of sculpture media and techniques. Builds upon technical skills and concepts covered in ART 005.

152C.title: Advanced Sculpture: Concepts
152C.description: Investigation of a specific idea chosen by the class. Relationship of idea to form and content. Individual development of conceptual awareness.

190.title: Seminar in Art Practice
190.description: Introduction to professional practices. Development of an artist's packet including a resume, cover letter, artist statement, and statement of purpose. Ongoing independent studio work with group critiques. Research on galleries and museums, and readings in contemporary theory and criticism.
190.prereq_text: Upper division standing Art Studio major; completion of two upper division ART classes.

221A.title: Critical Exploration & Collaboration
221A.description: During the first year of study, MFA graduate students take the Critical Exploration & Collaboration seminar. Explore and analyze a range of subjects in contemporary art and begin to define their relationship to these ideas through speaking, writing, research and presentation in ways that are relevant to their own art practice.

221B.title: Advanced Critical Exploration & Collaboration
221B.description: Advanced course for second-year graduate students. Explore and analyze a range of subjects in contemporary art and begin to define their relationship to these ideas through speaking, writing, research and presentation in ways that are relevant to their own art practice.

290A.title: Critical Discourse in Contemporary Art
290A.description: Critical discourse in contemporary art and application to practice. Exploration of concerns in broader artistic and contemporary context. How artists look to shift prevalent expectations through critical analysis.

290D.title: Critical Discourse in Context
290D.description: Advanced course for second-year Graduate students. Discussion of social, political, cultural, and economic issues in a constantly changing world. How contemporary art practice are affected by global issues.

001.title: Historical Experience of Asian Americans
001.description: Introduction to Asian American Studies through an overview of the history of Asians in America from the 1840s to the present within the context of the development of the United States.

002.title: Contemporary Issues of  Asian Americans
002.description: Introduction to Asian American Studies through the critical analysis of the impact of race, racism, ethnicity, imperialism, militarism, and immigration since post-World War II on Asian Americans.  Topics may include sexuality, criminality, class, hate crimes, and inter-ethnic relations.

113.title: Asian American Sexuality
113.description: Restrictive U.S. immigration laws, labor exploitation, race-based exclusionary laws, removal and internment, anti-miscegenation laws, and other examples of social control are surveyed to assess their role in shaping the sexuality of the different Asian American groups.

121.title: Asian American Performance
121.description: Performance work by, for, and/or about Asian Pacific Americans including dramatic literature, performance art, dance, and film. Ethnicity, gender and sexuality, class and age as they intersect with Asian Pacific American identities in and through dramatic performance.

189B.title: Topics in Asian American Studies: Culture
189B.description: Intensive treatment of a topic in Asian American Studies; culture.

189C.title: Topics in Asian American Studies: Physical & Mental Health
189C.description: Intensive treatment of a topic in Asian American Studies; physical and mental health.

010G.title: Introduction to Stars, Galaxies, & the Universe
010G.description: Non-mathematical introduction to astrophysics of the Universe beyond our solar system using concepts of modern physics.
010G.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002, the former AST 010, any quarter of PHY 009 or PHY 009H, or any upper division physics course (other than PHY 137 or PHY 160).

010L.title: Observational Astronomy Lab
010L.description: Introduction to observations of the night sky using small telescopes in nighttime laboratory.
010L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002 or AST 010.

005.title: Global Climate Change
005.description: Scientific concepts needed to understand climate and climate change. Principles of regional variations in climate. Understanding observed seasonal, decadal and millennial changes. Analysis of the Antarctic ozone hole, El Nino and human-induced global warming.

060.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Science
060.description: Fundamental principles of the physics, chemistry, and fluid dynamics underlying weather and climate. Solar radiation, the greenhouse effect, and the thermal budget of the Earth. Clouds and their formation, convection, precipitation, mid-latitude storm systems.

092.title: Atmospheric Science Internship
092.description: Internship off and on campus in atmospheric science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

116.title: Modern Climate Change
116.description: Factors that determine the Earth’s climate, including natural and human-caused changes. Impacts of climate change. Possible future climates and policies to reduce human emissions of greenhouse gases.

120.title: Atmospheric Thermodynamics & Cloud Physics
120.description: Atmospheric composition and structure, thermodynamics of atmospheric gases, thermal properties of dry and moist air, atmospheric stability; cloud nucleation, cloud growth by condensation and collision, cloud models.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; three upper division units in Atmospheric Science.

245.title: Climate Change Science & Impacts
245.description: Overview of climate change science with a focus on climate change communication. Impacts of climate change on water, agriculture, energy, health, infrastructure, ecosystem services, tribal and indigenous communities. Climate justice, political, societal, and economic dimensions of these issues.

270A.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Meteorological Statistics
270A.description: Applications and concepts in meteorological statistics.

270B.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Computer Modeling of the Atmosphere
270B.description: Applications and concepts in computer modeling of the atmosphere.

270C.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Design of Experiments & Field Studies in Meteorology
270C.description: Applications and concepts in design of experiments and field studies in meteorology.

270E.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Aerosol & Cloud Physics
270E.description: Applications and concepts in aerosol and cloud physics.

270F.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Atmospheric Chemistry
270F.description: Applications and concepts in atmospheric chemistry.

270G.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: General Meteorology
270G.description: Applications and concepts in general meteorology.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current developments in selected areas of atmospheric research. Topics will vary according to student and faculty interests.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Atmospheric Science or related field.

291A.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Air Quality Meteorology
291A.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Air Quality Meteorology.

291C.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Boundary Layer Meteorology
291C.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Boundary Layer Meteorology.

291D.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Climate Change
291D.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Climate Change.

013.title: Birds, Humans & the Environment
013.description: Interrelationships of the worlds of birds and humans. Lectures, discussions, field trips and projects focus on ecology, avian evolution, physiology, reproduction, flight, behavior, folklore, identification, ecotoxicology and conservation. Current environmental issues are emphasized. Half-day field trip.

092.title: Internship in the Avian Sciences
092.description: Internship on and off campus in poultry, game birds or exotic bird production, management and research; or in a business, industry, or agency concerned with these entities. Compliance with Internship Approval form essential.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Sophomore standing preferred.

160.title: Designing & Performing Experiments in Avian Sciences
160.description: Experiments in current problems in avian biology. Introduction to experimental design. Students choose a project, design a protocol, perform an experiment and report their findings.
160.prereq_text: AVS 100 or WFC 111; or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Avian Sciences
192.description: Internship on and off campus in poultry, game birds or exotic bird production, management and research; or in a business, industry, or agency concerned with these entities. Compliance with Internship Approval form essential.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

195.title: Topics in Current Research
195.description: Discussion of topics of current interest in avian sciences.

197T.title: Tutoring in Avian Sciences
197T.description: Tutoring of students in lower division avian sciences courses; weekly conference with instructors in charge of courses; written critiques of teaching procedures.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description:
Major professors lead research discussions with their graduate students. Research papers are reviewed and project proposals
presented and evaluated. Format will combine seminar and discussion.

297T.title: Supervised Teaching in Avian Sciences
297T.description: Tutoring of students in lower, upper division, and graduate courses in Avian Sciences; weekly conference with instructor in charge of course; written critiques of teaching methods in lectures and laboratories.

BCB.name: Bio, Molec, Cell, Dev Bio GG

210.title: Molecular Genetics & Genomics
210.description: Emphasizes molecular genetic and genomic approaches to address fundamental biological questions. Introduces and emphasizes the strengths of prokaryotic and eukaryotic model systems and serves as building block for the BMCDB core courses, which use model systems to develop their themes.
210.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); MCB 121; or equivalent courses.

211.title: Macromolecular Structure & Interactions
211.description: Conceptual and quantitative basis for macromolecular structure-function relationships. Investigation of the paradigm form follows function. Review of key elements of protein, nucleic acid, and membrane structure. Exploration of specific macromolecular associations by analyzing chemical structure and physical-chemical behavior.
211.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or the equivalent, or consent of instructor.

220L.title: Advanced Biochemistry Laboratory Rotations
220L.description: Two five-week assignments in BMCDB research laboratories. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience, experimental design, proposal writing and oral communication of results.
220L.prereq_text: BCB 210; BCB 211 (can be concurrent); BCB 120L or the equivalent.

257.title: Cell Proliferation & Cancer Genes
257.description: Genetic and molecular alterations underlying the conversion of normal cells to cancers, emphasizing regulatory mechanisms and pathways. Critical reading of the current literature and development of experimental approaches.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate-student research.
290.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and/or graduate standing.

092.title: Internship in Biological Chemistry
092.description: Supervised work experience in biological chemistry and related fields
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Biological Chemistry
192.description: Supervised work experience in Biological Chemistry and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to internship by preceptor.

198.title: Group Study
198.description: For undergraduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth. Lecture and conferences may be involved.

230.title: Practical NMR Spectroscopy & Imaging
230.description: Basic theory, experimental methods, and instrumentation of NMR. Enables understanding of NMR spectroscopy and imaging experiments.
230.prereq_text: CHE 107A; CHE 107B; (PHY 009A,  PHY 009B,  PHY 009C; or PHY 005A, PHY 005B, PHY 005C) or consent of instructor.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: For graduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth. Lectures and conferences may be involved.

002A.title: Introduction to Biology: Essentials of Life on Earth
002A.description: Essentials of life including sources and use of energy, information storage, responsiveness to natural selection and cellularity. Origin of life and influence of living things on the chemistry of the Earth. May be taught abroad.
002A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001A with a grade of C- or better.
002A.prereq_text: CHE 002A or CHE 004A or equivalent recommended.

002B.title: Introduction to Biology: Principles of Ecology & Evolution
002B.description: Introduction to basic principles of ecology and evolutionary biology, focusing on the fundamental mechanisms that generate and maintain biological diversity across scales ranging from molecules and genes to global processes and patterns.
002B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001B with a grade of C- or better.

002C.title: Introduction to Biology: Biodiversity & the Tree of Life
002C.description: Introduction to organismal diversity, using the phylogenetic tree of life as an organizing theme. Lectures and laboratories cover methods of phylogenetic reconstruction, current knowledge of the tree of life, and the evolution of life's most important and interesting innovations.
002C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001C with a grade of C- or better.
002C.prereq_text: BIS 001B C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better.

005.title: Exploring Biological Sciences
005.description: Introduction to biology at UC Davis through discussions with faculty and speakers from industry and medicine.

092.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
092.description: Internship in Biological Sciences.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Primarily for lower division students. May be taught abroad.

101.title: Genes & Gene Expression
101.description: Nucleic acid structure and function; gene expression and its regulation; replication; transcription and translation; transmission genetics; molecular evolution.
101.prereq_text: (BIS 002A C- or better or BIO 002 C- or better); (BIS 002B C- or better or BIO 001 C- or better); (CHE 008A or CHE 118A or CHE 128A); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100 or STA 102 or STA 130A); STA 100 preferred.

102.title: Structure & Function of Biomolecules
102.description: Structure and function of macromolecules with emphasis on proteins, catalysis, enzyme kinetics, lipids, membranes, and proteins as machines. May be taught abroad.
102.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit for students who have completed ABI 102; only 1.5 units of credit for students who have completed BIS 105.
102.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B).

103.title: Bioenergetics & Metabolism
103.description: Fundamentals of the carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles in nature, including key reactions of biomolecules such as carbohydrates, amino acids, lipids, and nucleotides, and of energy production and use in different types of organisms. Principles of metabolic regulation.
103.credit_limit_text: 1.5 units of credit for students who have completed BIS 105; 1 unit of credit if students who have completed ABI 103.

104.title: Cell Biology
104.description: Membrane receptors and signal transduction; cell trafficking; cell cycle; cell growth and division; extracellular matrix and cell-cell junctions; cell development; immune system.
104.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 105 or ABI 102 C- or better).

181.title: Comparative Genomics
181.description: Comparison of genomes at the population and species level. Genomic techniques for mapping disease (and other) genes, reconstruction of evolutionary history and migration patterns, determination of gene function, prediction of organismal traits, and metagenomics: determination of community composition and function.
181.prereq_text: BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better; or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
192.description: Internship in Biological Sciences.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194H.title: Research Honors
194H.description: Students majoring in Biological Sciences who have completed two quarters (3-5 units per quarter) of 199 and who qualify for the honors program as defined by the current catalog. Opportunity for Biological Sciences majors to pursue intensive research culminating in the writing of a senior thesis with the guidance of faculty advisors.

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Sciences
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Biological Sciences' regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study in Biological Sciences
199.description: Special study in Biological Sciences. May be taught abroad.
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: College of Biological Sciences staff members offer group study courses under this number.

001.title: Foundations of Biological Systems Engineering
001.description: Introduction to engineering and the engineering design process with examples drawn from the field of biological systems engineering. Introduction to computer-aided design and mechanical fabrication of designs. Quarter-long group design project.

090C.title: Research Group Conference in Biological Systems Engineering
090C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing in Biological Systems Engineering or Food Engineering.

092.title: Internship in Biological Systems Engineering
092.description: Supervised work experience in biological systems engineering.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing; project approval prior to period of internship.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Group study of selected topics; restricted to lower division students.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

127.title: Mass Transfer & Kinetics in Biological Systems
127.description: Fundamentals of mass transfer and kinetics in biological systems. Molecular diffusion and convection. Thermodynamics and bioenergetics. Biological and chemical rate equations. Heterogeneous kinetics.  Batch and continuous reaction processes. Mass transfer operations.

144.title: Groundwater Hydrology
144.description: Global role of groundwater resources in society; groundwater in the hydrologic cycle; geology of groundwater; global, US, and California geography of groundwater; physical measures of groundwater occurrence and flow; water balance; modeling groundwater flow; principles of well construction; aquifer tests; groundwater quality; contaminant transport and monitoring; groundwater law, water quality regulations, and sustainable management.
144.prereq_text: MAT 012 (can be concurrent) or MAT 021A (can be concurrent) or MAT 019A (can be concurrent) or MAT 016B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

165.title: Bioinstrumentation & Control
165.description: Instrumentation and control for biological production systems. Measurement system concepts, instrumentation and transducers for sensing physical and biological parameters, data acquisition and control.

170A.title: Engineering Design & Professional Responsibilities
170A.description: Engineering design including professional responsibilities. Emphasis on project selection, data sources, specifications, human factors, biological materials, safety systems, and professionalism. Detailed design proposals developed for EBS 170B and EBS 170BL.

189A.title: Special Topics in Biological Systems Engineering: Agricultural Engineering
189A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Engineering.

instructors.full_name: Juliana Leite Nobrega De Moura Bell
instructors.display_name: J. Leite Nobrega De Moura Bell

190C.title: Research Group Conference in Biological Systems Engineering
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Biological Systems Engineering of Food Engineering.

192.title: Internship in Biological Systems Engineering
192.description: Supervised work experience in biological systems engineering.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Systems Engineering
197T.description: Tutoring individual students, leading small voluntary discussion groups, or assisting the instructor in laboratories affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

200.title: Research Methods in Biological Systems Engineering
200.description: Planning, execution and reporting of research projects. Literature review techniques and proposal preparation. Record keeping and patents. Uncertainty analysis in experiments and computations. Graphic analysis. Oral and written presentation of research results, manuscript preparation, submission and review.

241.title: Precision Irrigation Systems & Management
241.description: Advanced irrigation science and engineering for agricultural, horticultural, engineering, and hydrology graduate students. Precision irrigation techniques for application of water to meet specific requirements of individual plants or management units and maximum economic benefits of crop production.

242.title: Hydrology & Sustainability of Irrigated Lands
242.description: Impact of irrigated agricultural on groundwater depletion, surface water and groundwater quality, soil salinization, downstream ecosystems, and seawater intrusion. Exploration of efficient resource use, and policies adopted in California to enhance sustainability of irrigated crop production.
242.prereq_text: ABT 110 or ESM 110 or HYD 110 or EBS 145.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Weekly seminars on recent advances and selected topics in biological systems engineering. Theme changes from quarter to quarter.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference
290C.description: Research problems, progress and techniques in biological systems engineering.

390.title: Supervised Teaching in Biological & Agricultural Engineering
