390.description: Tutoring and teaching students in undergraduate courses offered in the Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering. Weekly conferences with instructor; evaluation of teaching. Preparing for and conducting demonstrations, laboratories and discussions. Preparing and grading exams.

001.title: Introductory Biology: Ecology & Evolution
001.description: Fundamentals of ecology, evolution, and heredity. Processes that generate and maintain biological diversity, spanning genes to ecosystems. May be taught abroad.
001.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken BIS 002B.

001L.title: Introductory Biology Lab: Ecology & Evolution
001L.description: Inquiry-based, hands-on field and lab experience in ecology, evolution, and heredity. Processes that generate and maintain biological diversity, spanning genes to ecosystems.
001L.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken BIS 002B.

002.title: Introductory Biology: Molecules to Cells
002.description: Molecular basis of life, illustrating mechanistic underpinnings and evolution. Fundamentals of molecular biology, cellular biology, and metabolism. May be taught abroad.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken BIS 002A.
002.prereq_text: BIO 001 C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better.

002L.title: Introductory Biology Lab: Molecules to Cells
002L.description: Inquiry-based, hands-on laboratory experience in molecular and cellular biology. Interactions and responses of cells to a changing environment.
002L.prereq_text: (BIO 001L C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better); BIO 002 (can be concurrent).

003.title: Introductory Biology: Cells Through Organisms
003.description: How multicellular organisms solve life’s problems. Basics of cell communication, cell organization into tissues and organs, and examples of how organisms across the tree of life address challenges such as sensing and responding to the abiotic and biotic environment, acquiring resources, maintaining homeostasis, preventing disease, and reproducing
003.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have taken BIS 002D.
003.prereq_text: (BIO 001 C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better); (BIO 002 C- or better or BIS 002A C- or better).

150.title: Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experience in Biology
150.description: Course-based undergraduate research experience. Hands-on participation in inquiry-based, discovery research on questions of broad relevance and significance in the biological sciences. Experimental design, modern techniques, and data analysis, with critical synthesis and presentation of findings.

001.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
001.description: Introduction to the field of biomedical engineering with emphasis on design, careers, and specializations, including (1) medical devices (2) cellular & tissue engineering, (3) biomechanics, (4) systems & synthetic biology, and (5) biomedical imaging.

105.title: Probability & Data Science for Biomedical Engineers
105.description: Concepts of probability, random variables, stochastic processes, mathematical modeling, and data analysis, with applications to biomedical engineering. Includes combinatorics, discrete, continuous, and jointly distributed random variables, probability distributions and models, Markov Chains, and Poisson Processes. Computer labs using MATLAB cover mathematical and computational modeling techniques, hands-on data analysis, and computer simulations.
105.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have taken MAT 107 or BIS 107; only 2 units of credit for students who have completed MAT 135A or STA 131A.
105.prereq_text: (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or BIS 027A C- or better); ENG 006 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

110A.title: Biomedical Engineering Senior Design Experience
110A.description: Application of bioengineering theory and experimental analysis to a design project culminating in the design of a unique solution to a biomedical problem. Continues in BIM 110B.
110A.prereq_text: BIM 105; BIM 106; BIM 107; BIM 108; BIM 109; BIM 020L; (BIM 116 or BIM 181 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V).

111.title: Biomedical Instrumentation Laboratory
111.description: Basic biomedical signals and sensors. Topics include analog and digital records using electronic, hydrodynamic, and optical sensors, and measurements made at cellular, tissue and whole organism level.
111.prereq_text: BIM 105; BIM 106; BIM 107; BIM 108; BIM 109; (ENG 100 or EEC 100); (BIM 116 or BIM 181 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V).

116.title: Quantitative Physiology
116.description: Human physiology from a quantitative and engineering perspective; quantitative models to understand human physiology of the pulmonary and cardiovascular systems with an emphasis on organ transport (convection and diffusion) and biomechanics.
116.prereq_text: BIS 002A C- or better; BIM 020 C- or better; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B); PHY 009C recommended.

162.title: Introduction to the Biophysics of Molecules & Cells
162.description: Introduction to fundamental physical mechanisms governing structure and function of bio-macromolecules. Emphasis on a quantitative understanding of the nano- to microscale biomechanics of interactions between and within individual molecules, as well as of their assemblies, in particular membranes.
162.prereq_text: PHY 009C C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better or BIS 027B C- or better).

170.title: Aspects of Medical Device Design & Manufacturing
170.description: Survey of medical device design & impact on manufacturing operations. Introduction to medical device design process & product lifecycle. Principles of Design for Manufacturability, Design for Lean Manufacturing, and quality management systems.

meetings.building_name: Aggie Sq Life Long Learn Bldg

174.title: Microcontroller Applications Lab
174.description: Hands-on design module to introduce microcontroller platforms, e.g., Arduino; programming microcontroller development board, use of external programs to support development of controlled systems, design of simple control systems.
174.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have previously taken EEC 010.
174.prereq_text: ENG 017 C- or better or ENG 017V C- or better..

201.title: Scientific Communication for Biomedical Engineers
201.description: Designed to improve the written and oral communication skills of first-year graduate students through writing fellowship proposals, analyzing data, and critically reviewing research papers.

202.title: Cell & Molecular Biology for Engineers
202.description: Preparation for research and critical review in the field of cell and molecular biology for biomedical or applied science engineers Emphasis on biophysical and engineering concepts intrinsic to specific topics including receptor-ligand dynamics in cell signaling and function, cell motility, DNA replication and RNA processing, cellular energetics and protein sorting. Modern topics in bioinformatics and proteomics.

204.title: Physiology for Bioengineers
204.description: Basic human physiology of the nervous, muscular, cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal systems and their interactions; Emphasis on the physical and engineering principles governing these systems, including control and transport processes, fluid dynamics, and electrochemistry.
204.prereq_text: BIS 001A; or equivalent; graduate standing or consent of instructor.

242.title: Introduction to Biomedical Imaging
242.description: Basic physics and engineering principles of image science. Emphasis on ionizing and nonionizing radiation production and interactions with the body and detectors.  Major imaging systems: radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, ultrasound, and optical microscopy.
242.prereq_text: PHY 009D; EEC 106 or consent of instructor.

260.title: Techniques in Molecular & Cellular Mechanics
260.description: Physical techniques used to visualize and manipulate mechanical processes in cells. Biophysical techniques used to characterize cellular and molecular mechanics, with a particular emphasis on single molecule technologies.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar in biomedical engineering

295.title: Literature in Neuroengineering
295.description: Critical presentation and discussion of current literature in neuroengineering.

201.title: Current Topics in Biophotonics & Bioimaging Research
201.description: Designed to help graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in the field of Biophotonics and Bioimaging research and related areas.

200LA.title: Biophysics Laboratory
200LA.description: One five-week laboratory assignment in the research laboratory of a Biophysics Graduate Group faculty member. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

200LB.title: Biophysics Laboratory
200LB.description: Two five-week laboratory assignments in the research laboratories of Biophysics Graduate Group faculty members. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

290.title: Biophysics Seminar
290.description: Presentation of current research by experts in biophysics.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

293.title: Introduction to Research Topics
293.description: Presentation of current research activities of the Biophysics Graduate Group faculty. Facilitation of students in developing their research interest, and promoting collegial interactions.

222.title: Biostatistics: Survival Analysis
222.description: Incomplete data; life tables; nonparametric methods; parametric methods; accelerated failure time models; proportional hazards models; partial likelihood; advanced topics.

298.title: Directed Group Study
298.description: Special topics in Biostatistics appropriate for group study at the graduate level.

299.title: Special Study for Biostat Graduate Students
299.description: Special topics in Biostatistics appropriate for directed individual study on advanced topics not otherwise covered in the Biostatistics curriculum.

299D.title: Dissertation Research
299D.description: Research in Biostatistics under the supervision of major professor.
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advancement to Candidacy for Ph.D.

092.title: Internship in Biotechnology
092.description:
Work experience on or off campus in subject area pertaining to biotechnology or in a business, industry or agency associated with
biotechnology. Internship supervised by faculty member in the animal or plant sciences.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

150.title: Applied Bioinformatics
150.description:
Concepts and programs needed to apply bioinformatics in biotechnology research. Sequence analysis and annotation and use of plant and animal databases for students in biological and agricultural sciences. 

BIS 101V added to prereqs effective 202501. 9/11/24 DV
150.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed ECS 124.
150.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 032B or ECS 010 or ECS 015 or PLS 021 or PLS 021V); (PLS 120 or STA 013 or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y or STA 100); or consent of Instructor.

160.title: Principles of Plant Biotechnology
160.description: Principles and concepts of plant biotechnology including recombinant DNA technology, molecular biology, genomics, cell and tissue culture, gene transfer and crop improvement strategies using transgenic crops.
160.prereq_text: (BIS 002A C- or better or BIO 002 C- or better); (BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better or PLS 152 C- or better); or consent of instructor.

171.title: Professionalism & Ethics in Genomics & Biotechnology
171.description: Real and hypothetical case studies to illustrate ethical issues in genomics and biotechnology. Training and practice in difficult ethical situations and evaluating personal and social consequences.
171.prereq_text: Upper division standing in a natural science major.

189L.title: Laboratory Research in Genomics & Biotechnology
189L.description: Formulating experimental approaches to current questions in biotechnology; performance of proposed experiments.

192.title: Internship in Biotechnology
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in a subject area pertaining to biotechnology or in a business, industry or agency associated with biotechnology. Internship supervised by faculty member in the animal or plant sciences.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

194H.title: Honors Thesis in Biotechnology
194H.description: Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior thesis.
194H.prereq_text: BIT 188; BIT 189L; consent of instructor; senior standing in Biotechnology with 3.250 GPA or higher.

401.title: Information, Insight & Impact
401.description: Introduction to the process of analyzing raw data to gain profitable business insight. Applications selected across organizational functions include prediction, process improvement, and general operational decision-making.

421.title: Data Management
421.description: Introduction to the extraction, assembly, storage and organization of data in IT systems.

441.title: Statistical Exploration & Reasoning
441.description: Introduction to statistical reasoning and inference extraction from large data-sets. Learn to obtain preliminary insights and form initial hypotheses through exploratory data analysis (EDA).

462.title: Practicum Elaboration
462.description: Building on problems chosen in BAX 461, teams refine the business opportunity and draw insights from exploratory data analysis.

192.title: Internship in Cardiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in cardiology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

199.title: Cardiology Research
199.description: Special study by individual arrangement in cardiovascular medicine. Work will include directed readings, laboratory and discussions.

192.title: Internship in Morphology
192.description: Experience of supervised internship in research laboratories of members of the department.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; laboratory science experience including some chemistry; approval of project by preceptor prior to period of internship.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed reading, discussion, and/or laboratory experience on selected topics.

001Y.title: Design of Coffee–An Introduction to Chemical Engineering
001Y.description: Non-mathematical introduction to how chemical engineers think, illustrated by elucidation of the process of roasting and brewing coffee. Qualitative overview of the basic principles of engineering analysis and design. Corresponding experiments testing design choices on the sensory qualities of coffee.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 001, ECM 001, ECM 005 or ECH 005.

002Y.title: World Coffee Cultures
002Y.description: Coffee cultural traditions and practices from around the world. Historical perspectives and analysis of future trends. Corresponding experiments testing distinct cultural influences on the sensory qualities and nutritional aspects of coffee beverages.

051.title: Material Balances
051.description: Application of the principle of conservation of mass to single and multicomponent systems in chemical process calculations. Studies of batch, semi-batch, and continuous processes involving mass transfer, phase change, and reaction stoichiometry.
051.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 151.

080.title: Chemical Engineering Profession
080.description: Professional opportunities and professional responsibilities of chemical engineers. Opportunities and needs for post-baccalaureate education.  Relationship of chemical engineering to contemporary issues.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.

140.title: Mathematical Methods in Biochemical & Chemical Engineering
140.description: Mathematical and computational methods for solving problems in chemical/biochemical engineering, with an emphasis on transport phenomena. Tensor analysis. Solutions of nonlinear equations. Filtering data and images. Numerical differentiation and integration. Ordinary and partial differential equations. Finite difference methods. Fourier series and separation of variables. Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue problems. Similarity transformations. Bessel functions.
140.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 159.
140.prereq_text: (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); (ECH 060 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV; or equivalents of ECH 060 or ECS 032A).

141.title: Fluid Mechanics for Biochemical & Chemical Engineers
141.description: Principles and applications of fluid mechanics in chemical and biochemical engineering. Hydrostatics. Stress tensor and Newton's law of viscosity.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 150B.
141.prereq_text: ECH 051 (can be concurrent); ECH 140 (can be concurrent).

148A.title: Chemical Kinetics & Reaction Engineering
148A.description: Ideal chemical reactors. Rate laws and stoichiometry. Design and analysis of isothermal reactors with multiple reactions.
148A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECH 146. (Formerly ECH 146.)

157.title: Process Dynamics & Control
157.description: Fundamentals of dynamics and modeling of chemical processes. Design and analysis of feedback control of chemical processes.

158AN.title: Separations & Unit Operations
158AN.description: Senior design experience with multiple realistic constraints. Heuristic and rigorous design of chemical process equipment. Separation by filtration, distillation and extraction. Synthesis of reactor and separation networks, heat and power integration.
158AN.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken ECH 158B.

161AN.title: Bioseparations
161AN.description: Product recovery and purification of biochemicals.  Cell disruption, centrifugation, filtration, membrane separations, extraction, and chromatographic separation.
161AN.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken ECH 161B.

192.title: Internship in Chemical or Biochemical Engineering
192.description: Supervised work experience in Chemical or Biochemical Engineering.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of a minimum of 84 units; project approval before period of internship.

200.title: Preparing for Graduate Student Success
200.description: Introduction to the soft-skills and campus resources needed to succeed in graduate school.  Emphasis on the student-mentor relationship and the process of selecting a research mentor.

252.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
252.description: A treatment of the statistical basis of thermodynamics; introduction to statistical mechanics; discussion of the laws of thermodynamics; application of thermodynamic relationships to phase and chemical reaction equilibrium; introduction to molecular simulations and the evaluation of thermodynamic properties from molecular simulations.

253A.title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics
253A.description: Kinematics and basic principles of fluid flow.  Principles of constitutive equations.  Navier-Stokes equations for Newtonian fluids.  Survey of rectilinear creeping flow, lubrication flow and boundary layer theory.

289E.title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering: Biotechnology

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

294.title: Current Progress in Biotechnology
294.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research activities.

001.title: Preparation for General Chemistry
001.description: Preparation for the general chemistry series (CHE 002ABC & CHE 004ABC); unit conversion, dimensional analysis, periodic table, chemical equations, stoichiometry, and gases.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 002A or CHE 004A with a grade of C- or better.

002A.title: General Chemistry
002A.description: Periodic table, stoichiometry, chemical equations, physical properties and kinetic theory of gases, chemical equilibrium, acids and bases. Laboratory experiments in stoichiometric relations, properties and collection of gases, atomic spectroscopy, introductory quantitative analysis and acids and bases.
002A.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 004A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002AH or CHE 004B.
002A.prereq_text: High school chemistry and physics, and concurrent enrollment in mathematics at or above the level of MAT 012 strongly recommended; must earn a qualifying score of 24 or higher on the Chemistry Placement Exam or complete CHE 001 or CHE 001V with a C- or higher; more information about the Chemistry Placement Requirements can be found at https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/undergraduate/general-chemistry-series/chemistry-placement-requirements/0000.

002C.title: General Chemistry
002C.description: Continuation of CHE 002B. Kinetics, electrochemistry, spectroscopy, structure and bonding in transition metal compounds, application of principles to chemical reactions. Laboratory experiments in selected analytical methods and syntheses.
002C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CHE 002CH.
002C.prereq_text: CHE 002B C- or better or CHE 002BH C- or better or CHE 004B C- or better.

004A.title: General Chemistry for the Physical Sciences & Engineering
004A.description: General chemistry course with a more rigorous treatment of material covered in CHE 002A, intended for students majoring in the physical sciences and engineering.
004A.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 002A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002AH or 002B.
004A.prereq_text: MAT 021A (can be concurrent); must earn a qualifying score of 28 or higher on the Chemistry Placement Exam or complete CHE 001 or CHE 001V with a C- or higher; high school chemistry and physics strongly recommended; more information about the Chemistry Placement Requirements can be found at https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/undergraduate/general-chemistry-series/chemistry-placement-requirements/0000.

004C.title: General Chemistry for the Physical Sciences & Engineering
004C.description: General chemistry course with a more rigorous treatment of material covered in CHE 002C, intended for students majoring in the physical sciences and engineering.
004C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002C or 002CH.
004C.prereq_text: (CHE 004B C- or better or CHE 002B B or better or CHE 002BH B or better); or consent of instructor.

008A.title: Organic Chemistry: Brief Course
008A.description: With CHE 008B, an introduction to the nomenclature, structure, chemistry, and reaction mechanisms of organic compounds. Intended for students majoring in areas other than organic chemistry.
008A.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed CHE 118A or 128A.
008A.prereq_text: CHE 002B C- or better or CHE 002BH C- or better or CHE 004B C- or better.

008B.title: Organic Chemistry: Brief Course
008B.description: Laboratory concerned primarily with organic laboratory techniques and the chemistry of the common classes of organic compounds. Lecture portion a continuation of CHE 008A.
008B.credit_limit_text: Varying credit hours according to courses taken previously and corresponding expected workload for this course; full credit to students who complete CHE 118A or 128A; 3 units credit to students who have completed CHE 128A and CHE 129A (students who have completed CHE 129A are exempt from the laboratory portion of CHE 008B); 2 units credit to students who have completed CHE 128B; 1 unit credit to students who have completed CHE 118B or CHE 128B and CHE 129A (students who have completed CHE 118B are exempt from the laboratory portion of CHE 008B).

010.title: Concept of Chemistry
010.description: Survey of basic concepts and contemporary applications of chemistry. Designed for non-science majors and not as preparation for CHE  002A.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have had CHE 002A; but students with credit for CHE 010 may take CHE 002A for full credit.

105.title: Analytical & Physical Chemical Methods
105.description: Fundamental theory and laboratory techniques in; analytical and physical chemistry, errors and data analysis methods, basic electrical circuits in instruments, advanced solution equilibria, potentiometric analysis, chromatographic separations, UV-visible spectroscopy, lasers.
105.prereq_text: CHE 110A (can be concurrent) or CHE 107B (can be concurrent).

107A.title: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
107A.description: Physical chemistry intended for majors in the life science area. Introductory development of classical and statistical thermodynamics including equilibrium processes and solutions of both non-electrolytes and electrolytes. The thermodynamic basis of electrochemistry and membrane potentials.
107A.prereq_text: (CHE 002C or CHE 002CH or CHE 004C); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 021C); (PHY 007C or PHY 009C or PHY 009HC).

110A.title: Physical Chemistry: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
110A.description: Introduction to the postulates and general principles of quantum mechanics. Approximations based on variational method and time independent perturbation theory. Application to harmonic oscillator, rigid rotor, one-electron and many-electron atoms, and homo-and hetero-nuclear diatomic molecules.
110A.prereq_text: (PHY 007C or PHY 009C or PHY 009HC); (CHE 002C or CHE 002CH or CHE 004C); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 021C); completion of MAT 021D, MAT 022A, MAT 022AL; PHY 009C or PHY 009HC, strongly recommended.

110B.title: Physical Chemistry: Properties of Atoms & Molecules
110B.description: Group theory. Application of quantum mechanics to polyatomic molecules and molecular spectroscopy. Intermolecular forces and the gas, liquid and solid states. Distributions, ensembles and partition functions. Transport properties.

115.title: Instrumental Analysis
115.description: Intermediate theory and laboratory techniques in analytical and physical chemistry. Advanced data analysis methods and goodness-of-fit criteria.  Fourier-transform spectroscopic methods and instrumentation. Mass spectrometry. Electrochemistry. Liquid chromatography.

118A.title: Organic Chemistry for Health & Life Sciences
118A.description: The 118A-C series is for students planning professional school studies in health and life sciences. Rigorous, in-depth presentation of basic principles with emphasis on stereochemistry and spectroscopy and preparations and reactions of nonaromatic hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, alcohols and ethers.
118A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit for students who have completed CHE 008A; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 008B or CHE 128A.
118A.prereq_text: CHE 002C C- or better or CHE 002CH C- or better or CHE 004C C- or better.

118C.title: Organic Chemistry for Health & Life Sciences
118C.description: Continuation of CHE 118B, with emphasis on the preparation, reactions and identification of carboxylic acids and their derivatives, alkyl and acyl amines, ß-dicarbonyl compounds, and various classes of naturally occurring, biologically important compounds.
118C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 128C.

124A.title: Inorganic Chemistry: Fundamentals
124A.description: Symmetry, molecular geometry and structure, molecular orbital theory of bonding (polyatomic molecules and transition metals), solid state chemistry, energetics and spectroscopy of inorganic compounds.

128A.title: Organic Chemistry
128A.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of organic chemistry with emphasis on stereochemistry and the chemistry of hydrocarbons. Designed primarily for majors in chemistry. Chemistry majors should enroll in CHE 129A concurrently.
128A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit allowed for students who have completed CHE 008A; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 008B or 118A.
128A.prereq_text: CHE 002C C or better or CHE 002CH C or better or CHE 004C C- or better.

128C.title: Organic Chemistry
128C.description: Continuation of CHE 128B with emphasis on enolate condensations and the chemistry of amines, phenols, and sugars; selected biologically important compounds.
128C.credit_limit_text: Full credit to students who completed CHE 118B; Not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 118C.

129A.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
129A.description: Introduction to laboratory techniques of organic chemistry. Emphasis on methods used for separation and purification of organic compounds.
129A.credit_limit_text: Full credit to students who completed CHE 008B; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 118B.
129A.prereq_text: (CHE 002C C or better or CHE 002CH C or better or CHE 004C C- or better); CHE 128A (can be concurrent).

130A.title: Principles of Medicinal Chemistry
130A.description: Examination of the design principles and experimental methods used in pharmaceutical and medicinal chemistry.

131.title: Modern Methods of Organic Synthesis
131.description: Introduction to modern synthetic methodology in organic chemistry with emphasis on retrosynthetic analysis, reaction mechanisms, and application to multistep syntheses of pharmaceuticals and natural products.

135.title: Drug Development Laboratory
135.description: Separation, purification, identification and biological evaluation of organic compounds using modern methods of synthesis, computational chemistry and instrumentation. Emphasis on pharmaceutical and medicinal substances.

192.title: Internship in Chemistry
192.description: Supervised internship in chemistry; requires a final written report.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; project approval by faculty sponsor prior to enrollment.

194HA.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HA.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HA.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

194HB.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HB.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HB.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

194HC.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HC.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HC.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

197.title: Projects in Chemical Education
197.description: Participation may include development of laboratory experiments, lecture demonstrations, autotutorial modules or assistance with laboratory sessions.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor based upon adequate preparation in chemistry, mathematics and physics.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor based upon adequate preparation in chemistry, mathematics, and physics.

201.title: Chemical Uses of Symmetry & Group Theory
201.description: Symmetry elements and operations, point groups, representations of groups. Applications to molecular orbital theory, ligand field theory, molecular vibrations, and angular momentum. Crystallographic symmetry.
201.prereq_text: CHE 124A; CHE 110B; or consent of instructor.

204.title: Mathematical Methods in Chemistry
204.description: Introduction to mathematical and numerical methods in chemistry. Real and complex functions.  Methods of integration. Differential equations. Linear algebra and matrices. Special functions. Integral transforms. Statistics.

211A.title: Advanced Physical Chemistry: Statistical Thermodynamics
211A.description: Principles and applications of statistical mechanics; ensemble theory; statistical thermodynamics of gases, solids, liquids, electrolyte solutions and polymers; chemical equilibrium.

221F.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry
221F.description: Selected topics of current interest in organic chemistry. Topics will vary each time the course is offered, and in general will emphasize the research interests of the staff member giving the course.

226.title: Principles of Transition Metal Chemistry
226.description: Electronic structures, bonding, and reactivity of transition metal compounds.

228C.title: Solid-State Chemistry
228C.description: Design and synthesis, structure and bonding of solid-state compounds; physical properties and characterization of solids; topics of current interest such as low-dimensional materials, inorganic polymers, materials for catalysis. Offered every third year.

233.title: Physical-Organic Chemistry
233.description: Introduction to elementary concepts in physicalorganic chemistry including the application of simple numerical techniques in characterizing and modeling organic reactions.
233.prereq_text: CHE 128A; CHE 128B; CHE 128C; CHE 110A; CHE 110B; CHE 110C; or equivalent.

238.title: Introduction to Chemical Biology
238.description: Synthesis of complex molecules in nature. Use of biosynthetic pathways in synthesis of new chemical entities. Applications of small molecules in chemical genetics and structural biology. Solving biological problems using synthetic biomolecules.
238.prereq_text: CHE 118C or CHE 128C; or equivalent; CHE 130A, CHE 130B and BIS 102, BIS 103, and BIS 104, or the equivalents recommended.

240.title: Advanced Analytical Chemistry
240.description: Numerical treatment of experimental data; thermodynamics of electrolyte and non-electrolyte solutions; complex equilibria in aqueous and non-aqueous solutions; potentiometry and specific ion electrodes; mass transfer in liquid solutions; fundamentals of separation science, including column, gas and liquid chromatography.

261.title: Current Topics in Chemical Research
261.description: Designed to help chemistry graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in their immediate field of research and related areas.
261.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Chemistry or consent of instructor.

262.title: Introduction to Chemistry Research
262.description: Group and individual discussion of research activities in the Department and research topic selection. Designed for incoming graduate students preparing for higher degrees in chemistry.

263.title: Introduction to Chemical Research Methodology
263.description:
Introduction to identification, formulation, and solution of meaningful
scientific problems including experimental design and/or theoretical analyses of new and prevailing techniques, theories and hypotheses. May be repeated for credit when topic differs.
263.prereq_text: CHE 293; and consent of instructor; graduate student standing in Chemistry.

264.title: Advanced Chemical Research Methodology
264.description: Applications of the methodology developed in CHE 263 to experimental and theoretical studies. Advanced methods of interpretation of results are developed. Includes the preparation of manuscripts for publication.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

296.title: Research in Pharmaceutical Chemistry
296.description: Laboratory provides qualified graduate students with the opportunity to pursue original investigation in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and allied fields in order to fulfill the letter-graded research requirement of the Integrated B.S./M.S. Program in Chemistry (Pharmaceutical Chemistry Emphasis).
296.prereq_text: CHE 130A; CHE 130B; CHE 135; CHE 233 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

299.title: Research
299.description: The laboratory is open to qualified graduate students who wish to pursue original investigation. Students wishing to enroll should communicate with the department well in advance of the quarter in which the work is to be undertaken.

390.title: Methods of Teaching Chemistry
390.description: Practical experience in methods and problems of teaching chemistry. Includes analyses of texts and supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques, preparing for and conducting of discussion sessions and student laboratories. Participation in the teaching program required for Ph.D. in chemistry.
390.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate student standing in Chemistry.

010.title: Introduction to Chicana/o Studies
010.description: Analysis of the situation of the Chicana/o (Mexican-American) people, emphasizing their history, literature, political movements, education and related areas.

023.title: Qualitative Research Methods
023.description: Dominant models of qualitative inquiry in educational and social science research as well as mestizo approaches to research with latinos. Emphasis given to choosing and designing culturally appropriate strategies to investigate latino health, education, social context, and policy issues.

040.title: Comparative Health: Top Leading Causes of Death
040.description: Introduction to the epidemiology of the leading causes of death for ethnic/racial minorities. Assessment of disproportionate rates at which ethnic/racial minorities suffer and die from chronic and infectious diseases and injuries and statistical methods used to calculate these rates.
040.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHI 040S.
040.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y; or consent of instructor.

050.title: Chicana & Chicano Culture
050.description: Interdisciplinary survey of Chicana/o cultural representation in the 20th century. Examines Chicana/o culture within a national and transnational context. Explores how Chicano cultural forms and practices intersect with social/material forces, intellectual formations and cultural discourses. (Former CHI 020.)

060.title: Chicana & Chicano Representation in Cinema
060.description: Introductory-level study of Chicana and Chicano representation in cinema. Depiction of Chicana and Chicano experience by Chicana/o filmmakers, as well as by non-Chicanos, including independent filmmakers and the commercial industry.

070.title: Survey of Chicana/o Art
070.description: Survey of contemporary Chicana/o art in context of the social turmoil from which it springs. Includes political use of the poster and the mural, the influence of the Mexican mural and graphic movement, and social responsibility of the artist.

073.title: Chicana/o Art Expression Through Silk Screen
073.description: Introductory level studio course using silk screen and basic printing techniques to explore and develop images of Chicana/o cultural themes and expressions. Students experiment with images and symbols from their immediate environment/culture. Integrated approach to Chicana/o philosophy of art.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Academic guidance combined with internship in community agencies serving Mexican/Latina/Latino/Chicana/Chicano clients. Students will use their bilingual skills and knowledge of history, culture, economics, politics and social issues.
092.prereq_text: CHI 010 or CHI 010V; or consent of instructor.

110V.title: Sociology of the Chicana/o Experience
110V.description: Chicana/o experience in the American society and economy viewed from theoretical perspectives. Immigration, history of integration of Chicana/o labor into American class structure, education inequality, ethnicity, the family and Chicana/o politics. (Former course SOC 110)
110V.prereq_text: CHI 010 or CHI 010V or SOC 001 or SOC 001V.

121.title: Chicana/o Community Mental Health
121.description: Mental health needs, problems, and service utilization patterns of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os will be analyzed. Analysis of social service policy, and the economic context of mental health programs.

130.title: United States-Mexican Border Relations
130.description:
Theories of U.S.-Mexican border relations, with an overview of the political, economic, and social relationships and an in-depth
analysis of immigration issues, border industrialization, women's organizations, economic crises, and legal issues.

132.title: Political Economy of Chicana/o Communities
132.description: Historical and contemporary study of political and economic forces which define and influence the development of Chicana/o communities. Includes critiques of traditional and Marxian theories and concepts applicable to Chicana/o communities, case studies of Chicana/o communities, especially in California and Texas.
132.prereq_text: Upper division standing; lower division Chicana/o Studies (CHI) course recommended.

155.title: Chicana/o Theater
155.description: Examination of the formal and thematic dimensions of Chicana/o theater in the contemporary period with special emphasis on El Teatro Campesino and Chicana Feminist Theater. Bilingual readings, lectures, discussions, and writing in Spanish. (Former course SPA 126B.)
155.prereq_text: Intermediate Spanish or consent of instructor.

165.title: Chicanas, Latinas & Mexicanas in Commercial Media
165.description: The portrayal of Chicanas, Latinas and Mexicanas in commercial media. The relation between the representation of Chicana, Latina, and Mexicana women in commercial television and cinema and the role of women in Mexican and U.S. societies.
165.prereq_text: CHI 060; or other film or feminist theory course; conversational fluency in Spanish.

181.title: Chicanas & Latinas in the U.S.: Historical Perspectives
181.description: Historical issues in the lives of Chicanas and Latinas in the U.S. and their diverse countries of origin.

182.title: Race & Juvenile Justice
182.description: Individual and institutional responses to "troublesome" youth of color through history and in contemporary society. Emphasis on how race, as well as ethnicity, class, and gender have informed the treatment of "delinquent" youth.

192.title: Internship in the Chicana/Chicano/Latina/Latino Community
192.description: Academic guidance combined with internship in community agencies serving Mexican/Latina/Latino/Chicana/Chicano clients. Use of bilingual skills and knowledge of history, culture, economics, politics and social issues. Internship project required.
192.prereq_text: (CHI 010 or CHI 010V or CHI 021 or CHI 050); (SPA 003 or SPA 003V or SPA 003Y); or equivalent of SPA 003.

194HA.title: Senior Honors Research Project
194HA.description: Student is required to read, research, and write Honors Thesis on Chicana/o Studies topics.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Chicana/o Studies major.

194HB.title: Senior Honors Research Project
194HB.description: Student is required to read, research, and write Honors Thesis on Chicana/o Studies topics.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Chicana/o Studies major.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of Program Chairperson.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of Program Chairperson.

001.title: Elementary Chinese
001.description: Developing elementary level skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing in Mandarin Chinese in everyday communication settings. Introduction of fundamentals of pronunciation, grammar, and Chinese characters will be introduced.
001.prereq_text: No background in Chinese or placement exam or consent of instructor.

001BL.title: Accelerated Chinese for Heritage Speakers  I
001BL.description: Training in all the communicative skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing for students who already have elementary level ability to understand or speak Mandarin Chinese. Emphases on standard Mandarin pronunciation, Chinese characters, and discourse level conversations.
001BL.prereq_text: Placement exam or consent of instructor.

002.title: Elementary Chinese
002.description: Continuation of elementary level skill development in listening, speaking, reading and writing Mandarin Chinese in everyday communication settings.  Continued introduction of basic vocabulary and characters as well as core grammar, and further train pronunciation.
002.prereq_text: CHN 001; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

004.title: Intermediate Chinese
004.description: Continuation of intermediate-level communication skills in spoken and written Mandarin, based on language skills developed in CHN 003.
004.prereq_text: CHN 003 or placement exam or consent of instructor.

009.title: Introduction to Chinese Language & Culture
009.description: Chinese culture through the lens of Chinese language. Relationship of language to religion, food, arts, ethnic groups, dialects, writing systems, etc. All readings are in English; no previous background is necessary. May be taught abroad.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

107.title: Traditional Chinese Fiction (in English)
107.description: Dawn of Chinese fiction and its development down to modern times. Survey of literary history with close reading of representative works. Readings, lectures, and discussions in English.

111.title: Modern Chinese: Reading & Discussion
111.description: Building on Chinese 006/003BL, further development of communication skills in Modern Standard Mandarin-speaking environments. Reading of dialogues/articles pertaining to contemporary China.
111.prereq_text: CHN 006 C- or better or CHN 003BL C- or better or CHN 004A C- or better; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

114.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
114.description: Introduction to the language in which, until the 20th century, most official, documentary, scholarly, and belle-lettristic Chinese literature was written.
114.prereq_text: CHN 112; or equivalent language proficiency. consent of instructor.

150.title: Fifth-Year Chinese: Selected Topics in Chinese Language, Literature, & Culture
150.description: Examination of literary works and scholarly essays on selected topics of Chinese culture and society. Development of a deep understanding of Chinese culture and society through sophisticated Chinese speaking and writing exercises.
150.prereq_text: CHN 120; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

192.title: Chinese Internship
192.description: Work experience in the Chinese language, with analytical term paper on a topic approved by instructor.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Chinese
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Department.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

001.title: Introduction to Film Studies
001.description: Analysis of film form and narrative, including cinematography, editing, and sound. Issues in film studies including authorship, stardom, race, gender, class, and cultural identity. Introduction to selected cinematic movements and national film traditions.

002.title: Introduction to Technocultural Studies
002.description: Contemporary developments in the fine and performing arts, media arts, digital arts, and literature as they relate to technological and scientific practices.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken TCS 001.

020.title: Filmmaking Foundations
020.description: Introduction to filmmaking concepts, principles, and methods. Emphasis on form, content and historical dialectic between classical narrative filmmaking conventions and artists' challenges to these conventions.
020.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CTS 020.

040A.title: Media History 1: Gutenberg to Oppenheimer
040A.description: History of media to 1945, with particular focus on mechanically reproduced mass media technologies including the printing press, the newspaper, photography, cinema, radio and early computing technology. Analysis of interrelated cultural and political topics.

041B.title: History of Cinema from 1945-Present
041B.description: Examines cinema from 1945 through the present, with focus on neo-realist, new wave and third-world movements. Examines social critique in cinema from studio system to New Wave, Cine Novo, postcolonial cinema and contemporary independent cinema.

100.title: Experimental Digital Cinema I
100.description: Experimental approaches to the making of film and video in the age of digital technologies. Builds upon the foundation provided by CDM 020. Instruction in technical, conceptual, creative, and critical skills for taking a project from idea to fruition.
100.prereq_text: CDM 020 or ART 012; or consent of instructor.

104.title: Documentary Production
104.description: Traditional and new forms of documentary, with focus on technocultural issues. Skills and strategies for producing work in various media. Progression through all stages of production, from conception through post-production to critique.
104.prereq_text: CDM 020; CDM 155; TCS 155; or consent of instructor.

107.title: Acting for Camera
107.description: Analysis and practice of acting skills required for camera work and digital media.

167.title: Topics in Film Genres
167.description: Study of one or more of the film genres (such as musicals, film noir, screwball comedy, or westerns), including genre theory and the relationship of the genre(s) to culture, history, and film industry practices. May be taught abroad.

174.title: Special Topics in Analog Game Design
174.description: Special topics in analog game design for upper division students.
174.prereq_text: CDM 072 or CDM 172 or CTS 172; or consent of instructor; Recommended: CDM 173, CDM 175 or CDM 177.

189.title: Special Topics in Cinema & Digital Media
189.description: Special topics in cinema & digital media.

146B.title: Modern South Asia Cinema
146B.description: South Asian cinema of last 100 years in the context of cultural, social, and political changes. South Asian history, Independence, Partition, urban life, class, migration, postcolonial identity, diaspora, gender, sexuality, religion, sport, performance, etc.
146B.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

003.title: Civil & Environmental Infrastructure & Society
003.description: Introduction to civil infrastructure and its relationship with society and the natural environment. Exposure to innovative research on civil engineering and environmental systems. Participation in laboratory experiments illustrative of the solution of representative but simplified engineering problems.

040.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
040.description: Introduction to topics in environmental engineering; discussion on influence of literary work, art, and media on the evolution of environmental engineering practice, relevant laws, and regulations; presentations of historical case studies. Major themes include sustainability, environmental justice, and laws/regulations.

100.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics for Civil & Environmental Engineers
100.description: Fluid flow in civil & environmental engineering, basis for design, buoyancy, hydrostatics, gravity dams, hydraulic modeling: similarity & scaling, conservation laws, flow in bends, nozzles, pipes, pumps, turbines, complimentary lab experiments.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ENG 103.
100.prereq_text: ENG 035 C-  or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better); PHY 009B C-  or better.

101.title: Transfer Transition for Civil & Environmental Engineering
101.description: Introduction to the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering for transfer and junior-level change-of-major students. Exploration of civil and environmental engineering disciplines and active areas of research in the department. Interaction with faculty in the department and campus student services that can support them while at UC Davis.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECI 003.

130.title: Structural Analysis
130.description: Elastic structural analysis of determinate and indeterminate trusses, beams and frames. Plastic bending and limit analysis.
130.prereq_text: (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A).

131.title: Matrix Structural Analysis
131.description: Matrix formulation and computer analysis of statically indeterminate structures. Stiffness and flexibility formulations for elastic structures. Finite element methods for elasticity and bending problems.
131.prereq_text: (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); ENG 006.

137.title: Construction Principles & Project Management
137.description: Project management, with civil engineering construction and design applications, including project scope, schedule, resources, cost, quality, risk, and control. Construction industry overview. Interactions between planning, design, construction, operations. Construction operations analysis. Contract issues. Project management software, field trips, guest lectures.

140A.title: Environmental Analysis of Aqueous Systems
140A.description: Introduction to "wet chemical" and instrumental techniques commonly used in the examination of water and wastewater and associated data analysis.
140A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECH 140 or CHE 100.

141.title: Engineering Hydraulics
141.description: Nature of flow of a real fluid; flow in pipes; open channel flow; turbomachinery; fluid forces on objects: boundary layers, lift and drag.
141.prereq_text: ENG 103 C- or better or ECI 100 C- or better.

141L.title: Engineering Hydraulics Laboratory
141L.description: Laboratory experiments and demonstrations on flow measurements, sluice gates, hydraulic jump, flow characteristics, and centrifugal pumps.

142.title: Engineering Hydrology
142.description: The hydrologic cycle. Evapotranspiration, interception, depression storage and infiltration. Streamflow analysis and modeling. Flood routing through channels and reservoirs. Frequency analysis of hydrologic variables. Precipitation analysis for hydrologic design. Hydrologic design.

153.title: Deterministic Optimization & Design
153.description: Operations research. Optimization techniques such as linear programming, dynamic programming, and non-linear programming. Applications in civil engineering disciplines, including multiple realistic constraints, through computer-based course projects.
153.prereq_text: MAT 021C; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A); computer programming course.

162.title: Transportation Infrastructure Design
162.description: Foundation in roadway design with a multimodal perspective. Transportation content related to sight distance, horizontal and vertical roadway design. Holistic perspective to design for multiple roadway users including bicycles, pedestrians, vehicle sharing, and public transit.
162.prereq_text: PHY 009A C- or better; MAT 021B C- or better.

163.title: Energy & Environmental Aspects of Transportation
163.description: Engineering, economic, and systems planning concepts. Analysis and evaluation of energy, air quality and selected environmental attributes of transportation technologies. Strategies for reducing pollution and petroleum consumption in light of institutional and political constraints. Evaluation of vehicle emission models.
163.prereq_text: Upper division standing in engineering or economics or environmental studies.

171.title: Soil Mechanics
171.description: Soil formations, mass-volume relationships, soil classification, effective stress, soil-water-void relationships, compaction, seepage, capillarity, compressibility, consolidation, strength, states of stress and failure, lateral earth pressures, and slope stability.
171.prereq_text: (ENG 103 (can be concurrent) or ECI 100 (can be concurrent)); (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); ECI 171L (can be concurrent); ECI 171L required concurrently.

171L.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
171L.description: Laboratory studies utilizing standard testing methods to determine physical, mechanical and hydraulic properties of soil and demonstration of basic principles of soil behavior.
171L.prereq_text: ECI 171 (can be concurrent); ECI 171 required concurrently.

175.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
175.description: Tectonics, faults, site response, and probabilistic ground motion prediction equations. Cyclic loading and liquefaction of soil elements and layers. Empirical procedures and field tests for evaluation of triggering and consequences, of liquefaction.

183.title: Heavy Civil Construction
183.description: Means and methods used to build civil infrastructure. Construction of bridges, tunnels, roads, railroads, dams, water and wastewater treatment facilities, utilities, foundations, and port facilities. Industry experts, collaborative group discussions, building exercises, construction site visits, and hands-on building projects.

191A.title: Advocating for Equity in Engineering
191A.description: Diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice in engineering academia and professional culture. Challenges specific to engineering and tools to empower students to take action.

191B.title: Construction Engineering & Project Management Seminar
191B.description: Aspects of project management and delivery such as estimating, scheduling, scoping, contract law, and construction of all types of civil and mechanical engineering infrastructure. Contractor, supplier, consultant, and owner point of view, including consideration of construction in design. Engagement with guest speakers featuring industry and government leaders followed by discussions.

201.title: Introduction to Theory of Elasticity
201.description: Fundamental equations of elasticity in three dimensions; plane stress and plane strain; flexture and torsion of bars of various shapes. Introduction to variational and approximate methods.

211A.title: Advanced Matrix Structural Analysis
211A.description: Matrix structural analysis for automated analysis of structures using computers. Application of matrix analysis techniques to complex problems in structural engineering arising from soil-structure interactions, three-dimensional effects, and nonlinear material response.
211A.prereq_text: ECI 130; or equivalent or consent of instructor.

213.title: Structural Dynamics
213.description: Analysis of structures subjected to dynamic loading; single and multi-degree of freedom systems; response spectrum analysis; numerical methods for analysis of linear systems.
213.prereq_text: ECI 138; Or equivalent or consent of instructor.

243A.title: Water & Waste Treatment
243A.description: Characteristics of water and airborne wastes; treatment processes and process kinetics; treatment system design.

247.title: Aerosols
247.description: Behavior of airborne particles including particle formation, modification, and removal processes.

256.title: Urban Traffic Management & Control
256.description: Basic concepts, models, and methods related to the branch of traffic science that deals with the movement of vehicles on a road network, including travel speed, travel time, congestion concepts, car-following and hydrodynamic traffic models.

264A.title: Transport, Mixing & Water Quality in River & Lakes
264A.description: Principal causes of mixing and transport in rivers, lakes and reservoirs, and their impacts on water quality. Case studies of specific lakes and rivers.

267.title: Water Resource Management
267.description: Engineering, institutional, economic, and social basis for managing local and regional water resources. Examples in the context of California's water development and management. Uses of computer modeling to improve water management.
267.prereq_text: ECI 114; ECI 142; or consent of instructor.

272N.title: Contaminant Fate & Transport in Porous Media
272N.description: Solute and colloid mass transport processes in porous media. Characterizing and quantifying physical processes of advection, diffusion/dispersion, sorption, as well as basic biogeochemical reactions. Colloid-facilitated transport in porous media. Analytical and numerical solutions to the reactive advection-dispersion equation in Eulerian and Lagrangian forms with an introduction to advanced random walk models.
272N.prereq_text: ECI 144; MAT 021A; MAT 021B; MAT 021C; MAT 022A; MAT 022B; Ability to program.

274.title: Introduction to Turbulence
274.description: Fundamental theory, statistics, analysis tools and models for turbulence and turbulent flows. Practical skills related to the analysis and study of turbulence.
274.prereq_text: MAT 022B; ECI 100; ECI 141; or consent of instructor.

276.title: Watershed Hydrology
276.description: Analysis and mathematical modeling of hydrologic processes taking place in a watershed. Precipitation analysis and modeling. Theory of overland flow and its kinematic wave approximation. Analysis and modeling of saturated and unsaturated subsurface flow processes taking place on a hill slope.

281A.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
281A.description: Consolidation and secondary compression. Preloading and wick drains.  Seepage and seepage pressures. Filtration, drainage, and dewatering. Shear strength: friction, cohesion, dilatancy and critical states.

281BN.title: Engineering Geology
281BN.description: Principles of geology in engineering design, construction, and natural hazards. Study of geologic setting, geologic processes, properties of geologic materials and influence on safety, constructability, economic feasibility, environmental impact, and performance.

289B.title: Selected Topics in Civil Engineering: Hydraulics & Hydrologic Engineering
289B.description: Directed group study in Hydraulics & Hydrologic Engineering.

292A.title: Geotechnical Professional Practice 1
292A.description: Geotechnical practice issues that affect the delivery of technical solutions for geotechnical projects, including business and management practices, contract documents, legal constraints, public policy and societal concerns, ethics, and professional development. Part 1 of three part series that includes a capstone project.

296.title: Topics in Water & Environmental Engineering
296.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty, researchers, postdocs, and graduate students.
296.prereq_text: Graduate standing; or consent of instructor.

001.title: Ancient Near East & Early Greece: 3000-500 B.C.E.
001.description: Introduction to the literature, art, and social and political institutions of ancient Mesopotamia, Egypt, Palestine, and early Greece from 3000 to 500 B.C.E.

010.title: Greek, Roman, & Near Eastern Mythology
010.description: Examination of major myths of Greece, Rome, and the Ancient Near East; their place in the religion, literature and art of the societies that produced them; their subsequent development, influence and interpretation.

015.title: Women & Gender in Classical Antiquity
015.description: Lives and roles of women and men in ancient Greece and Rome. Readings from history, philosophy, medical and legal documents, literature and myth.

020.title: Pompeii AD 79
020.description: Roman life in an urban community at the time of the eruption of Vesuvius. Slide presentations of the archeological evidence will be supplemented by selected readings from Petronius' Satyricon and other ancient authors.

030.title: Greek & Latin Elements in English Vocabulary
030.description: Knowledge of Latin and Greek not required. Elements of Greek and Latin vocabulary for increased understanding of English word formation and improved ability to understand and retain unfamiliar words. Emphasis on Greek and Latin elements but other languages not neglected.

035.title: Food & Wine in the Ancient Mediterranean
035.description: Social, political, and economic history of food and wine in ancient Mediterranean cultures. Development of agriculture and technology, trade, empires. Representation of food and wine in literary and visual arts, religious significance.
035.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CLA 036V.

050.title: Ancient Science
050.description: Study of science in ancient Greece and Rome; consideration of its social context; concentration on the basic concepts of physics, the world of medicine and biology, the history of mathematics, and the practices of astronomy, astrology and meteorology.

100A.title: Methods for Ancient Mediterranean Studies
100A.description: Survey of methods and major scholarly schools in study of Ancient Mediterranean. Modern history of academic disciplines, archaeological work, influence of museums and other large institutions.
100A.prereq_text: Lower division Classics course; or consent of instructor

143.title: Greek Tragedy
143.description: Reading in English of selected plays of Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides. Discussion of the development and influence of Athenian tragedy.
143.prereq_text: A lower division Classics (CLA) course or consent of instructor.

172A.title: Early Greek Art & Architecture
172A.description: Examination of the origin and development of the major monuments of Greek art and architecture from the 8th century to the mid-5th century B.C.

175.title: Architecture & Urbanism in Mediterranean Antiquity
175.description: Architecture and urban development in the ancient Near East, Greece, and Rome. Special emphasis on the social structure of the ancient city as expressed in its architecture, and on the interaction between local traditions and the impact of Greco-Roman urbanism.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis under the direction of faculty advisor.
194HA.prereq_text: Admission to the Honors Program; consent of faculty member supervising honors thesis.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in Classical Languages
197TC.description: Supervised instruction of Greek or Latin in nearby schools by qualified students in department.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

200A.title: Approaches to the Classical Past
200A.description: Survey of major areas of classical scholarship, with special emphasis on the continuing impact of Mediterranean antiquity on later literature, history, art, and culture.
200A.prereq_text: Graduate student status or consent of instructor.

200.title: Introduction to Translational Research
200.description: Introduction to the CRGG program and overview of major clinical research topics. Overview of basic clinical skills needed to accomplish CRGG mentored research project.
200.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; one of the following degrees: MD, DDS, DMD, OD, ND, DO, PharmD, DVM, PhD or DNS in nursing; application and acceptance into the Clinical Research Graduate Group, K30 program or other SOM/CTSC training programs.

202.title: Introduction to Clinical Research
202.description: Anatomy and physiology of conducting clinical epidemiologic research. Familiarity with three basic study designs: cross-sectional, case-control, and cohort. Discussion of principles of measurements in clinical epidemiological studies, basic methods for analyzing data, and ethical issues involved in conducting research.
202.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completed one of the following degrees: MD, DDS, DMD, OD, ND, DO, PharmD, DVM, PhD or DNS in nursing; application and acceptance into the Clinical Research Graduate Group, MRCTP program, Clinical Research Certificate or other SOM/CTSC training programs.

208.title: Introduction to Grant Writing, I
208.description: First in a two-quarter series. Scholars are encouraged to enroll in both classes. The two-course sequence provides training in practical aspects of competitive grant writing. The focus is NIH, but information will apply to other funding agencies.

211.title: Critical Assessment of the Biomedical Literature
211.description: Exposure to topical issues and controversies in the design of interdisciplinary translational research, with an emphasis on critical assessment of the biomedical and health sciences literature. Extends students’ knowledge of study design through practical application.

212.title: Introduction to Stem Cell Biology
212.description: Introduction to Stem Cell Biology. Each week will focus on different aspects of stem cells, including general concepts, stem cells in lower organisms, embryonic stem cells and cellular reprogramming.

222.title: Ethical Issues in Stem Cell Biology
222.description: Critical presentation and analysis of recent articles in stem cell biology and small group discussions of the ethical issues surrounding this area of research.

240.title: Predoctoral Clinical Research Training Program Research Integration
240.description: Alternating sessions:  journal club, seminar/discussion, and research integration sessions.
240.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment in the Predoctoral Clinical Research Training Program in the CTSC, School of Medicine.

244.title: Introduction to Medical Statistics
244.description: Introduction to statistical methods and software in clinical, laboratory, and population medicine. Graphical and tabular presentation of data; probability, binomial, Poisson, normal, t-, F-, and Chi-square distributions; one and two sample t-test; elementary nonparametric methods; simple linear regression; and correlation.
244.prereq_text: SPH 281; or ability to read a dataset such as a .csv file into SAS and to do data steps (label variables, format values, create new variables) and create summary measures (frequencies and means) in SAS.

290A.title: Hot Topics in Clinical Research
290A.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research activities
290A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

290B.title: Hot Topics in Stem Cell Biology
290B.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research

290C.title: Literature in Stem Cell Biology
290C.description: Critical presentation and analysis of recent journal articles in stem cell biology by students.

298.title: Group Study in Clinical Research
298.description: Special topics in Clinical Research appropriate for group study at the graduate level.

299.title: Clinical Research
299.description: Independent research and special topics in clinical research appropriate for graduate level.

001.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
001.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary cognitive scientific approach to the study of mind, drawing concepts and methods from psychology, philosophy, linguistics, artificial intelligence, and other disciplines.

134.title: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience
134.description: Explorations of how brain secretes mind, via computer simulations that are manipulated and probed to investigate how neurons produce perception, attention, memory, language, and cognitive control.
134.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 100 or PSC 101 or PSC 135 recommended.

001A.title: First Year Engagement: Student Success
001A.description: Introduction to university life. Transition to academic and campus life; academic expectations and the skills to meet them; campus resources; social and professional development; assistance in choice of major, and academic planning.

001.title: Introduction to Public Speaking
001.description: Practice in the preparation and delivery of speeches based on principles and strategies of informing and persuading audiences drawn from the social sciences and humanities.

003.title: Interpersonal Communication Competence
003.description: Communication competence in professional settings. Managing face-to-face and virtual teams. Leadership, conflict management and negotiation skills. Communication in diverse organizations. Leveraging communication networks. Effective interviewing.

010V.title: Introduction to Communication
010V.description: Basic principles of communication and communication processes; models of communication; foundations of empirical research in communication; contexts of communication and communication research, including interpersonal, intercultural, news, entertainment, mediated, and others.
010V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 010Y.

012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

101.title: Communication Theories
101.description: Forms, functions, development, and testing of communication theory, with emphasis on social scientific approaches. Survey and comparison of significant micro and macro theories and models of face-to-face and mediated communication. Application of theories to real-world problems.

102.title: Empirical Methods in Communication
102.description: Social scientific research methods employed in Communication. Topics include research design, measurement, sampling, questionnaire construction, survey research, experimental design, content analysis and qualitative field methods.
102.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y; or equivalent of STA 013.

111.title: Gender Differences in Communication
111.description: Examination of communication differences between men and women as sources of male/female stereotypes, misunderstandings, dilemmas, and difficulties (real and imagined). Treatment of genders as cultures. Topics include male/female differences in discursive practices and patterns, language attitudes, and relationship dynamics.
111.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 103.

112.title: Theories of Persuasion
112.description: Theories and models of persuasion that account for the effects of source, channel and audience factors on message recipients. Examination of message strategies for altering attitudes and gaining compliance. Contexts of application include interpersonal relationships, advertising, politics, and health.
112.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 152.

114.title: Communication & Cognition
114.description: Relationship between communication and cognition in interpersonal and mediated contexts. Discourse comprehension and production, impact of language attitudes on social judgments, the effects of information processing on decision making.
114.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMN 138.

120.title: Interpersonal Communication
120.description: Theories and principles of interpersonal communication related to perception, verbal and nonverbal channels, mutual understanding, and relationship development. Communication processes in face-to-face and technologically-mediated encounters. Consideration of different relationship contexts, including friendships, dating and family relationships, and the workplace.
120.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 134.

123.title: Intercultural Communication
123.description: Major concepts and theories of intercultural communication. Topics include cultural similarities and differences in verbal and nonverbal communication; dimensions of cultural variations, barriers to intercultural communication, and intercultural communication competence.
123.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 137.

124.title: Family Communication
124.description: Theories and research on family communication. Communication in courtship, marriage, and relational dissolution. Processes and outcomes of parent-child, sibling, family roles, and inter-generational communication. Interaction patterns associated with marital/family satisfaction, maintenance, divorce, and dysfunction. Cultural influences on family communication.

130.title: Group Communication
130.description: Communication processes in the development and maintenance of effective groups and teams in organizations. Examination of both face-to-face and computer-mediated group interaction. Topics include group development, power, norms, cohesion, decision making, problem solving, creativity, conflict management, working remotely, and leadership.

131.title: Strategic Communication in Public Relations
131.description: Principles, evolution, and professional practice of public relations. Planning and execution of effective, ethical communication strategies and campaigns. Distribution of messages through traditional and new media, including social media. Cultivation of relationships between organizations and their publics. Crisis communication management.

140.title: Introduction to Mass Communication
140.description: History of mass media and media research traditions. Organization and economics of the media industry. Media policy, law, regulation and ethics.  Impact of the media on individuals and society. Traditional, new and emerging communication technologies.

141.title: Media Effects: Theory & Research
141.description: Social scientific studies of the effects of mass media messages on audience members' actions, attitudes, beliefs, and emotions. Topics include the cognitive processing of media messages, television violence, political socialization, cultivation of beliefs, agenda-setting, and the impact of new technologies.

143.title: Analysis of Media Messages
143.description: Examination of alternative approaches to the analysis, interpretation, and evaluation of media messages, including those disseminated through broadcasting, print, and new technologies.

144.title: Media Entertainment
144.description: Effects and appeal of media entertainment, emphasizing emotional reactions. Topics include key concepts of entertainment research such as mood management, and the respective features and emotional/social-psychological effects of genres such as comedy, mystery, thriller, sports, music, horror, and erotica.

148.title: Contemporary Trends In Media
148.description: Global trends in media, including media and globalization, impacts of the new media economy, media and security, and effects of ownership on media content and culture.

150V.title: Computational Social Science
150V.description: Nontechnical survey of modern computational research methods. Web scraping, artificial intelligence, visualizing social networks, and computer simulations. Hands-on use of diverse software applications. Professors from all ten UC campuses contribute.

151.title: Social Systems & Social Complexity
151.description: Science and art of social modeling and the representation of complex communication phenomena. Models of social interaction from an interdisciplinary perspective to discover systems thinking and the science of social complexity. Focus on thinking in systems.

161.title: Health Communication
