161.description: Health communication theories and research. Health literacy, social support and coping, doctor-patient interaction, health communication campaigns, media influences on health, and applications of new technologies in health promotion.

165.title: Media & Health
165.description: Content and effects of health messages in the media. Topics include health news reporting; portrayals of disease, disability, death and health-related behaviors; promotion of drugs and other health products; and tobacco and alcohol advertising.

172.title: Interpersonal Technologies
172.description: Theories and research findings on how people use technologies for interpersonal and relational purposes, including impression formation, self-presentation, deception, anonymity, friendship maintenance, online dating, and emotional expression.

174.title: Social Media
174.description: Application of communication theories to the study and design of social media. Examination of social media in contexts such as political activism and collaboration. Topics include online credibility, participatory culture, viral media and privacy.

178.title: Persuasive Technologies
178.description: Designing and testing ethical, technology-based communication interventions in the domains of health, marketing, education, and environment. Social media, mobile apps, wearable devices, recommendation systems, serious games, and augmented reality.

194H.title: Senior Honors Thesis
194H.description: Directed reading, research, and writing culminating in the preparation of honors thesis under direction of faculty advisor.
194H.prereq_text: Senior standing and approval by Honors Committee.

197T.title: Tutoring in Communication
197T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate Communication courses, including leadership of discussion groups affiliated with departmental courses.
197T.prereq_text: Upper division standing with major in Communication and consent of Department Chairperson.

201.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Communication
201.description: Social scientific study of Communication. Research on interpersonal, organizational, mass, political, and health communication; communication technologies (e.g., video games, social media, persuasive technologies); and communication network analysis.
201.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing in Communication.

213.title: Simulation Methods in Communication Research
213.description: Simulation methods for modeling human communication. Single and multiple agent approaches to developing process theories of cooperation, coordination, strategic behavior, information and innovation diffusion, and other aspects of sociality.

214.title: Analysis of Communication Networks
214.description: Theoretical and analytic issues pertaining to network perspectives on communicating and organizing. Consideration of structural and dynamic features of communication networks. Introduction to network analysis software and various analysis techniques.

260.title: Political Communication
260.description: Theories and research on the connections between media, politics, and citizens in the digital age. Critical framework for understanding the nature of mediated politics by assessing inter-relationships between production of news, political elites’ campaign strategies, and behaviors of citizens.

283.title: Special Topics in Organizational Communication
283.description: Reading, discussion, research, and writing on a selected topic in the specialty of organizational communication.

001.title: The Community
001.description:
Basic concepts of community analysis and planned social change. The dynamics of community change through case studies of communities including peasant, urban ghetto, suburban mainline, and California
farm workers.

020.title: Food Systems
020.description: Social aspects of agri-food systems. Social science perspectives applied to food and agricultural sustainability in relation to ecology, knowledge, technology, power, governance, labor, social difference, and social movements. Social and environmental effects of commodity chains in comparative global context.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

142.title: Rural Change in the Industrialized World
142.description: Geography of rural environment with emphasis on rural restructuring. Demographics, community, economy, governance, agriculture, and environmental conservation in rural areas of industrialized world. Case studies from and comparisons drawn between North America, Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Japan.
142.prereq_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001V or CRD 001 or CRD 002 or ANT 002.

147.title: Community Youth Development
147.description: Community influences on youth well-being, youth as agents of community change, and policies to support healthy communities for young people. Special emphasis on disparities in youth well-being related to race, class, immigration status, gender, sexual-orientation.

157.title: Politics & Community Development
157.description: Analyzes political, economic and sociocultural forces shaping the form and function of local communities in the U.S. Considers theories of the state, the community and social change and case studies of actual community development in comparative historical perspective.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional
settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

197T.title: Tutoring in Community & Regional Development
197T.description: Assisting instructor in one of the Community & Regional Development's regular courses by tutoring individual students or small groups of students in a laboratory, in voluntary discussion groups, or other voluntary activities.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing; completion of course to be tutored.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

251.title: Critical Social Science of the Environment
251.description: Relationships between forces of society and the environment through careful examination of the interactions between politics, economics, and global dynamics. Schools of thought concerning society, gender, environmental dynamics, and political economic arrangements across local and global spheres.

260.title: Thesis Seminar
260.description: Workshop to help finalize thesis proposals and complete thesis.

290.title: Community Development Seminar
290.description: Speaker series on key topics in community development.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off campus, in community or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Group study. May be taught abroad.

001.title: Major Works of the Ancient World
001.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the ancient world (up to 5th century CE) such as The Odyssey, the Bible, Augustine's Confessions, and works by Plato and Confucius. Examined genres include religious texts, the epic, philosophy, drama, poetry.
001.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

002.title: Major Works of the Medieval & Early Modern World
002.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the medieval and early modern worlds (6th century to the mid-17th century) such as Dante’s Comedy, 1001 Nights, The Tale of Genji, and Elizabethan/Jacobean plays. Examined genres include framed narratives, courtly literature, and early modern drama.
002.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

003.title: Major Works of the Modern World
003.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the modern world (mid-17th to the mid-20th centuries) such as those by Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Flaubert, Woolf, Lu Xun, Borges and Yeats. Examined genres include realist fiction, modernist fiction, and modernist poetry.
003.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

004.title: Major Works of the Contemporary World
004.description: Comparative study of selected major Western and non-Western texts composed in the period from 1945 to the present. Intensive focus on writing about these texts, with frequent papers written about these works.
004.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005.title: Fairy Tales, Fables, & Parables
005.description: Introduction to fairy tales, fables, and parables as recurrent forms in literature, with such readings as tales from Aesop & Grimm, Chaucer & Shakespeare, Kafka & Borges, Buddhist & Taoist parables, the Arabian Nights, and African American folklore.

007.title: Literature of Fantasy & the Supernatural
007.description: Role of fantasy and the supernatural in literature: tales of magic, hallucination, ghosts, and metamorphosis, including diverse authors such as Shakespeare, P'u Sung-Ling, Kafka, Kawabata, Fuentes, and Morrison.

014.title: Introduction to Poetry
014.description: Comparative study of poetry in a variety of lyric and other poetic forms from different historical periods and different linguistic, national, and cultural traditions.
014.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

100.title: World Cinema
100.description: Comparative, cross-cultural study of a topic, theme, or movement in world cinema beyond the boundary of a single national tradition. Topics may include "postsocialist cinemas in East Europe and Asia," "cinema and globalization," and "popular Asian cinemas."
100.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), upper division standing, or consent of instructor.

141.title: Introduction to Critical Theoretical Approaches to Literature & Culture
141.description: Introduction to critical theory and its use for interpreting literary texts, film, and media forms in global culture.
141.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

153.title: The Forms of Asian Literature
153.description: Introduction to distinctive Asian literary forms, such as haiku, noh, the Chinese novel and tale, through reading of major works. Comparison with Western genres and study of native and Western critical traditions.
153.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

166.title: Literatures of the Modern Middle East
166.description: Major translated works in modern Middle Eastern and North African Literature, including Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Turkish. Social and historical formation, with topics such as conflict and coexistence, journeys, and displaced people, gender and family.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description:
Guided research, under the direction of a faculty member approved by the Program Director, leading to a senior honors thesis on a comparative
topic.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Open only to majors of senior standing who qualify for Honors Program.

198.title: Directed Group Study for Advanced Undergraduates

210.title: Topics & Themes in Comparative Literature
210.description: Comparative, interpretive study of the treatment of specific topics and themes in literary works from various periods, societies, and cultures, in light of these works' historical and sociocultural contexts.
210.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Comparative Literature, English, or a foreign-language literature, or consent of instructor.

250A.title: Research in Primary Literature
250A.description: Individually guided research in the primary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member culminating in a conference paper. Required of M.A. and Ph.D. candidates.

250B.title: Research in Second Literature
250B.description: Individually guided research in the secondary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member, culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

250C.title: Research in Third Literature or Special Topic
250C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, in the third literature of concentration or on a special topic culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

250D.title: Dissertation Prospectus
250D.description: Individually guided writing of the dissertation prospectus under supervision of a faculty member.  Must be taken prior to completion of the qualifying exam. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

299D.title: Special Study for the Doctoral Dissertation
299D.description: Special study for the doctoral dissertation.

390.title: Teaching Comparative Literature in College
390.description: Discussion of the theory and practice of teaching composition at the college level in a department of comparative literature in relation to the major cultural and social developments and with specific application to the introductory COM 001, COM 002, COM 003, COM 004.
390.prereq_text: Appointment as a Comparative Literature Associate Instructor or consent of instructor.

392.title: Teaching Internship in Comparative Literature
392.description: Regular consultations between the student instructor teaching Comparative Literature courses and a supervisor. Specifically designed for first-time TAs in COM 005, COM 006, COM 007, and COM 010. Instruction in the teaching of writing in a literature course, grading of papers, leading discussions.

032A.title: Introduction to Programming
032A.description: Introduction to programming and problem solving in Python. Aimed primarily at non-major students.
032A.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 036A, ECS 036B, ECS 036C.

032B.title: Introduction to Data Structures
032B.description: Design and analysis of data structures using Python; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, and graphs.
032B.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
032B.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better or ECS 036A C- or better.

032C.title: Implementation of Data Structures in C
032C.description: Programming in the C language. Use of basic UNIX tools. Writing good programs of increased complexity and efficiency. Implementation of data structures in C.
032C.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

036A.title: Programming & Problem Solving
036A.description: Programming in modern C++ for students with prior experience. Fundamental programming constructs, abstraction using functions and basic classes, algorithmic design, and debugging. Emphasis on good programming style and effective use of UNIX-based development tools.
036A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed ECS 032A or ECS 032AV; no credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
036A.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better; or must satisfy computer science placement exam; prior experience with basic programming concepts (variable, loops, conditional statements) required.

036C.title: Data Structures, Algorithms, & Programming
036C.description: Design and analysis of data structures for a variety of applications; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, hashing, and graphs. Extensive programming.
036C.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
036C.prereq_text: (ECS 040 C- or better or ECS 036B C- or better); ECS 020 C- or better.

050.title: Computer Organization & Machine-Dependent Programming
050.description: Comparative study of different hardware architectures via programming in the assembly languages of various machines. Role of system software in producing an abstract machine. Introduction to I/O devices and programming.
050.credit_limit_text: 1 unit of credit if student has taken EEC 070.
050.prereq_text: ECS 040 C- or better or ECS 036B C- or better or ECS 032C C- or better.

088.title: Ethics of Technology
088.description: Foundations of normative ethics for technology, its relationships to moral philosophy and to the law. Technologies and their impacts on the environment and society. Justice, meritocracy, and computer science and engineering. Ethical issues with AI and machine learning.
088.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 188.

092.title: Internship in Computer Science
092.description: Supervised work experience in computer science.
092.prereq_text: Lower division standing; project approval prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

119.title: Data Processing Pipelines
119.description: Introduction to software systems for processing large datasets. Hands-on experience with scripting, data streams, distributed computing, and software development and deployment infrastructure.

120.title: Theory of Computation
120.description: Fundamental ideas in the theory of computation, including formal languages, computability and complexity. Reducibility among computational problems.

122A.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
122A.description: Complexity of algorithms, bounds on complexity, analysis methods. Searching, sorting, pattern matching, graph algorithms. Algorithm design techniques: divide-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming. Approximation methods. NP-complete problems.

130.title: Scientific Computation
130.description: Matrix-vector approach using MATLAB for floating-point arithmetic, error analysis, data interpolation, least squares data fitting, quadrature, zeros, optimization and matrix eigenvalues and singular values. Parallel computing for matrix operations and essential matrix factorizations.
130.prereq_text: (ECS 030 or ENG 006 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 010 or ECS 036A); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

140A.title: Programming Languages
140A.description: Syntactic definition of programming languages. Introduction to programming language features including variables, data types, data abstraction, object-orientedness, scoping, parameter disciplines, exception handling. Non-imperative programming languages. Comparative study of several high-level programming languages.

150.title: Operating Systems & System Programming
150.description: Basic concepts of operating systems and system programming. Processes and interprocess communication/synchronization; virtual memory, program loading and linking; file and I/O subsystems; utility programs. Study of a real operating system.
150.prereq_text: (ECS 034 or ECS 036C or ECS 060); (ECS 154A or EEC 170).

154A.title: Computer Architecture
154A.description: Introduction to digital design. Interfacing of devices for I/O, memory and memory management. Input/output programming, via wait loops, hardware interrupts and calls to operating system services. Hardware support for operating systems software.
154A.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have taken EEC 170.

160.title: Software Engineering
160.description: Requirements, specification, design, implementation, testing, and verification of large software systems. Study and use of software engineering methodologies.

170.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
170.description: Design and implementation of intelligent computer systems. Knowledge representation and organization. Memory and inference. Problem solving. Natural language processing.

171.title: Machine Learning
171.description: Introduction to machine learning. Supervised & unsupervised learning, including classification, dimensionality reduction, regression & clustering using modern machine learning methods. Applications of machine learning to other fields.
171.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

174.title: Computer Vision
174.description: Computer vision is the study of enabling machines to "see" the visual world; e.g., understand images and videos. Explores several fundamental topics in the area, including feature detection, grouping and segmentation, and recognition.
174.prereq_text: (ECS 060 or ECS 032B or ECS 036C); recommended (STA 032 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 27A or MAT 067).

179.title: Gameplay Programming
179.description: Developing gameplay systems in the context of game design and software engineering. Aspects of technical game development that depend on the genre or details of a specific game design, thus making them difficult to abstract and engineer into game engines.
179.prereq_text: ECS 032B or ECS 036C; extensive programming experience recommended.

189G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

191.title: Software Design Project
191.description: Teams plan, implement, and evaluate large-scale projects involving computer and computational systems. Project proposed and supervised by a faculty member.

220.title: Theory of Computation
220.description: Time and space complexity classes. Reductions, completeness, and the role of randomness. Logic and undecidability.

231.title: Large-Scale Scientific Computation
231.description: Algorithms and techniques for large-scale scientific computation, including basics for high performance computing, iterative methods, discrete approximation, fast Fourier transform, Poisson solvers, particle methods, spectral graph partition and its applications.

240.title: Programming Languages
240.description: Advanced topics in programming languages, including formal syntax and semantics, the relation between formal semantics and verification, an introduction to the lambda calculus. Additional topics will include language design principles, alternative programming languages, in-depth semantic theory and models of language implementation.

271.title: Machine Learning & Discovery
271.description: Artificial intelligence techniques for knowledge acquisition by computers. Fundamental problems in machine learning and discovery. Systems that learn from examples, analogies, and solved problems. Systems that discover numerical laws and qualitative relationships. Projects centering on implementation and evaluation.

282.title: Advanced Natural Language Processing
282.description: Use of deep learning techniques in advanced natural language processing. Practicing advanced learning and inference techniques with large language models.
282.prereq_text: ECS 171 or ECS 271; or equivalent machine learning course.

289G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

293A.title: Research in Computer Science
293A.description: Study of research topics in computer science, Ph.D. level research methodologies (experimental, applied and theoretical). Study skills necessary to successfully find/solve significant research problems. Finding and successful interacting with a research advisor. Ethical issues in research/collaborative work.

390.title: The Teaching of Computer Science
390.description: Participation as a teaching assistant or associate-in in a designated engineering course. Methods of leading discussion groups or laboratory sections, writing and grading quizzes, use of laboratory equipment, and grading laboratory reports.
390.prereq_text: Meet qualifications for teaching assistant and/or associate-in in Computer Science.

092.title: Internship in Consumer Science
092.description: Internship on and off campus in a consumer science related area.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Consumer Science
192.description: Internship on and off campus in a consumer science related area.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of a minimum of 84 units.

101.title: Introduction to Critical Theoretical Approaches to Literature & Culture
101.description: Introduction to critical theory and its use for interpreting literary texts, film, and media forms in our present global culture.
101.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

200B.title: Problems in Critical Theory
200B.description: Focused study of a particular critical theoretical approach, school or perspective. Topics may include but are not limited to: critical approaches to the study of literature, culture, film, historiography, visual culture, the body, and aesthetics.

200A.title: Histories of Cultural Studies
200A.description: Histories and traditions of cultural studies internationally;  multiple legacies of cultural studies as a field of inquiry in various geographical contexts; foregrounds important critical perspectives resulting from social and intellectual movements world-wide.
200A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor required. Undergraduate coursework in the humanities or social sciences recommended.

270A.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270A.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270A.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

270B.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270B.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270B.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

270C.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270C.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

290.title: Colloquium
290.description: Designed to provide cohort identity and faculty student exchange.  Opportunity to present papers, hear guest lecturers, and see faculty presentations, gather for organizational and administrative news, exchange information, and make announcements.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

295.title: Special Topics
295.description: Special topics courses offered according to faculty and student interests and demands.
295.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

092.title: Internship in Data Science
092.description: Work experience in Data Science. Supervised internship, on or off campus in areas of data science including data analysis, machine learning, optimization, quantitative finance, geographic information systems, engineering, or data science applications in other fields of inquiry.  Final written report on internship experience required.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Data Science
192.description: Work experience in Data Science. Supervised internship, on or off campus in areas of data science including data analysis, machine learning, optimization, quantitative finance, geographic information systems, engineering, or data science applications in other fields of inquiry.  Final written report on internship experience required.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

194HA.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing, culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of a faculty advisor.

194HB.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HB.description: Directed reading, research and writing, culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of a faculty advisor.

192.title: Internship in Cutaneous Biology
192.description: Approval of project prior to internship by preceptor. Supervised work experience involving research on the skin. Final report.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

199.title: Special Study in Cutaneous Biology
199.description: Special study by individual arrangement of specialized topics in biology of skin. Work may be assigned readings, laboratory research or a combination.
199.prereq_text: Advanced undergraduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research in Cutaneous Biology
299.description: Independent research in cellular and biochemical mechanisms of cutaneous biology and pathology.

001.title: Introduction to Design
001.description: Introduction to design discipline through readings, writing, visual problem solving, and critical analysis. Topics: design principles and elements, vocabulary, color theory, Gestalt principles, conceptualization strategies. Role of designer and products in contemporary culture including social responsibility and sustainability.

014.title: Design Drawing
014.description: Drawing as a tool for design. Basic skills in objective observation and representation, including line, shape, tone, and space. Drawing as a tool for formulating and working through design problems.
014.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); students who have prior unarticulated college level credit in design drawing are encouraged to submit a course equivalency review; this can include classes that have been granted Advanced Placement or International Baccalaureate credits; please see Design Department website for submission requirements and deadlines.

015.title: Form & Color
015.description: Understanding color, form and composition as ways of communicating design concepts and content. Color theory, color mixing, interaction of color. Design principles and elements. Gestalt theory. Explores a variety of materials, media and presentation techniques.
015.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

016.title: Graphic Design & Computer Technology
016.description: Introduction to digital tools with emphasis on graphic design including theory, practice and technology. Includes principles of color, resolution, pixels, vectors, image enhancement, layout, visual organization, visual hierarchy, typography.
016.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

021.title: Drafting & Perspective
021.description: Introduction to mechanical drafting, including scaled drawing, orthogonal projection, isometric, axonometric and perspective. Includes basic rendering techniques.
021.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

040E.title: Design & Social Good
040E.description: Introduction to the relationship of design and social good through theory and practice. Approaches to social good and positive impact including social justice and social entrepreneurship. Climate change, environmental hazards, food justice, and housing justice amidst rapid technological changes. Using design to describe, interrogate, and alleviate some of society’s most pressing issues.

051.title: Computer-Assisted Drawing for Designers
051.description: Computer-assisted drawing (CAD) and modeling using a mid-level, multi-use CAD program. Basic architectural drawing and modeling technique in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional CAD environments.
051.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken DES 150A.
051.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

077.title: Introduction to Structural Design for Fashion
077.description: Study and practice of designing clothing for the human body. Emphasis on flat pattern development, structural joining sequences and the development of three-dimensional garments from two-dimensional drawings.
077.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed DES 077A.
077.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

111.title: Coding for Designers
111.description: Programming concepts/skills for design. Algorithm-based design and development flowcharts. Pseudo-code entry level programming. Principles of coding logic syntax structure. Analysis of history. Development iteration presentation of design projects.
111.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who completed DES 037.
111.prereq_text: DES 001; DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

112.title: UI/UX Design: Principles & Practices
112.description: Principles and practices of User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX). Design for digital, interactive media. Iterative design processes, audience research.

113.title: Photography & Digital Imaging
113.description: Digital imaging techniques using black/white and color. Critical analysis of photographs and the role of photography in society. Explore use and meaning of single, sequence and single composite images.
113.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken DES 031.

115.title: Letterforms & Typography
115.description: Fundamentals of letterforms and typography. Characteristics of typefaces; formatting and composition of type. Principles of legibility, visual hierarchy, grid systems, and the integration of type and image.
115.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit to students who have completed DES 022.
115.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

116.title: Visual Communication: Graphic Design Studio
116.description: Multiple, conceptually-linked assignments focusing on the fundamental choices designers make in translating concepts into effective graphic form. Problem finding and analysis of audience needs. Design process from research and initial concepts to project prototypes. May be taught abroad.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed DES 152 or DES 152A.
116.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; DES 115; or consent of instructor.

117.title: Interactive Media I
117.description: Practice of creating interactive visual media for network-based applications and principles of human computer interaction. Responsive design. User-centered research, information architecture, interface and interaction. Analysis of usability. Development and presentation of design production materials and completed interactive projects.
117.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

134A.title: Introduction to Interior Design–Residential
134A.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of interior design with focus on residential spaces. Basic methods of design conceptualization, development, and presentation.
134A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 021 or DES 051 or DES 150A); or consent of instructor.

135A.title: Furniture Design & Detailing
135A.description: Development of designs for contemporary furniture. Consideration of behavioral and physical requirements, cultural and historic expression, and structural and aesthetic qualities. Process includes research, drawings, and construction of scale models. Required field trip.
135A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

136A.title: Lighting Technology & Design
136A.description: Introduction to lighting design and technology. Understanding the role of lighting and vision in the development of functional and aesthetically pleasing environments.
136A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

145.title: History of Visual Communication
145.description: Historical developments of visual communication, concentrating on the technological and aesthetic development of graphic design; origins and manifestations of current issues in visual communication; provide framework for analysis of current and future trends in visual communication.

151.title: Type in Motion
151.description: Fundamentals of creating motion-based, screen-based typography.  Consideration of narrative structures, movement assemblage, and other visual languages, synthesized within a nuanced understanding of typography within digital space.
151.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor. DES 115 recommended.

154.title: Visual Communication: Message Campaign Design
154.description: Principles and application of visual design strategies for projects that address a broad public audience. Emphasis on design for social awareness/interaction/benefit. Creation of public visual-media campaign.
154.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed DES 152B.
154.prereq_text: DES 115; DES 116; DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

157A.title: Interactive Media II
157A.description: Technical practice for interactive media using the front-end stack (html, css, js). Conceptual framework, user experience, visual interface and interaction design. Research and written pre-production materials required.
157A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; DES 111; DES 117; or consent of instructor.

161.title: Textile Surface Design: Screen & Digital Printing
161.description: Design of textiles and screen printing on fabrics; soft-product development; integration of hand-produced and digitally generated imagery on cloth.

166.title: Human Centered Design
166.description: Human-centered approach to problem solving, ethnography, ideation, project framing, rapid prototypes, visual communication, and experiential learning. Creative approaches to graphic design, industrial design, fashion, business, and entrepreneurship.

167.title: Prototyping: From Objects to Systems
167.description: Exploration of rapid prototyping techniques for objects, interactive experiences, services and organizations. Understanding of additive manufacturing, foam models, digital interfaces and business models.
167.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; or consent of instructor.

171.title: Fashion Drawing: Technical & Illustration
171.description: Exploration of fashion design processes for industry within the social and physical context. Emphasis on two-dimensional conceptualization of ideas, garment construction, and ideation processes utilizing commercial textiles. Field trip required.
171.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor; DES 014 recommended.

177.title: Computer-Assisted Fashion Design
177.description: Advanced exploration of apparel design processes for industry and personal expression with emphasis on computer-assisted design applications. Field trip required.
177.prereq_text: DES 077; DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

180A.title: Advanced Interior Design: Institutional Spaces
180A.description: Advanced interior design problems focused on complex institutional spaces. Introduction to building codes related to interior design. Integration of building systems with interior design solutions.
180A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 021 or DES 051 or DES 150A); or consent of instructor.

191B.title: Workshops in Design
191B.description: Faculty initiated workshops featuring advanced studies and applications of original work in Design: Environment. Letter grading by contract. Field trips included.
191B.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 12 units in one section or a combination of sections.
191B.prereq_text: DES 014; DES 015; and consent of instructor; upper division standing.

221.title: Theory & Issues in Design
221.description: Perspectives on theoretical and aesthetic issues related to the design professions such as methodology in historical and contemporary contexts, implications of technology on design theory and practice, and design relationships to environmental sustainability, recycling, and other social issues.
221.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Design or consent of instructor.

225.title: Studio Practice in Design
225.description: Students work together on a collective project to experience the multiple phases of design through an iterative process. Design projects will be geared towards relevance in contemporary social, cultural and political contexts.

282.title: Biotechnology Internship
282.description: Research at a biotechnology company or interdisciplinary cross-college lab for a minimum of three months as part of the Designated Emphasis in Biotechnology Program.
282.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

294.title: Current Progress in Biotechnology
294.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research activities.

002.title: Acting: The Basics: History & Practice
002.description: Introduction to the historical evolution of the actor–from ancient Greece & Asia to the Hollywood icon & postdramatic performer–and the practical foundations of acting for stage and screen. Onstage opportunities within lecture course structure.

010.title: Introduction to Performance & Digital Media
010.description: An embodied exploration of the fundamentals of movement, speech, theatre, sound and the foundations of digital media. Collaborative and solo performance (spoken and movement) assignments, selected readings and viewing of live and digital performance productions.

014.title: Introduction to Contemporary Dance
014.description: Introduction to basic issues and methods in contemporary dance. Focus on preparing the student for dancing and dance-making through basic techniques of improvisation and composition. Consideration of dance as a cultural practice.

021A.title: Fundamentals of Acting
021A.description: Physical and psychological resources of the actor. Experience in individual and group contact and communication, theatre games, advanced improvisation, sound and movement dynamics. Viewing of theatre productions.

040A.title: Beginning Modern Dance
040A.description: Fundamentals of modern dance focusing primarily on the development of techniques and creative problem solving. Basic anatomy, dance terminology, and a general overview of modern dance history.

042A.title: Beginning Ballet
042A.description: Fundamentals of ballet, focusing on the development of technique through proper alignment, quality, and rhythm. Basic anatomy, ballet terminology, and dance history.

056B.title: History of Theatre & Dance II: Romance, Revenge & Rebellion
056B.description: Exploration of aesthetic movements in various disciplines of theatre and dance from 1550-1850. Examination of genres related to romance, revenge and rebellion using European, North and South American, and Asian examples. Offered once a year.

111.title: Presentation, Communication & Collaboration
111.description: Use of theater techniques for development of clear oral and physical communication skills that build confidence, presentational style and clarity for students whose command of English is at a competent to fluent level.

126.title: Principles of Performing Arts Stage Management
126.description: Stage management principles for theatre, dance, musical theatre, music, and concerts. The dynamical role of the stage manager in the performing arts, upper-management team.

127A.title: Principles of Directing
127A.description: Director's creative approach to the play and to its staging.

130.title: Approaches to Theatrical Design: Practice & Theory
130.description: Advanced design study in specific areas including but not limited to: research, design styles and concepts, new materials and techniques, scenery, lighting, costume, makeup, photography, projections, computer technology, spectacle and special effects, and alternative theatre forms and genres.
130.prereq_text: DRA 124A or DRA 124B or DRA 124C or DRA 124D or DRA 124E; upper division standing in Theatre & Dance, Art Studio or Design; or consent of instructor.

140A.title: Dance Composition
140A.description: Introduction to the craft of choreography. Compose phrases and present movement studies based on the elements of choreography: motivation, space, time, force/energy.
140A.prereq_text: DRA 040A or DRA 041A or DRA 042A; or consent of instructor.

141.title: Introduction to the Fundamentals of Movement
141.description: Introduction to fundamentals of movement that combines intellectual and kinesthetic understanding of the body's skeletal and muscular systems. Explorations based on theories of various body mind specialists including Laban, Feldenkrais, Bartenieff and Sweigard as well as the eastern discipline of Yoga.

145.title: Directed Choreography Projects
145.description: Conceptualization, creation, casting, rehearsing, and concert presentation of complete dances, with students integrating elements of stagecraft and directing the on-stage rehearsals.
145.prereq_text: DRA 140A or DRA 140B or DRA 140C; or consent of instructor.

155.title: Representing Race in Performance
155.description: Representation and performance of "race" in American culture featuring different sub-headings such as "African American Theatre" or "Asian-Americans on Stage."

160A.title: Principles of Playwriting
160A.description: Analysis of dramatic structure; preparation of scenarios; the composition of plays.

174.title: Acting for Camera
174.description: Analysis and practice of acting skills required for camera work and digital media.

185A.title: Special Topics: Artist in Residence-Seminar
185A.description: Exploration of contemporary topics in Theatre and Dance. Individual and collaborative project-based learning. Topics vary by instructor.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of Theatre & Dance.
194HA.prereq_text: Qualification for Letters & Science Honors Program and admission to Theatre & Dance Senior Honors Program.

001.title: The Earth
001.description: Introduction to the study of the Earth. Earth's internal structure; tectonic processes; geological hazards and resources; human relationship to the environment.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050 or EPS 050; only 2 credits for students who have taken GEL 002 or EPS 002.

005.title: Mass Extinctions: Past & Future
005.description: Modern extinctions reviewed and compared to the “big five” mass extinctions that occurred in deep time. Timings, magnitudes, causes, victims, and survivors of each mass extinction, together with the aftermaths of and recovery from each. Climate changes and other related mechanisms at global scales. Similarities and dissimilarities between the past and modern extinctions.
005.prereq_text: Ability to interpret a table of data.

010.title: Climate Change: A Paleo Perspective
010.description: Scientific concepts underlying modern climate change, illustrated through presentation of how Earth’s atmosphere, water resources, land and life are linked and how climate change in the geologic past informs the future. New and anticipated climate solutions and how they address present and projected climate change.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 010

012.title: Dinosaurs - Evolution & Ecology
012.description: Introduction to evolutionary biology, paleobiology, ecology and paleoecology, using dinosaurs as case studies.

016V.title: The Oceans
016V.description: Introductory survey of the marine environment. Oceanic physical phenomena, chemical constituents and chemistry of water, geological history, the seas biota and human utilization of marine resources.
016V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 016 or GEL 016V  or GEL 116 or GEL 116N or EPS 116 or ESP 116N.

025.title: Geology of National Parks
025.description: Appreciation of the geologic framework underlying the inherent beauty of U.S. National Parks. Relationship of individual parks to geologic processes such as mountain building, volcanism, stream erosion, glacial action and landscape evolution.
025.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 025 or GEL 025V.

035.title: Rivers
035.description: Introduction to the dynamics, diversity, and development of rivers and watersheds, with a primary focus on California. Basic geology, hydrology, geomorphology, and ecology of rivers along with assessment of past and current management impacts on river processes, riverine ecosystems, and water supply. Policy and science applications in the field of watershed science.  Optional river field trip.
035.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 035

036.title: The Solar System
036.description: Nature of the sun, moon, and planets as determined by recent manned and unmanned exploration of the solar system. Comparison of terrestrial, lunar, and planetary geological processes. Search for life on other planets. Origin and evolution of the solar system.
036.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 036.

050.title: Physical Geology
050.description: The Earth, its materials, its internal and external processes, its development through time by sea-floor spreading and global plate tectonics.
050.credit_limit_text: Only 2 credits for students who have taken GEL 001 or EPS 001 or the equivlalent; not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050.

050L.title: Physical Geology Laboratory
050L.description: Introduction to classification and recognition of minerals and rocks and to interpretation of topographic and geologic maps and aerial photographs.
050L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050L
050L.prereq_text: GEL 050 (can be concurrent) or EPS 050 (can be concurrent).

100.title: Earth Systems Science
100.description: Interconnectedness of Earth's atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere, biosphere systems and how energy drives material flux and cycling within and between the different Earth systems. Processes, interactions, and feedback within the Earth's systems and how these earth systems are impacted by anthropogenic activities.
100.prereq_text: GEL 050 or EPS 050; GEL 050L or EPS 050L; CHE 002A or CHE 002AH or CHE 004A; CHE 002B or CHE 002BH or CHE 004B.

100L.title: Earth Systems Science Lab
100L.description: Practical, quantitative and analytical skills that pertain to material fluxes and cycling in the atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere and biosphere that constitute the Earth’s interconnected systems.

101.title: Earth Materials & Geochemistry
101.description: Physical and chemical properties of Earth materials; structure, chemical composition, and identification of rock-forming minerals; mineral-rock associations, and their origin from silicate liquids, aqueous fluids, and solid state transformations. Application of understanding of Earth materials to broad problems in Earth sciences. Connections between different Earth sciences disciplines and how Earth materials influence processes and record past processes.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 060
101.prereq_text: (CHE 002A or CHE 002AH or CHE 004A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH or CHE 004B); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 050 or EPS 050); (GEL 050L or EPS 050L).

101L.title: Earth Materials & Geochemistry Lab
101L.description: Introduction to Earth Materials and Geochemistry, including crystallography, optical mineralogy, igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic metamorphic rocks and minerals, and analytical methods. Emphasizes ways in which these subjects inform and underpin broad areas of Earth Science and connections between Earth Sciences disciplines.
101L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 060

107.title: Paleobiology
107.description: The fossilization process and the application of fossils to biological research.
107.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 107
107.prereq_text: GGEL 003 or EPS 003 or GEL 053 or EPS 142 or BIS 002A or BIS 002B or BIO 001.

108.title: Paleoclimatology
108.description: Overview of the climate system;  methods for studying climate history beyond observational records; analyses of drivers, consequences, and characteristics of Earth's climate fluctuations with a focus on the last 600 million years; implications for present climate change from a paleo perspective.
108.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 108.
108.prereq_text: GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 050 or EPS 050 or GEL 116N or EPS 116 or ESP 116N or GEL 016 or EPS 016 or GEL 010 or EPS 010; or consent of instructor.

131.title: Risk, Natural Hazards, & Related Phenomena
131.description: Risk, prediction, prevention and response for earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides, floods, storms, fires, impacts, global warming, modeling and analysis.
131.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 131.
131.prereq_text: (GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 050 or EPS 050); (MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); or consent of instructor; or equivalent introductory geology, calculus, and statistics; STA 013 or STA 013Y recommended.

133.title: Environmental Geochemistry
133.description: Introduction to Earth surface processes with a focus on topics of current environmental interest such as groundwater contamination, radioactivity and nuclear waste disposal, environmental impact of mining operations, and geological approaches to carbon sequestration.
133.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 133
133.prereq_text: (CHE 002A or CHE 002AH or CHE 004A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH or CHE 004).

166.title: Crustal Deformation
166.description: Theory and analysis of Earth’s surface deformation in response to tectonic, volcanic, hydrologic, and human processes. Analysis of deformation fields using geodetic, seismic, and remote sensing data.  Linking patterns of surface deformation to physical mechanisms with elastic, viscoelastic, and poroelastic models. Case studies and data exercises build skills for interpreting deformation in diverse tectonic and environmental settings.
166.prereq_text: (GEL 050 or EPS 050); (MAT 017C or MAT 019C or MAT 021C); (PHY 007C or PHY 009C or PHY 009HC); (ECS 032A or PHY 040), or consent of Instructor or equivalent Python programming course.

186.title: Facilitating Learning in STEM Classrooms
186.description: STEM Learning Assistant Seminar. Theoretical and practical issues of effective teaching in discussion/labs: student-centered, active, cooperative learning environments, responsive teaching, and differentiated classroom instruction.
186.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 186

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Group study focused on topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences.

200AN.title: Principles & Applications of Ecology
200AN.description: Covers principles of community structure and functioning, species diversity patterns, ecosystem ecology and biogeochemistry, landscape ecology, biogeography and phylogenetics.
200AN.prereq_text: MAT 016A; MAT 016B; STA 102; or consent of instructor; first course in Ecology (e.g., ESP 100).

224.title: Data Management & Visualization in R
224.description: Introduction to programming and data analysis in R. Workflow (version control, markdown, reading and writing data), object-oriented programming, statistical analysis, and visualization.

234.title: Bayesian Models: A Statistical Primer
234.description: Practical model-building skills and intuition in statistical modeling. Construction of accurate mathematical expressions to link observation to specific hypotheses. For researchers in the natural and social sciences.
234.prereq_text: EVE 231 or PLS 205 or PLS 120 or EVE 225; or consent of instructor; experience with basic linear modeling and R coding strongly recommended.

245.title: Climate Change Science & Impacts
245.description: Overview of climate change science with a focus on climate change communication. Impacts of climate change on water, agriculture, energy, health, infrastructure, ecosystem services, tribal and indigenous communities. Climate justice, political, societal, and economic dimensions of these issues.

296.title: Topics in Ecology & Evolution
296.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty, and graduate students.

001A.title: Principles of Microeconomics
001A.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the allocation of resources and the distribution of income through a price system; competition and monopoly; the role of public policy; comparative economic systems.

001B.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
001B.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the economy as a whole; determinants of the level of income, employment and prices; money and banking, economic fluctuations, international trade, economic development; the role of public policy.

100A.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Consumer & Producer Theory
100A.description: Consumer and producer theory. Equilibrium and welfare analysis. Topics include competitive markets, consumer and producer surplus at an intermediate level.
100A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100A
100A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

100B.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Imperfect Competition & Market Failure
100B.description: Imperfect competition and market failure. Topics include exchange, monopoly, game theory, uncertainty, asymmetric information, and public goods.
100B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100B.

101.title: Intermediate Macro Theory
101.description: Theory of income, employment and prices under static and dynamic conditions, and long term growth.
101.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

102.title: Analysis of Economic Data
102.description: Analysis of economic data to investigate key relationships emphasized in introductory micro and macro economics. Obtaining, transforming, displaying data; statistical analysis of economic data; basic univariate and multivariate regression analysis.
102.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032); ((MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C) or (MAT 017A, MAT 017B) or (MAT 019A, MAT 019B, MAT 019C) or (MAT 021A or MAT 021B)); or consent of instructor.

111A.title: Economic History
111A.description: Survey of economic change in the United States from Colonial times to 1865; reference to other regions in the Western Hemisphere.
111A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001 BV); or consent of instructor.

115A.title: Economic Development
115A.description:
Major issues encountered in emerging from international poverty, including problems of growth and structural change, human welfare,
population growth and health, labor markets and internal migration. Important issues of policy concerning international trade and industrialization.
115A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

115BY.title: Economic Development
115BY.description: Macroeconomic issues of developing countries. Problems in generating capital, conduct of monetary and fiscal policies, foreign aid and investment.  Issues of policy concerning international borrowing and external debt of developing countries.
115BY.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

122.title: Theory of Games & Strategic Behavior
122.description: Introduction to game theory. Explanation of the behavior of rational individuals with interacting and often conflicting interests. Non-cooperative and cooperative theory. Applications to economics, political science and other fields.
122.prereq_text: (MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better); or consent of instructor.

134.title: Financial Economics
134.description: General background and rationale of corporation; finance as resource allocation over time; decision making under uncertainty and the role of information; capital market and interest rate structure; financial decisions.
134.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ARE 171.
134.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y); (ECN 100B or ARE 100B).

135.title: Money, Banks, & Financial Institutions
135.description: Banks and the banking system. Uncertainty and asymmetric information in the lending process; efficiency of competitive equilibrium in lending markets. Regulation and the conduct of monetary policy.
135.prereq_text: (ECN 101 or ECN 101Y or ECN 101V); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032).

140.title: Econometrics
140.description: Problems of observation, estimation and hypotheses testing in economics through the study of the theory and application of linear regression models. Critical evaluation of selected examples of empirical research and exercises in applied economics.
140.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (ECN 102 or STA 108); or consent of instructor.

151A.title: Economics of the Labor Market
151A.description: Theory of labor supply and demand; determination of wages and employment in the labor market. Policy issues:  labor force participation by married women; minimum wages and youth unemployment; effect of unions on wages.
151A.prereq_text: ECN 100 or ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ARE 100A.

151B.title: Economics of Human Resources
151B.description: Human resource analysis; introduction to human capital theory and economics of education; the basic theory of wage differentials, including theories of labor market discrimination; income distribution; poverty. Policy issues; negative income tax; manpower training programs; incomes policy.
151B.prereq_text: ECN 100 or ECN 100A  or ECN 100AV or ARE 100A.

162.title: International Economic Relations
162.description: International trade and monetary relations, trade policy, exchange rate policy, policies toward international capital migration and investment. Emphasis on current policy issues. Intended for non-majors.
162.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECN 160A or ECN 160B.
162.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); or consent of instructor.

164.title: International Finance
164.description: Advanced international finance. Decision-making processes of large firms, institutional investors and sovereign governments, and their interactions in global financial markets. Pricing of currencies, equities and bonds as well as intermediation and regulation of asset markets. Solving theoretical models, analyzing financial data, and presenting real-life case studies.
164.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an advanced upper division economics course in economic international finance.
164.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100 or ARE 100A); ECN 101.

167.title: Economic Development in Weak States
167.description: Barriers to economic development in developing countries. Economic and policy tools to address barriers within a functioning, well-intentioned government and non-functioning or ill-intentioned governments. Conflict between the state and other subnational actors for legitimate political control. Field experiments and other methodology to understand the success of economic and policy tools in weak states
167.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in economic development in weak states.

200A.title: Microeconomic Theory
200A.description: Linear and non-linear optimization theory applied to develop the theory of the profit-maximizing firm and the utility-maximizing consumer.

200D.title: Macroeconomic Theory
200D.description: Macro static theory of income, employment, and prices.
200D.prereq_text: ECN 101; MAT 021A; MAT 021B; MAT 021C; or equivalent courses.

203C.title: Topics in Economic Theory
203C.description: Selected topics in contemporary microeconomic theory.

210B.title: Economic History
210B.description:
The United States from Colonial times to the present. Other areas of the
western hemisphere may be studied, according to student interest.

215C.title: Microdevelopment Theory & Methods II
215C.description: Extension of development theory and microeconomic methods. Agricultural growth and technological change; poverty and income inequality; multisectoral, including village and regional models. Computable general equilibrium methods and applications.

230A.title: Public Economics
230A.description: Measures of deadweight loss and consumer surplus; optimal commodity and income taxation; tax incidence; policy issues in personal taxation, corporate taxation, and social insurance; the evaluation of effective tax rates.

239.title: Econometric Foundations
239.description: Prepares students for econometric theory and empirical work by examining the statistical foundation of econometrics. Special attention is paid to problems specific to non-experimental data common to social sciences. Topics from matrix algebra are also covered.
239.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

240D.title: Cross Section Econometrics
240D.description: Estimation and inference for nonlinear regression models for cross-section data; models for discrete data and for limited dependent variables; models for panel data; additional topics such as bootstrap and semiparametric regression.

290.title: Topics in Economics
290.description: Selected topics in economic analysis and public policy, focusing on current research.

291.title: Contemporary Economics Seminar
291.description: Seminar series on topics of current interest.

001.title: Cracking the Education Code
001.description: Forces shaping the U.S. educational system and how education intersects with various dimensions of people’s lives. How education influences and is impacted by: law and politics, capital and financial resources, social opportunities, and technological advancements.

081.title: Learning in Science & Mathematics
081.description: Exploration of how students learn and develop understanding in science and mathematics classrooms. Introduction to case studies and interview techniques and their use in K-6 classrooms to illuminate factors that affect student learning.

100.title: Introduction to Schools
100.description: Study of both traditional classroom and out of school/classroom settings; skills for observing educational activities; school and educational organization and finance; school reform movement; observing, aiding, and tutoring in schools and out of school spaces.

110.title: Educational Psychology: General
110.description: Learning processes, cognitive development, individual differences, testing and evaluation.

114.title: Quantitative Methods in Educational Research
114.description: Problems and methods in quantitative research design and analysis in education.

115.title: Educating All Learners: Inclusion & Disability
115.description: Theories, topics, and frameworks related to disability, neurodiversity and inclusive education. Complex learning needs of neurodiverse students within mainstream, general education classrooms.

120.title: Philosophical & Social Foundations of Education
120.description: Philosophical and sociological foundations of education and schools in contemporary societies.

150.title: Cultural Diversity & Education in a Sociopolitical Context
150.description: Critical examination of cultural diversity in U.S. schools in light of long-standing inequalities in education and the identity-affirming pedagogies intended to address them.

152.title: Academic Spanish for Bilingual Teachers
152.description: Communicative class taught in Spanish focused on the development of Spanish communication skills for current and/or future bilingual teachers. Main topics are related to school content areas in bilingual settings, with an emphasis on standard and Southwest Spanish dialects.
152.prereq_text: Acceptance in Teaching Credential Program or consent of instructor.

173.title: Language Development
173.description: Introduction to research and theoretical perspectives on major domains of language development (infant speech perception and production, pragmatics, phonology, vocabulary, grammar, and extended discourse).

181.title: Teaching in Science & Mathematics
181.description: Exploration of effective teaching practices based on examination of how middle school students learn math and science. Selected readings, discussion and field experience in middle school classrooms.
181.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus.

182.title: Visual Communications, Multiliteracies, & Graphic Narratives in Education
182.description: Multiliteracies and the use of graphic narratives and other visual media during instruction and assessments. Multimodal nature of in-person and online interactive communication experiences in society and how these interactions inform learning and instruction in and out of schools.

183.title: Teaching High School Mathematics & Science
183.description: Exploration and creation of effective teaching practices based on examination of how high school students learn mathematics and science. Field experience in high school classrooms.
183.prereq_text: Major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus and consent of the instructor.

200.title: Educational Research
200.description:
Defining educational research questions, reviewing relevant literature,
developing research designs, developing research instruments, selecting appropriate data analysis procedures, and writing research projects. A case problem will provide practice in designing and reporting research.
200.prereq_text: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.

238.title: Participatory Action Research (PAR)
238.description: Principles and strategies of PAR and related methodologies that emphasize collaborating with those affected by the issue being researched in order to educate, take action or effect social change. Conduct interviews with potential collaborators, case analyses and research proposals.

297A.title: Preparing for the Preliminary Writing Exam Paper, Part I
297A.description: Development of a comprehensive literature review in the field of education, including approaches to identifying, critically reviewing and synthesizing the literature, integrating theory in the literature review and developing an argument.

001.title: Global Thinking
001.description: Global perspectives on challenges facing our planet and humanity in historical and contemporary contexts. Understanding transnational systems’ impacts and roles in generating equitable solutions. Global diversity and global action on climate, migration, public health, food/water, inequality, and more.

192.title: Internship in Education Abroad
192.description: Internship with Education Abroad program, potentially either at university or taught abroad.
192.prereq_text: Participation in a study abroad program.

100.title: Circuits II
100.description: Theory, application, and design of analog circuits. Methods of analysis including frequency response, SPICE simulation, and Laplace transform. Operational amplifiers and design of active filters.
100.credit_limit_text: Students who have completed ENG 100 may receive 3.5 units of credit.
100.prereq_text: (ENG 017 C- or better or ENG 017V C- or better); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); EEC 010; or consent of instructor.

116.title: VLSI Design
116.description: CMOS devices, layout, circuits, and functional units; VLSI fabrication and design methodologies.
116.prereq_text: EEC 110A or EEC 111; EEC 018 or 180A recommended.

130A.title: Introductory Electromagnetics I
130A.description: Basics of static electric and magnetic fields and fields in materials. Work and scalar potential. Maxwell's equations in integral and differential form. Plan waves in lossless media. Lossless transmission lines.

132A.title: RF & Microwaves in Wireless Communication
132A.description: Study of Radio Frequency and Microwave theory and practice for design of wireless electronic systems. Transmission lines, microwave integrated circuits, circuit analysis of electromagnetic energy transfer systems, the scattering parameters.

133.title: Electromagnetic Radiation & Antenna Analysis
133.description: Properties of electromagnetic radiation; analysis and design of antennas: ideal, small loop, aperture, and arrays; antenna simulations/measurements.

140A.title: Principles of Device Physics I
140A.description: Semiconductor device fundamentals, equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, conductivity, diffusion, electrons and holes, p-n and Schottky junctions, first-order metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) field effect transistors, bipolar junction transistor fundamentals.
140A.prereq_text: (ENG 017 (can be concurrent) or ENG 017V (can be concurrent)).; (PHY 009D or PHY 009HE).

151.title: Digital Signals & Systems
151.description: Characterization and analysis of discrete time systems. Difference equation models. Z-transform analysis methods. Frequency Analysis. Discrete and fast Fourier transforms. Digital Filtering.

160.title: Signal Analysis & Communications
160.description: Signal analysis based on Fourier methods. Fourier series and transforms; time-sampling, convolution, and filtering; spectral density; modulation: carrier-amplitude, carrier-frequency, and pulse-amplitude.

170.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
170.description: Introduces basic aspects of computer architecture, including computer performance measurement, instruction set design, computer arithmetic, pipelined/non-pipelined implementation, and memory hierarchies (cache and virtual memory). Presents a simplified Reduced Instruction Set Computer using logic design methods from the prerequisite course.
170.prereq_text: (ECS 036B or ECS 030 or ECS 034 or EEC 007); (EEC 018 or EEC 180A).

174AY.title: Applied Machine Learning
174AY.description: Applied machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) in engineering systems. Design and evaluation of components that are critical to artificial intelligence (AI) driven control systems, including but not limited to sensor fusion, feature engineering, computer vision (semantic segmentation, objection detection), ML based classification, and learning-based control systems. Team project including a final presentation and report.
174AY.prereq_text: ENG 006 or MAT 022AL); (EEC 007 or ECS 036B); (EEC 161 or EEC 151 or ECS 036C).

175A.title: Internet of Things
175A.description: Introduction to principles, technologies, challenges, and required expertise to build the Internet of Things (IoT) solutions. Sensing, computing, wireless communication, IP communication, and cloud processing for building an IoT solution.

189L.title: Special Topics in ECS: Solid-State Devices & Physical Electronics
189L.description: Special topics in Solid-State Devices & Physical Electronics.

196.title: Issues in Engineering Design
196.description: Covers various electrical and computer engineering standards and realistic design constraints including economic, manufacturability, sustainability, ethical, health & safety, environmental, social, and political.
196.prereq_text: Senior standing in Electrical or Computer Engineering.

200.title: Navigating Graduate School
200.description: Practical and non-technical skills necessary for first-year students in the Electrical & Computer Engineering Graduate Group. Mentorship, time management, research ethics, science communication, intellectual property.
200.prereq_text: First-year Electrical & Computer Engineering graduate student, Electrical & Computer Engineering transfer student, or instructor approval.

210.title: MOS Analog Circuit Design
210.description:
Analysis and design of MOS amplifiers, bias circuits, voltage references and other analog circuits. Stability and compensation of feedback amplifiers. Introduction to noise analysis in MOS circuits.

Updated prereq to add new V course, ECC 140AV, effective Spring 2023. DS
210.prereq_text: EEC 110B; (EEC 140A B or better or EEC 140AV B or better).

214.title: Integrated Circuit Design for Power Electronics
214.description: IC design for power electronics. Linear and switching regulation. Integrated power management. DC/DC and AC/DC conversion. Applications in portable electronics and wireless sensors.

239A.title: Optical Communication Technologies  for High-Speed Data Networking
239A.description: Enabling technologies for optical fiber communication and data center networks. Physical layer issues for component and system technologies in high-speed data optical communications. High-capacity data multiplexing technologies including wavelength-division-multiplexing, time-division-multiplexing, and advanced coherent modulation. Optical signal transmission, optical amplification, and optical switching for telecom and data center networks.

242.title: Advanced Nanostructured Devices
242.description:
Physics of nano-structured materials and device operation. Overview of new devices enabled by nanotechnology; fabrication and characterization methods; applications of nano-structures and devices.

Updated prereq to add new V course, ECC 140AV, effective Spring 2023. DS

250.title: Linear Systems & Signals
250.description: Mathematical description of systems. Selected topics in linear algebra. Solution of the state equations and an analysis of stability, controllability, observability, realizations, state feedback and state estimation. Discrete-time signals and systems, and the Z-transform.

260.title: Random Signals & Noise
260.description: Random processes as probabilistic models for signals and noise. Probability and random variables, Convergence and limit theorems, Specification of random processes, Markov Chains, Wiener process and white Gaussian noise, Poisson process and shot noise, Processing and frequency analysis of random signals.

266.title: Information Theory & Coding
266.description: Topics include Entropy, Relatively Entropy, Mutual Information; Asymptotic Equipartition Property; Entropy Rates of Stochastic Process; Data Compression; Channel Capacity; Differential Entropy; Gaussian Channel; Rate Distortion Theory; Network Information Theory.

289O.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Integrated Circuits

289Q.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Computer Engineering

290.title: Seminar in Electrical & Computer Engineering
