290.description: Discussion and presentation of current research and development in Electrical & Computer Engineering.

192.title: Emergency Medicine Clinical Research Internship
192.description: Intended to give the upper division undergraduate student an opportunity to conduct "hands-on" clinical research in the Emergency Department. Through the lecture/discussion, students learn the basics of conducting and developing clinical research studies.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; undergraduate student in good academic standing at UC Davis.

192.title: Internship in Endocrinology
192.description: Supervised work experience in endocrinology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

200.title: Introduction to Energy Systems
200.description: Technical, societal and environmental components of energy systems at global, national and regional scales from an interdisciplinary perspective. Energy resources; end-uses and demand; electricity systems; energy efficiency; energy justice; energy emissions; energy policy.

290.title: Energy Seminar
290.description: Selected topics of current interest in energy. Topics vary and will be announced at the beginning of each quarter. Seminar speakers include invited speakers from outside the university as well as faculty.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

001.title: Introduction to Engineering
001.description: Introduction to the role of engineers in the acquisition and development of engineering knowledge, the differences and similarities among engineering fields, and the work ethic and skills required for engineering.

003Y.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
003Y.description: Introduction to the engineering design process that incorporates the development of oral and written communication skills  integral to the design process. Conducted in workshop format with hands-on engagement in the design process.
003Y.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

004.title: Engineering Graphics in Design
004.description: Engineering design, descriptive geometry, pictorial sketching, computer-aided graphics, and their application in the solution of engineering problems.

006.title: Engineering Problem Solving with Applied AI
006.description: Problem-solving methodology, engineering computing, and visualization, emphasizing the responsible application of generative AI to enhance coding, testing, and algorithmic thinking. Foundational programming skills for data analysis and future-ready engineering workflows.
006.prereq_text: (MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better); (MAT 016B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 017B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 019B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B C- or better (can be concurrent)).

008.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
008.description: Students from all majors will learn the processes involved in modern entrepreneurship and identify an opportunity for innovation. The 3 C's of the entrepreneurial mindset (developed by KEEN) will be covered: Curiosity, Connections, and Creating Values.

009.title: Technology Startup Speaker Series
009.description: Presentations from successful entrepreneurs about the challenges of building a technology company, leadership, barriers faced by underrepresented founders, and professional resources to support student entrepreneurship.

017.title: Circuits I
017.description: Basic electric circuit analysis techniques, including electrical quantities and elements, resistive circuits, transient and steady-state responses of RLC circuits, sinusoidal excitation and phasors, and complex frequency and network functions.

035.title: Statics
035.description: Force systems and equilibrium conditions with emphasis on engineering problems.
035.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); MAT 021D C- or better (can be concurrent).

045.title: Properties of Materials
045.description: Introduction to the properties of engineering materials and their relation to the internal structure of materials.
045.prereq_text: (MAT 016C C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better); (CHE 002B C- or better or CHE 004A C- or better); (PHY 007B C- or better or PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better).

100.title: Electronic Circuits & Systems
100.description: Introduction to analog and digital circuit and system design through hands on laboratory design projects.
100.credit_limit_text: Students who have completed EEC 100 may receive only 1.5 units of credit.
100.prereq_text: ENG 017 C- or better or  ENG 017V C- or better.

102.title: Dynamics
102.description: Kinematics and kinetics of particles, systems of particles, and of rigid bodies; application of these topics are applied to engineering problems.
102.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have previously taken ENG 036.
102.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

103.title: Fluid Mechanics
103.description: Fluid properties, fluid statics, continuity and linear momentum equations for control volumes, flow of incompressible fluids in pipes, dimensional analysis and boundary-layer flows.
103.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 150A.
103.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; PHY 009B C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

104.title: Mechanics of Materials
104.description: Uniaxial loading and deformation. General concepts of stress-strain-temperature relations and yield criteria. Torsion of shafts. Bending of beams. Deflections due to bending. Introduction to stability and buckling.
104.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

105.title: Thermodynamics
105.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics: heat energy and work, properties of pure substances, First and Second Law for closed and open systems, reversibility, entropy, thermodynamic temperature scales. Applications of thermodynamics to engineering systems.
105.prereq_text: PHY 009B C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

108.title: Launching a Company
108.description: Technological innovation and product development. Working as a team to turn ideas into companies through customer development.
108.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have previously completed ENG 002 or ENG 080.

188.title: Science & Technology of Sustainable Power Generation
188.description: Focus on scientific understanding and development of power generation that is the basis of modern society. Concentration on power generation methods that are sustainable, in particular, discussion of the most recent innovations.
188.prereq_text: PHY 007C or PHY 009C; upper division standing.

003.title: Introduction to Literature
003.description: Introductory study of several genres of English literature, emphasizing both analysis of particular works and the range of forms and styles in English prose and poetry. Frequent writing assignments.
003.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); or concurrent enrollment in ENL 003A.

003A.title: Writers' Workshop
003A.description: Focuses on the development of writing and revision strategies, exploring ways to understand a writing task; to develop appropriate content for a writing task; to revise content to reflect competence as a communicator.
003A.prereq_text: Has not yet completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement and concurrent enrollment in ENL 003 or ENL 003V

003V.title: Introduction to Literature
003V.description: Introductory study of several genres of English literature, emphasizing both analysis of particular works and the range of forms and styles in English prose and poetry. Frequent writing assignments will be made.
003V.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); or concurrent enrollment in ENL 003A or ENL 003AV.

005F.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Fiction
005F.description: Elementary principles of writing fiction. Write both in prescribed forms and in experimental forms of their own choosing. No final examination.
005F.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005NF.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Non-Fiction
005NF.description: Elementary principles of writing creative non-fiction. Work in prescribed literary forms (such as essay, meditation, biography, memoir, book review, documentary, or experimental non-fiction forms) and forms of students' choosing. No final examination.
005NF.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005P.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Poetry
005P.description: Elementary principles of writing poetry. Write both in prescribed forms and in experimental forms of their own choosing. No final examination.
005P.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

010A.title: Literatures in English I: To 1700
010A.description: Historical introduction to English language and literature from 800-1700. Linguistic borrowing, innovation, and change. Emergence of key literary genres. Colonial America as a new site of English literary production and consumption.
010A.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent.

040.title: Introductory Topics in Literature
040.description: Study of a special topic. Literature written in English in any period or place or genre.  Thematic, formal, or temporal focus.
040.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent.

041.title: Introductory Topics in Literature & Media
041.description: Study of a topic centered on the relationships between literature and moving-image media.
041.prereq_text: (ENL 003 or ENL 003V) or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y); or equivalent.

042.title: Approaches to Reading
042.description: Close reading and interpretation of literature from a variety of traditional and contemporary approaches.  Topics include traditional textual and historical approaches; new criticism; formalism; psychological criticism; feminism and gender; reader-response; materialist approaches. Frequent written assignments.
042.prereq_text: (ENL 003 or ENL 003V) or (UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y); or equivalent.

046.title: Topics in Creative Writing
046.description: Focus on topics in writing fiction, nonfiction/memoir, and poetry at an introductory level. Emphasis on guided practice in techniques of literary creative writing alongside examination of key themes and concerns for writers. Involves a mix of creative and literary-critical writing to develop competencies in these related areas.
046.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

050.title: Careers in English
050.description: Career options for English Majors. Career exploration and decision making using the design thinking process. Learn career tools and skills to help them articulate the application of their major into job skills.

052.title: Pop Culture Shakespeare
052.description: Critical approaches to the study of Shakespeare’s afterlife in contemporary American media. Focus on visual, audio, and kinesthetic modes of analysis and presentation. Relation of Shakespeare to contemporary society, politics, media, and economics.

059.title: Racial Imaginaries
059.description: Critical vocabularies and frameworks for studying the cultural construction of race as a signifier of human difference. Theories of racial formation in poetry, fiction, and other imaginative genres. Rhetorical and media strategies that present and/or obscure the material sources and institutional histories of race and racism.

092.title: Internship in English
092.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.
092.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; and consent of instructor.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; and consent of instructor.

100F.title: Creative Writing: Fiction
100F.description: Writing of fiction. No final examination.
100F.prereq_text: ENL 005F or ENL 005P; ENL 005NF; and consent of instructor.

100NF.title: Creative Writing: Non-Fiction
100NF.description: Writing of non-fiction. No final examination.
100NF.prereq_text: ENL 005F or ENL 005P or ENL 005NF; and consent of instructor.

106.title: English Grammar
106.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
106.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or consent of instructor.

110A.title: Introduction to Literary Theory
110A.description: Key theoretical terms, concepts, and thinkers from the Greeks to the modern era.
110A.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

111.title: Topics in Medieval Literature
111.description: Historically or thematically focused intensive examination of selected topics in Medieval British literature.
111.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

126.title: Food & Literature
126.description: English-language literatures of food from around the world. Literary cultures of food as they relate to broader cultural practices, ethnic and racial identities, place and diaspora. Literary genres and forms of food writing.
126.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003 or COM 004 or NAS 005 or NAS 005V.

130.title: British Romantic Literature
130.description: Historically or thematically focused study of works of Romantic English literature.
130.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

139.title: Topics in Global Literatures & Cultures
139.description: Historically or regionally focused study of world literatures in English (other than the national literatures of British Isles and the United States), particularly from post-colonial regions in Africa, the Caribbean, and Asia, and immigrant cultures in the English-speaking world.
139.prereq_text: ENL 003 or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

149.title: Topics in Literature
149.description: Intensive examination of literature considered in topical terms, not necessarily historically.
149.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

154.title: The Graphic Novel
154.description: Thematically, historically, and formally focused study of the graphic novel genre. Contents may include any regional, national, or transnational group of graphic novels.
154.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent courses.

158A.title: The American Novel to 1900
158A.description:
Historically or thematically organized examination of the rise and development of the American novel from its beginnings; Hawthorne,
Melville, Twain, James, and others.
158A.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

166.title: Love & Desire in Contemporary American Poetry
166.description: Close reading of contemporary American poems on the theme of love and desire by poets of diverse ethnicities and of gay, lesbian, and heterosexual orientations.
166.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

169.title: Memoir & Life-Writing
169.description: English-language memoir and life-writing across various periods. Literary cultures of memoir as they relate to questions of identity, social situation, and broader ideologies of self and culture.
169.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

177.title: Study of an Individual Author
177.description: In-depth study of an author's works; historical context; relation to predecessors and contemporaries; critical reception; influence.

184.title: Literature & the Environment
184.description: Historical and/or thematic survey of topics in writing about the environment.
184.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

187A.title: Topics in Literature & Media
187A.description: Group study of a topic centered on the relationships between literature and film or other moving-image media.
187A.prereq_text: ENL 110A or ENL 110B; and consent of instructor.

189.title: Seminar in Literary Studies
189.description: Intensive, focused study of literature at an advanced level. May be organized by topic, author, period, movement, or genre. High participation.

192.title: Internship in English
192.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills. A maximum of 4 units is allowed toward the major in English.
192.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

195H.title: Honors Thesis
195H.description: Preparation of a thesis, under the supervision of an instructor. Students satisfying requirements for the general major or the teaching emphasis write on a scholarly or critical subject; creative writing students submit a volume of poems or fiction.

197T.title: Tutoring in English
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups designed to develop reading and writing skills and affiliated with one of the university's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of Chairperson.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in English
197TC.description: Field experience, with individuals or in classroom in instruction of English language, literature, and composition. Does not fulfill requirement for major.
197TC.prereq_text: Upper division standing and a major in English; consent of Chairperson.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or ENL 005F or ENL 005P or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

200.title: Introduction to Graduate Studies in English
200.description: Introduction to literary scholarship with special attention to the elements of professionalism and to different modes of literary investigation.

248.title: 18th-Century Literature
248.description: Studies in 18th-century literature. Course materials to be selected by the instructor. Preparation and evaluation of research papers.

290F.title: Creative Writing: Fiction
290F.description:
Writing of prose fiction. Evaluation of written materials and individual student
conferences.
290F.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing, with preference given to those enrolled in master's program in Creative Writing.

290P.title: Creative Writing: Poetry
290P.description: Writing of poetry. Evaluation of written materials and individual student conferences.
290P.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing, with preference given to those enrolled in master's program in Creative Writing.

299D.title: Special Study for the Doctoral Dissertation
299D.description: Special study for the doctoral dissertation.

391.title: Teaching Creative Writing
391.description: Designed for new instructors of ENL 005F or ENL 005P; discussion of ways to facilitate creative writing workshops and to respond to student manuscripts.
391.prereq_text: Graduate standing; appointment as Teaching Assistant in the English Department.

393.title: Teaching Literature & Composition
393.description: Designed for new instructors of  ENL 003 or the equivalent courses; discussion of problems related to teaching literature and composition to lower division students.
393.prereq_text: Graduate standing; appointment as Teaching Assistant in the English Department.

001.title: Art, Science & the World of Insects
001.description: Fusion of entomology and art to create an appreciation of insect biology, ecology, interactions with humans and importance in human culture. Multidisciplinary approaches in education and career paths in entomology and art will be highlighted.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work-learn experience on and off campus in all subject areas offered by the department, supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

100.title: General Entomology
100.description: Biology, anatomy, physiology, development, classification, ecology and relation of insects to human welfare.
100.prereq_text: BIS 002B; or consent of instructor.

100L.title: General Entomology Laboratory
100L.description: Anatomy, development, population ecology, methods of collecting, classification and identification of insects of all orders and of major families.

105.title: Insect Ecology
105.description: Introduction to insect ecology combining fundamental concepts and questions in ecology with ideas, hypotheses and insights from insects. Integration of individual, population, community and ecosystem ecology.
105.prereq_text: BIS 002B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

108.title: Evolution & Ecology of Arachnids
108.description: Spider external morphology, functional anatomy, metabolism, neurobiology, development, predatory & reproductive behavior, ecology, phylogeny, systematics, zoogeography, and faunistics.

108L.title: Evolution & Ecology of Arachnids Laboratory
108L.description: Laboratory on spider natural history, identification, external morphology, and taxonomy, morphology and identification. Emphasis on the spiders of the California Floristic Province.
108L.prereq_text: (BIS 002C or ENT 100 or ENT 100L); ENT 108 (can be concurrent); ENT 108 required concurrently or consent of instructor.

110.title: Arthropod Pest Management
110.description: Sustainable management & ecology of arthropod pests in agricultural systems. Techniques for effective, management of arthropod pests via in-depth knowledge about pest biology, life strategies, spatial ecology, and food web functions. Lab & field trip exercises in applied research in pest management, ecology, and evolution using digital technologies (apps, remote sensing, cloud-based decision support).
110.prereq_text: (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100 C- or better); BIS 002B C- or better; or consent of instructor.

120.title: Pollination Biology
120.description: Natural history, ecology, evolution and applications of pollination. Conceptual underpinnings and basic methodologies of pollination. Primary focus on animal-mediated pollination.
120.prereq_text: BIS 002B C- or better; or consent of instructor. EVE 100 & EVE 101 recommended.

153L.title: Lab Course in Medical Entomology
153L.description: Medical entomology and vector control; physiology and identification of disease vectors; methods for trapping and sampling mosquitoes and ticks; techniques for testing insecticide resistance; utilization of online resources for epidemiological data analysis; inclusion of field trips for mosquito and tick collections and visits to vector control districts for practical insights.
153L.prereq_text: ENT 153 C or better; or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Laboratory experience or fieldwork off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Entomology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

197T.title: Tutoring in Entomology
197T.description: Leading small discussion groups. Preview assignments and prepare guidelines for discussion.

290.title: Exploratory Topics in Entomology
290.description: Interdisciplinary topics in entomology, including innovative applications of entomological concepts to other fields of research and human endeavor (e.g. medicine, technology, art, criminology).

006.title: Introduction to Environmental Plants
006.description: Classification, nomenclature and variation of environmental plants. The use of floral and vegetative characteristics and terminology to key unknown plants. Characteristics of plant groups and basics of climate, soils and plant selection. Identification of 150 common landscape plants.

100.title: Urban Forests are Nature-Based Solutions
100.description: Principles and practices of planning and managing urban vegetation, forests, green infrastructures and nature-based solutions. Basics of tree/site monitoring, natural resource inventory, and development of long term urban forest management plans at both local and landscape scales.
100.prereq_text: PLS 002 or BIS 002B or LDA 001.

200A.title: Climate Change Impacts, Mitigation, & Natural Resources Management
200A.description: Major topics in environmental sciences, with emphasis on climate change impacts on natural and human managed systems.

202.title: Policy Development & Implementation
202.description: Environmental policy development and implementation processes: developing and enacting legislation, regulation development and review, and implementation of new laws. California state processes. Local, federal, and international policy. Business’ role in climate policy. Theory, applied study, discussion with guest experts, and practical skills such as how to write for a policy audience.

224.title: Data Management & Visualization in R
224.description: Introduction to programming and data analysis in R. Workflow (version control, markdown, reading and writing data), object-oriented programming, statistical analysis, and visualization.

297.title: Professional Development Seminar
297.description: Weekly seminar focused on the development of professional skills needed for environmental careers. May feature guest speakers working in environmental or policy careers to discuss pathways and day-to-day job tasks and skills required.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in resource sciences. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

100.title: Introduction to Water Science
100.description: Basic concepts of water science. All components of the water cycle, including precipitation and snow, evaporation and transpiration, streamflow, hydraulic flow through porous media, groundwater flow, hydrographs and flow/flood routing, water quality, and representative water-resources problems.
100.prereq_text: CHE 002B; (MAT 016B (can be concurrent) or MAT 017B (can be concurrent) or MAT 019B (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B (can be concurrent)); (PHY 001B (can be concurrent) or PHY 007B (can be concurrent) or PHY 009B (can be concurrent)); consent of instructor.

144.title: Trees & Forests
144.description: Biological structure and function of trees as organisms; understanding of forests as communities and as ecosystems; use of forests by humans; tree phenology, photosynthesis, respiration, soil processes, life histories, dormancy, forest biodiversity, and agroforestry.
144.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 144 or ENH 144 or ERS 144. (Formerly PLB 144 or ENH 144 or ERS 144.)

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in resource sciences. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Senior Honor Thesis
194H.description: Independent study, guided research on an environmentally related subject of special interest to the student.
194H.prereq_text: Senior standing, overall GPA of 3.50 or higher and consent of master advisor.

001.title: Environmental Analysis
001.description: Analysis of the physical, biological, and social interactions which constitute environmental problems. Emphasis on analysis of environmental problems, the consequences of proposed solutions, and the interaction of environmental science and public policy in creating solutions.
001.prereq_text: UWP 001 (can be concurrent) or UWP 001Y (can be concurrent) or UWP 001V (can be concurrent) or ENL 003 (can be concurrent) or ENL 003V (can be concurrent); or equivalent; sophomore standing; ECN 001A and BIS 002B recommended.

100.title: General Ecology
100.description: Theoretical & experimental analysis of the distribution, growth & regulation of species populations; predator-prey & competitive interactions; and the organization of natural communities. Application of evolutionary & ecological principles to selected environmental problems.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken EVE 101.
100.prereq_text: (BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); STA 013 recommended.

101.title: Ecology, Nature, & Society
101.description: Interdisciplinary study of diversity and change in human societies, using frameworks from anthropology, evolutionary ecology, history, archaeology, psychology, and other fields. Topics include population dynamics, subsistence transitions, family organization, disease, economics, warfare, politics, and resource conservation.
101.prereq_text: ANT 001 or ANT 002 or ESP 030 or EVE 100 or BIS 101 recommended.

161.title: Environmental Law
161.description: Introduction for non-Law School students to some of the principal issues in environmental law and the judicial interpretation of some important environmental statutes, e.g., NEPA.
161.prereq_text: Upper division standing; one course in environmental science or political science recommended.

163.title: Energy & Environmental Aspects of Transportation
163.description: Engineering, economic, and systems planning concepts. Analysis and evaluation of energy, air quality and selected environmental attributes of transportation technologies. Strategies for reducing pollution and petroleum consumption in light of institutional and political constraints. Evaluation of vehicle emission models.
163.prereq_text: Upper division standing in engineering or economics or environmental studies.

165.title: Climate Policy
165.description: Models, data and assumptions behind competing arguments regarding societal response to the prospect of climate change at the state, national and international level from economic, ethical and policy science perspectives.
165.prereq_text: ESP 001 or ECN 001A  or ESP 001AY or ECN 001AV; or consent of instructor.

166.title: Ocean & Coastal Policy
166.description: Overview of U.S. and International ocean and coastal policy, including energy, coastal land-use and water quality, protected areas and species.

168A.title: Methods of Environmental Policy Analysis
168A.description: Evaluation of alternatives for solution of complex environmental problems; impact analysis, benefit cost analysis, distributional analysis, decision making under uncertainty, and multi-objective evaluation.
168A.prereq_text: (ESP 001 or ESP 010); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100); (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); ECN 100 recommended.

170.title: Conservation Biology Policy
170.description: Analysis of policies designed to conserve species and their habitats. Emphasis on how individual incentives affect the success of conservation policies. Valuation of endangered species and biodiversity. Criteria for deciding conservation priorities.
170.prereq_text: One course in environmental science (e.g., ESP 001), conservation (e.g., WFC 011 or WFC 154), or government (e.g., POL 001) recommended.

172.title: Public Lands Management
172.description: Investigation of alternative approaches to public lands management by Federal and state agencies. Role each agency's legislation plays in determining the range of resource allocations.

010.title: Introduction to Environmental Toxicology
010.description: Hazardous substances, their effects on humans and their actions and movement in the environment. Emphasis on substances of current concern.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

101.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
101.description: Principles of toxicology with a focus on environmental, industrial, and natural chemicals.  Topics include fate and effects of chemicals in organisms and the environment, air pollutants, insecticides, aquatic toxicology, endocrine disruptors, biomarkers and bioassays, and risk assessment.

104.title: Environmental & Nutritional Factors in Cellular Regulation & Nutritional Toxicants
104.description: Cellular regulation from nutritional/toxicological perspective. Emphasis: role of biofactors on modulation of signal transduction pathways, role of specific organelles in organization/regulation of metabolic transformations, major cofactor functions, principles of pharmacology/toxicology important to understanding nutrient/toxicant metabolism.

131.title: Environmental Toxicology of Air Pollutants
131.description: Field trip required. Toxicology of air pollutants in the ambient, indoor, and occupational environments.  Health effects, sources, environmental fates, pulmonary responses, sampling and analyses, and air-quality criteria and standards.  Field trip required.
131.prereq_text: CHE 008B (can be concurrent); or the equivalent; BIS 102 recommended.

135.title: Health Risk Assessment of Toxicants
135.description: Current practices of health risk assessment of environmental chemicals using toxicological principles and their application to regulatory control of these chemicals.

190.title: Seminar
190.description: Selected topics presented by students, faculty, or outside speakers covering current research and instructional activities within environmental toxicology. Reports and discussion concerning oral and written presentations, literature sources, and career opportunities.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference of advanced research methods and the interpretation of research results.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Honors Research
194HA.description: Specific research project conducted under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Experience to include experimental design, learning new techniques, data analysis and interpretation of findings.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing; minimum GPA of 3.250.

194HB.title: Honors Research
194HB.description: Specific research project conducted under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Experience to include experimental design, learning new techniques, data analysis and interpretation of findings.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing; minimum GPA of 3.250.

194HC.title: Honors Research
194HC.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing, minimum GPA of 3.250.

197T.title: Tutoring in Environmental Toxicology
197T.description: Teaching toxicology including conducting discussion groups for regular departmental courses under direct guidance of staff.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advanced standing in Environmental Toxicology, a related major, or the equivalent experience.

220.title: Analysis of Toxicants
220.description: Principles of microanalysis of toxicants.  Theoretical considerations regarding separation, detection and quantitative determination of toxicants using chemical and instrumental techniques.

220L.title: Analysis of Toxicants Laboratory
220L.description: Laboratory techniques for microanalysis of toxicants. Separation, detection, and quantitative determination of toxicants using chemical and instrumental methods.
220L.prereq_text: ETX 220 (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.

260.title: Immunotoxicology
260.description: Provides students with skills and knowledge for evaluating and applying research on the impact of environmental toxicants on immunological function in human and wildlife populations.
260.prereq_text: Undergraduate or graduate introduction to immunology coursework recommended but not required; graduate standing or consent of instructor.

280.title: Forensic DNA Analysis
280.description: Foundation in theory and practice of forensic DNA analysis; past, present, and emerging technologies; legal and quality assurance issues. DNA extraction, DNA quantitation, multiplex amplification of STR loci, capillary electrophoresis of amplified products, and analysis of STR typing data.
280.prereq_text: Coursework in genetics and molecular biology.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current topics in environmental toxicology.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of advanced research methods and interpretation of research results. Designed primarily for graduate students.

297T.title: Tutoring in Environmental Toxicology
297T.description: Teaching toxicology including conducting discussion groups for regular departmental courses under direct guidance of staff.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in Environmental Toxicology, a related major, or the equivalent experience.

202.title: Quantitative Epidemiology I: Probability
202.description: Foundations in probability for epidemiologists. Emphasis on properties of and relationships between distributions and application of probability concepts to epidemiology. Includes a mathematical skills laboratory to assist in solution of epidemiologic problems.
202.prereq_text: ((MAT 016A,  MAT 016B) or (MAT 017A,  MAT 017B) or (MAT 021A,  MAT 021B)); STA 100; STA 108 (can be concurrent); or equivalent of any listed course with consent of instructor; concurrent or previous enrollment in a basic epidemiology course (e.g., EPI 205).

205.title: Principles of Epidemiology
205.description: Basic epidemiologic concepts and approaches to epidemiologic research, with examples from veterinary and human medicine, including outbreak investigation, infectious disease epidemiology, properties of tests, and an introduction to epidemiologic study design and surveillance.
205.prereq_text: MPM 202; or consent of instructor; an introductory statistics course.

208.title: Analysis & Interpretation of Epidemiologic Data
208.description: Application of theory and concepts of statistics and epidemiology to analysis and interpretation of data typically found in veterinary and human epidemiologic research.
208.prereq_text: EPI 204 (can be concurrent); EPI 207; (STA 144 or PHR 202); and entry level skill in standard statistical software; e.g., SPSS, BMDP, SAS, Stata, MinTab, S-Plus.

290.title: Seminars in Epidemiology
290.description: Faculty and students will present and lead discussion of ongoing or published epidemiologic research.

291.title: Seminars in Human Health Services Research & Clinical Epidemiology
291.description: Critical review, evaluation, and discussion of research in health services and clinical epidemiology. Presentation of statistical, epidemiologic, and econometric methods. Students present their own research and critique the work of others.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Group study in selected areas of epidemiology.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research in selected areas of epidemiology.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Evolution & Ecology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

100.title: Introduction to Evolution
100.description: General survey of the origins of biological diversity and evolutionary mechanisms.
100.prereq_text: (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019B or MAT 021B); ((BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002,  BIO 003)); STA 100 recommended.

101.title: Introduction to Ecology
101.description: General survey of the principles of ecology.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ESP 100.
101.prereq_text: ((BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002, BIO 003)); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019B or MAT 021B); or the equivalent.

102.title: Population & Quantitative Genetics
102.description: Evolution as caused by random mating, genetic drift, natural selection, inbreeding, migration, and mutation in theory and actuality. The resemblance between relatives and consequences of selection for quantitative traits. Application of these ideas to topics such as the evolution of sex.

117.title: Plant Ecology
117.description: Study of the interactions between plants, plant populations or vegetation types and their physical and biological environment.  Special emphasis on California. Four full-day field trips and brief write-up of class project required.
117.prereq_text: (BIS 002A, BIS 002B, BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002, BIO 003); PLB 111 recommended.

125.title: Ecological Statistics
125.description: Statistical approaches appropriate for discrete counts, small sample sizes, and non-independent observations, applied to ecological data. Principles of probability and likelihood, discrete probability distributions, and generalized linear models, leading to mixed and mixture models.
125.prereq_text: BIS 002B; MAT 017A or MAT 016A or MAT 021A or MAT 019A; STA 100 recommended; some familiarity with data analysis (e.g., high school or university classes in statistics, experience analyzing data in lab classes or independent research) highly encouraged.

131.title: Human Genetic Variation & Evolution
131.description: Introduction to genome-wide nucleotide sequence variation in human populations and computational methods for its analysis. Topics to include forensics, disease gene mapping, and studies of human evolutionary history. Misuses, such as eugenics, and ethical/legal issues will be discussed.

189.title: Introduction to Biological Research
189.description:
Introduction to research methods in biology. Presentation and discussion
of research by faculty, graduate, and undergraduate students.
189.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Evolution & Ecology or related biological science.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Evolution & Ecology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Research Honors
194HA.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HA.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

194HB.title: Research Honors
194HB.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HB.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

194HC.title: Research Honors
194HC.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HC.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Sciences 2B
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in a Biological Sciences 2B laboratory. Tutoring is voluntary and is supervised by a Laboratory Teaching Assistant and the Laboratory Coordinator.
197T.prereq_text: BIS 001B B or better.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in biology.

390.title: Methods of Teaching
390.description: Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching. Includes analyses of texts and supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques and preparing and conducting of laboratory and discussion sections.

117.title: Exercise & Aging in Health & Disease
117.description: Etiology of and standard therapy for various diseases associated with inactivity and aging; e.g., cardiovascular, pulmonary, diabetes, obesity, lipemias, etc. Exercise will then be considered as a protective and/or therapeutic modality.
117.prereq_text: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C; or consent of instructor.

092C.title: Primary Care Clinic
092C.description: Students must apply and interview with the Board of Clinica Tepati or Imani Clinic. Field experience exposes lower division students to health care delivery, patient histories, physical examinations, health promotion, disease prevention, diagnosis; treatment of episodic, acute, chronic illness; appropriate referral and follow-up.
092C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment at the UC Davis campus, for freshman and sophomore students.

192C.title: Primary Care Clinics
192C.description: Students must apply and interview with the Board of Clinica Tepati or Imani Clinic. Field experience introduces students to health care delivery, patient histories and physical examinations, health promotions and disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment of episodic, acute and chronic illness, basic laboratory testing and appropriate referral and follow-up.
192C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment at the UC Davis campus; upper division standing.

192.title: Internship in Fiber & Polymer Science
192.description: Work experience off campus in a fiber and polymer science related area. Supervision by a member of the Textiles and Clothing faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Fiber & Polymer Science
197T.description: Tutoring of students in Fiber & Polymer Science courses. Assistance with discussion groups and laboratory sections under supervision of instructor.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division fiber and polymer science related major.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

127.title: Film Theory
127.description: Survey of the conceptual frameworks used to study film (including semiotics, psychoanalysis, spectatorship, auteur, genre and narrative theories). Historical survey of major film theorists.

001.title: Principles of Food Science
001.description: Food science fundamentals. Fresh and processed food technologies; world food problems; food composition; food microbiological and toxicological safety; food laws; evaluation of acceptability and nutritional value.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed any FST course, except FST 010.

010.title: Food Science, Folklore & Health
010.description: Ancient and modern food folklore in relation to health and well-being. Food safety, organic food, herbalism, food preservation, and nutritional enhancement.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed FST 002.

050.title: Introduction to Food Preservation
050.description: Introduction to modes of fresh food preservation including use of chemicals and microbes, heat and energy, control of water and atmosphere, and by indirect approaches such as packaging, hygienic design and sanitation.
050.prereq_text: CHE 002A; ((BIS 002A (can be concurrent) or BIO 002 (can be concurrent)); ((STA 013 (can be concurrent) or STA 013Y (can be concurrent) or STA 100 (can be concurrent)).
