100A.title: Food Chemistry
100A.description: Chemical aspects of food composition. Emphasis on the functional properties and chemical reactions of the major components of foods: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and water.
100A.prereq_text: (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B); BIS 002A recommended.

101A.title: Food Chemistry Laboratory
101A.description: Study of basic chemical and physical properties that influence the reactivity and functional properties of components in food systems.

102A.title: Malting & Brewing Science
102A.description: Technology of the malting, brewing and fermentation processes is integrated with the chemistry, biochemistry and microbiology that determine industrial practices and product quality.
102A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken FST 102.
102A.prereq_text: ((BIS 102 or BIS 102V), BIS 103) or BIS 105; senior standing recommended.

106.title: Food Chemistry for Clinical Nutrition
106.description: Chemical and physical principles that influence functional properties, nutrient content, safety, and sensory aspects of food. Emphasis on the application of these concepts in clinical nutrition.
106.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have completed FST 101A and/or FST 101B.
106.prereq_text: CHE 008B C- or better or CHE 118B C- or better or CHE 128B C- or better; concurrent with FST 100A recommended.

110.title: Food Processing
110.description: Application of the conservation of mass and energy to food processing. Elements of engineering thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer. Quantitative analysis through problem solving and simulation.
110.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students enrolled in College of Engineering.
110.prereq_text: PHY 007A; PHY 007B; PHY 007C (can be concurrent); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 021C).

117.title: Design & Analysis for Sensory Food Science
117.description: Methods of design and analysis for sensory food science. Experimental design strategies. Use of taste panels and consumer testing. Data analysis and computation including the relative merits and limitations of parametric and nonparametric approaches. Modifications for quality assurance.

131.title: Food Packaging
131.description: Principles of food packaging. Functions of packaging. Properties of metal, glass, paper and plastic materials and packages. Design, fabrication, and applications of food packaging. Packaging of fresh and processed foods, including fruits and vegetables, dairy foods, beer and wine.

192.title: Internship for Advanced Undergraduates
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in the practical application of food science.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

201.title: Food Chemistry & Biochemistry
201.description: Advanced topics in food chemistry and biochemistry, emphasizing the application of the basic principles of chemistry and biochemistry to food composition, properties, preservation and processing. Chemical structures, interactions, reaction mechanisms and experimental methods are stressed.
201.prereq_text: Undergraduate courses in organic chemistry and biochemistry; undergraduate course in food chemistry is recommended.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Critical presentation and evaluation of original research by graduate students. Planning of research programs and proposals. Discussion led by individual major instructors for their research group.

291.title: Advanced Food Science Seminar
291.description: Oral presentation of student's original research, discussion, and critical evaluation.
291.prereq_text: FST 290; completion of at least one quarter of FST 290.

120L.title: Quantity Food Production Laboratory
120L.description: Laboratory experience in quantity food production and service.

201A.title: Forensic Science Fundamentals-A
201A.description: Professional responsibilities and ethics, physical evidence concepts, drug chemistry and toxicology, controlled substances and analytical chemistry and instrumentation as practiced in the forensic sciences. First of three courses that, in part, covers the curriculum requirements of the Forensic Education Program Accreditation Committee (FEPAC).
201A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrolled in the Forensic Science Graduate Program.

207.title: Advanced Spectroscopy Methods in Forensic Science
207.description: Discuss, evaluate and interpret advanced molecular spectra/structure, Infrared Spectroscopy, such as chemical applications of spectroscopic methods, vibrational, rotational spectra; electronic spectra, photoelectron spectroscopy generated by various analytical instruments used in forensic science community.

220.title: Analysis of Toxicants
220.description: Principles of microanalysis of toxicants. Theoretical considerations regarding separation, detection and quantitative determination of toxicants using chemical and instrumental techniques.

221L.title: Forensic Science Analytical Instrumentation
221L.description: Methodology and instruments used for the analysis of substances of interest in the discipline of Forensic Science. Practical experience with modern instrumental techniques & methodologies used in the advanced forensic science laboratory.

280.title: Forensic DNA Analysis
280.description: Foundation in theory and practice of forensic DNA analysis; past, present, and emerging technologies; legal and quality assurance issues. DNA extraction, DNA quantitation, multiplex amplification of STR loci, capillary electrophoresis of amplified products, and analysis of STR typing data.
280.prereq_text: Coursework in genetics and molecular biology.

290.title: Seminar in Forensic Science
290.description: Students will be exposed to topical areas in Forensic Science by presentations conducted by expert guest speakers.  The seminar will also serve as a medium whereby the exiting students will present the research conducted as part of their thesis requirement.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference in Forensic Science
290C.description: Individual and/or group conference on problems, progress and techniques in forensic science and research.

001Y.title: Elementary French
001Y.description: Introduction to French grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent courses FRE 001 or FRE 001S; students who have completed two or more years of French in high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

021Y.title: Intermediate French
021Y.description: Review of grammar and vocabulary acquired in the elementary sequence, as well as the study of new grammatical structures and a continuing enrichment of vocabulary through oral work in class, written exercises, readings and compositions.
021Y.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have completed FRE 021 or FRE 021S.

022Y.title: Intermediate French
022Y.description: Continuation of FRE 021 or FRE 021S. Review of grammar and vocabulary, as well as the study of new grammatical structures and a continuing enrichment of vocabulary.

100.title: Composition in French
100.description: Instruction and practice in expository writing in French, with emphasis on organization, correct syntax, and vocabulary building.
100.prereq_text: FRE 023 or FRE 023Y.

102.title: Theater in French
102.description: Study of plays from across the French-speaking world, in various styles and genres.

107B.title: The Making of Modern France
107B.description: Political and cultural history of France from Wars of Religion through 1870, using historical documents, painting, architecture, music. Versailles and absolutism, revolts and revolutions, the industrial transformation of Paris, the role of women and minorities in society, and France’s relationship with the broader world. Practice reading, writing, and speaking French.
107B.prereq_text: FRE 023 or FRE 023Y; consent of instructor.

109.title: French Phonetics
109.description: Introduction to the sound-inventory of French and practice in phonetic transcription, with a focus on ways in which phonetic contrasts signal grammatical contrasts; spoken forms and spelling; formal differences between the "Standard" and other varieties across the French-speaking world.

200.title: Introduction to Graduate Study in French
200.description: Introduction to a range of methodologies and critical practices in the field of French Studies, including literature, culture, and linguistics. Covers basic principles of bibliographic research in the humanities.

390A.title: The Teaching of French in College
390A.description: Designed for graduate teaching assistants with emphasis on problems and procedures encountered by teachers of lower division classes at the university.
390A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

001.title: First-Year Seminar
001.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

002.title: First-Year Seminar
002.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

003.title: First-Year Seminar
003.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

004.title: First-Year Seminar
004.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

301.title: Developing Teaching Resources
301.description: Development of curricular materials relevant to undergraduate science courses including complete learning outcomes, lesson plans, learning activities, assessments, data from implementation, and student or peer evaluation of material.

192.title: Internship in Gastroenterology
192.description: Supervised work experience in gastroenterology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

050.title: Introduction to Critical Gender Studies
050.description: Introduction to interdisciplinary, critical gender studies. Emergence of women’s, gender and feminist studies internationally, its links to women’s movements, and its influence within the various arts, humanities, and social science disciplines.

080.title: Special Topics in Critical Gender Studies
080.description: In-depth examination of a women and gender studies topic related to the research interest of the instructor.

104.title: Feminist Research
104.description: Feminist applications and transformations of traditional disciplinary research practices; initial training in methodologies for feminist trans-disciplinary work.
104.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken WMS 104

170.title: Queer Studies
170.description: Queer sexualities, identities, theories, and practices. Alternative sexualities as historical, social, and cultural constructions in intersections with race, gender, class, nationality. Interdisciplinary exploration of sexual liberation and the regulation of sexuality through history, theory, and expressive cultural forms.
170.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously taken WMS 170
170.prereq_text: GSW 070 recommended or consent of instructor.

185.title: Women & Islamic Discourses
185.description: Introduction to debates/discourses about women and Islam. Transformations in debates/discourses in colonial and postcolonial periods in the Middle East & South Asia. Comparative study of debates/discourses on family, work, law, sexuality, religion, comportment, human rights, and feminist and religious movements.
185.prereq_text: GSW 050 or GSW 050V; or comparable course.

192.title: Internship in Gender, Sexuality, & Women's Studies
192.description: Supervised internship and study in positions or institutional settings dealing with gender-related problems or issues, for example, a women's center, affirmative action office, advertising agency, or social welfare agency. Final written report on internship experience required.
192.prereq_text: Completion of 84 units; enrollment is dependent on the availability of intern positions with priority given to GSW majors; consent of instructor.

194HA.title: Senior Honors Project in Gender, Sexuality, & Women's Studies
194HA.description: In consultation with an advisor, students complete a substantial research paper or significant creative project on a GSW topic.
194HA.prereq_text: Senior standing; GSW major; advisor's approval; consent of instructor.

200B.title: Feminism & Research Methodology
200B.description: Application of feminist epistemology and ethics in the design of graduate research.
200B.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; students are required to have Bachelor's Level Competency in Gender Studies.

201.title: Special Topics in Feminist Theory & Research
201.description: In-depth exploration of a topic of feminist theory and research related to the interests of the instructor.

192.title: Internship in General Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in general medicine.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

291.title: Seminars in Human Health Services Research & Clinical Epidemiology
291.description: Critical review, evaluation, and discussion of research in health services and clinical epidemiology. Presentation of statistical, epidemiologic, and econometric methods. Students present their own research and critique the work of others.

201A.title: Advanced Genetic Analysis
201A.description: Fundamentals of genetic analysis and chromosome structure using model organisms including mutation, transmission, complementation, suppression, and enhancement as well as epigenetic phenomena at the whole organism and molecular levels.
201A.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); STA 100; or the equivalent, graduate standing.

205.title: Molecular Genetics Laboratory
205.description: Students will conduct experiments in molecular genetics laboratories. Individual research problems will emphasize experimental design, experience with methodologies, and data interpretation.
205.prereq_text: BIS 101 (can be concurrent) or BIS 101V (can be concurrent); or the equivalent course; enrolled in Genetics Graduate Group.

220.title: Genomics & Biotechnology of Plant Improvement
220.description: Integration of modern biotechnology and classical plant breeding including the impact of structural, comparative and functional genomics on gene discovery, characterization and exploitation. Covers molecular markers, plant transformation, hybrid production, disease resistance, and novel output traits.

291.title: Seminar in History of Genetics
291.description: The development of modern genetic theories beginning with Mendel.

292.title: Seminar in Genomics & Epigenomics
292.description: Topics of current interest in genomics and epigenomics.

296.title: Scientific Professionalism & Integrity
296.description: Review of basic skills required of contemporary scientists. Topics include scientific conduct, manuscript preparation, grant writing, seminar presentations, and time management. Emphasis on responsibilities of scientists to factually and thoughtfully communicate results.
296.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Group study of selected topics in genetics.

212.title: Water Resource Management
212.description: Engineering, institutional, economic, and social basis for managing local and regional water resources. Examples in the context of California's water development and management. Uses of computer modeling to improve water management.
212.prereq_text: ECI 114; ECI 142; or consent of instructor.

298.title: Group Study
298.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

081.title: Learning in Science & Mathematics
081.description: Exploration of how students learn and develop understanding in science and mathematics classrooms. Introduction to case studies and interview techniques and their use in K-6 classrooms to illuminate factors that affect student learning.

181.title: Teaching in Science & Mathematics
181.description: Exploration of effective teaching practices based on examination of how middle school students learn math and science. Selected readings, discussion and field experience in middle school classrooms.
181.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus.

183.title: Teaching High School Mathematics & Science
183.description: Exploration and creation of effective teaching practices based on examination of how high school students learn mathematics and science. Field experience in high school classrooms.
183.prereq_text: Major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus and consent of the instructor.

262.title: Paleobiology Graduate Seminar: Methodological Aspects
262.description: One or more major methods used in the study of fossils: Morphometrics and three-dimensional reconstruction of fossils, phylogenetic methodology, the application of geochemical techniques, and electron microscopy.

290.title: Seminar in Geology
290.description: Presentation and discussion of current topics in geology by visiting lecturers, staff, and students.

390.title: Methods of Teaching & Research
390.description: Introduction to academia at UC Davis. Introduction to graduate-level research, professional development skills, and methods for undergraduate-level teaching. Includes methods in scientific communication (written, oral and poster presentations); literature review and synthesis; professional development; discussions on campus teaching resources, presenting information, managing classroom dynamics, and assessing student’s work.

001Y.title: Elementary German
001Y.description: Introduction to German grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Students who have successfully completed GER 002 or GER 003 in the tenth or higher grade in high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

010.title: German Fairy Tales from the Grimms to Disney
010.description: Introduction to the genre of fairy tale with a focus on the Brothers Grimm and Hans Christian Andersen in their respective political/cultural contexts. Discusses filmic adaptations by Disney, the East German DEFA and Hollywood.

020.title: Intermediate German
020.description: Review of grammatical principles by means of written exercises; expanding of vocabulary through readings of modern texts.
020.prereq_text: GER 003; can be concurrent with GER 006.

103.title: Writing Skills in German
103.description: Practice in different kinds of writing, such as abstracts, correspondence, lecture summaries, analysis of or response to short literary texts.

112.title: Topics in German Literature
112.description: Knowledge of German not required. Investigation of significant themes and issues within their European context.
112.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

090.title: Introduction to Global Disease Biology
090.description: Introduction to the Global Disease Biology major, research and internship opportunities, and potential career paths in human, animal, and plant health. Communication, ethics and the nature of science.
090.prereq_text: Open to GDB majors only, or consent of instructor.

101.title: Epidemiology
101.description: Principles and practice of epidemiology as applied to human, animal, and plant populations and the environment in which these populations co-exist. Quantitative analysis of both infectious and non-infectious disease. Inter-dependence between epidemiological analysis, decision-making and policy formulation will be highlighted.
101.prereq_text: SAS 013; BIS 002A; BIS 002B; BIS 002C; ((STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y) or (STA 100 or PLS 120)).

187.title: Global Disease Biology Seminar
187.description: Seminar leading to development of the research proposal and academic plan for the Global Disease Biology major.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Preparation of undergraduate students in identified graduate school pipeline programs (e.g. McNair scholars) for graduate education. Emphasis on educating and training undergraduates on key skills and competencies needed for the development of a successful graduate school applicant and future graduate scholar. Topics will vary.

001.title: Elementary Greek
001.description: Introduction to the basic grammar and vocabulary of Classical and New Testament Greek. Development of translation skills with emphasis on Greek-English.

100.title: Readings in Greek Prose
100.description: Review of Greek morphology, syntax, and vocabulary. Readings in Greek prose authors, including Xenophon.
100.prereq_text: GRK 003; or equivalent.

102.title: Euripides
102.description: Study of Euripides and his works.

001.title: Elementary Hebrew
001.description: Speaking, listening, comprehension, reading and writing fundamentals of modern Hebrew.

021.title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew I
021.description: Development and refinement of grammar, composition, and language skills required for reading literary texts and conversing about contemporary topics at an advanced level. History of the Hebrew language.
021.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken HEB 100 or HEB 100A.

199.title: Research in Hematology-Oncology
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

298.title: Topics in Hematology
298.description:
Basic concepts of the physiology of the hematopoietic organ, the pathophysiology of hematopoietic disease, and concepts of therapeutics
will be offered for study. The specific topics to be dictated by the interest and background of the students.
298.prereq_text: One year of graduate work and/or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research
299.description:
Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate
degree.

001.title: Elementary Hindi
001.description: Introduction to basic conversation, word structure, and literacy in the Hindi form of Hindi/Urdu using the Devanagari script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu.
001.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken HIN 001.

021.title: Intermediate Hindi/Urdu
021.description: Integrated continuation of HIN 003 and URD 003 with intermediate skills in reading and writing in the Hindi form in the Devanagari script and the Urdu form in the Nastaʿliq script and conversation in Hindi/Urdu.
021.prereq_text: (HIN 003 or URD 003); or consent of instructor.

002Y.title: Introduction to the History of Science & Technology
002Y.description: Introduction to topics and methods of the history of science and technology. Emphasis on understanding the role of science and technology in the modern world through a long-term historical perspective.

004C.title: History of Western Civilization
004C.description: Development of Western Civilization from the 18th century to the present.

007A.title: History of Latin America to 1700
007A.description: Introduction to the history of Spanish and Portuguese America from the late pre-Columbian period through the initial phase and consolidation of a colonial regime (circa 1700).  Topics include conquest, colonialism, racial mixture, gender, and labor systems.

009A.title: History of East Asian Civilization
009A.description: Surveys traditional Chinese civilization and its modern transformation. Emphasis is on thought and religion, political and social life, art and literature. Perspectives on contemporary China are provided.

010B.title: World History, c. 1350-1850
010B.description: Major topics in world history from the 14th century to the beginning of the 19th century. Topics will vary but may include: oceans as systems of human communication and conflict; the global consequences of "industrious revolutions" in Europe and Asia, etc.

017A.title: History of the United States
017A.description: The experience of the American people from the Colonial Era to the Civil War.

017B.title: History of the United States
017B.description: The experience of the American people from the Civil War to the end of the Cold War.
017B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed HIS 017C.

018B.title: Race in the United States Since 1865
018B.description: Introduction to the history of race and racial formation in America since 1865 though a comparative approach that examines the experiences of African Americans, Asian Americans, Native American and Mexican Americans and other Latino/a groups.

102D.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: Modern Europe to 1815
102D.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. Modern Europe to 1815.

102J.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: Latin America Since 1810
102J.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. Latin America since 1810.

102K.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: American History to 1787
102K.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. American History to 1787.

102L.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: United States, 1787-1896
102L.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. United States, 1787-1896.

109.title: Environmental Change, Disease & Public Health
109.description: Analysis of environmental changes from pre-history to the present and their influence on disease distribution, virulence and public health. Focus on critical study of many human-driven environmental changes and the accelerated transformation/spread of pathogens under globalization.
109.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HIS 109B.

146A.title: Europe in the 20th Century
146A.description: Survey of the history of Europe from 1919 to 1939.

164.title: History of Chile
164.description: Emphasis on the history of Chilean political economy from 1930 to the present. Various strategies of development (modernization, Marxism, Neo-Liberalism); the rise of mass politics; the course of foreign relations; and the richness of Chilean literature.

170A.title: Colonial America
170A.description: Colonial society from 1607 to the American Revolution, with emphasis on European expansion, political, social and economic foundations, colonial thought and culture, and imperial rivalry.

172.title: American Environmental History
172.description: American history through connections between people and nature, pre-Columbus to climate change. Native America; conquest; epidemics; extinctions; industrialization; pollution; environmentalism; climate change and global warming; ideas of nature.

174D.title: Selected Themes in 20th-Century American History
174D.description: Interpretive overview of a single topic in the history of the United States in the 20th century with attention to the phases and processes of historical change.

183A.title: The Frontier Experience: Trans-Mississippi West
183A.description: The fur trade, western exploration and transportation, the Oregon Country, the Greater Southwest and the Mexican War, the Mormons, mining discovery, and the West during the Civil War.

196A.title: Medieval India
196A.description: Survey of history of India in the millennium preceding arrival of British in the 18th century, focusing on interaction of the civilizations of Hinduism and Islam and on the changing nature of the state.

201I.title: Sources & General Literature of History: Latin America Since 1810
201I.description: Designed primarily for students preparing for higher degrees in history. Latin America since 1810.

202H.title: Major Issues in Historical Interpretation: United States
202H.description: Fundamental issues and debates in the study of history. United States. Readings, papers, and class reports.

203A.title: Second-Year Research Seminar
203A.description: Prepare for higher degrees in history. Individual research and analysis resulting in substantial research paper of publishable quality. Completion required of all Ph.D. candidates. HIS 203A & HIS 203B must be taken in continuous sequence, ordinarily during second year.

204.title: Historiography
204.description: Major issues in the philosophy and methodology of history.

389.title: Introductory Seminar for Teaching Assistants
389.description: An introduction to the broad comparative and theoretical issues of teaching methods and techniques in history.

195.title: Honors Thesis/Honors Project
195.description: Guided independent study of a selected topic leading to the presentation of an honors thesis/honors project.
195.prereq_text: Open only to students in the Davis Honors Challenge.

200A.title: Horticulture & Agronomy: Principles
200A.description: Core course to introduce students to the principles that are of general importance in horticultural and agronomic research, including agroecology, plant developmental physiology, crop improvement, and biotechnology. Generally taken in the first year of the graduate program.

211.title: Current Topics in Root Biology
211.description: How roots grow and interact with their environment, from embryonic roots to large tree roots. Analysis of recent literature related to the impact of internal controls on root growth and root system development (e.g., developmental signaling, carbohydrate availability, water status), and the impacts of the external environment on root physiology, root system development, and individual root growth (e.g., soil structure, soil microbial, water, nutrients).

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminars presented by invited speakers, students, or faculty on selected topics in horticulture.

012.title: Human Sexuality
012.description: Vocabulary, structure/function of reproductive system; sexual response; pre-natal development; pregnancy and childbirth; development of sexuality; rape and sexual assault; birth control; sexually transmitted diseases; homosexuality; establishing/maintaining intimacy; sexual dysfunctions; communication; enhancing sexual interaction, cultural differences in attitudes towards sexuality.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off campus and on campus, in community and institutional setting. Involves progressively greater (supervised) participation in program delivery or assessment.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; field work experience or at least one course related to fieldwork assignment (e.g. HDE 100A, HDE 100B, HDE 140 or HDE 140L).

100A.title: Infancy & Early Childhood
100A.description: Biological, social, and cultural influences in the psychological growth and development of children, prenatal through age six. Two observations of preschool children required.
100A.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (BIS 002A or BIS 010 or BIS 001A or BIS 010V) or MCB 010 or NPB 010 or NPB 012 or MIC 010.

100C.title: Adulthood & Aging
100C.description: Development during early, middle, and late adulthood; biological, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of adult development. Emphasis on normative patterns of development which characterize "successful aging."

104.title: Children in Families, Schools, Communities
104.description: Children's social contexts (e.g., family, peers, school, neighborhood, community culture), development, and environmental challenges (e.g., poverty, maltreatment) from birth through adolescence.
104.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V.

110V.title: Families in Communities
110V.description: Family members' roles, interactions, and development, and how families are impacted by the larger community and society in which they live. Relevant topics/issues include gender, race/ethnicity, parenting, marriage, grandparents, divorce, acculturation, migration, and policies relevant to family well-being.
110V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HDE 110.
110V.prereq_text: CRD 001 or CRD 002 or PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or SOC 002 or SOC 002V.

111.title: Family Stress & Resilience
111.description: Theories and research associated with stressors affecting family functioning throughout the lifespan. Normative transitions and non-normative stressors, family services and family based policies and interventions.

120.title: Research Methods in Human Development
120.description: Scientific process, research designs, and experimental controls; APA manuscript style and scientific writing; statistical analysis and interpretation of results. Laboratory exercises to collect data, analyze and interpret results, and write scientific papers.
120.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 or EDU 114 or PSC 041 or PSC 041V or (SOC 046A,  SOC 046B).

130.title: Developmental Psychopathology
130.description: Foundational principles and current issues in developmental psychopathology, the study of mental health problems and disorders that originate in childhood and adolescence (e.g., disruptive behavior, mood and anxiety disorders).
130.prereq_text: (HDE 100A,  HDE 100B or HDE 100BV) or (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V); consent of instructor.

131V.title: Thriving Across the Lifespan
131V.description: Positive developmental trajectories from womb to tomb. Developmental process of thriving (e.g., happiness, life satisfaction, wisdom) and the factors that support thriving.
131V.prereq_text: HDE 100A  or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

133.title: Stress, Adversity & Resilience
133.description: Short and long term biobehavioral responses to stress and adversity. The biological, psychological, social, and cultural factors of resilience. Interventions promoting resilience. Developmental perspective of stress and resilience across the lifespan.
133.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

137.title: Contextual Determinants of Health
137.description: Community, cultural, political, and physical environment influences on health and well-being. Developmental approach. Unique contextual determinants of health from womb to tomb.
137.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

140.title: Field Study in Early Childhood
140.description: Application of theories of learning and development to interaction with infants, toddlers, and preschoolers at Early Childhood Laboratory School. Applied skills in communication, guidance, and curriculum.

141.title: Field Study With Children & Adolescents
141.description: Study of children's affective, cognitive and social development within the context of family/school environments, hospitals and foster group homes.
141.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV; and consent of instructor.

190C.title: Introductory Research Conference
190C.description: Instructors lead discussions with undergraduate students who involve themselves in a research project. Research papers are reviewed and aspects of project proposals developed out of class are presented and evaluated.
190C.prereq_text: Involvement in ongoing research; consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Supervised internship off and on campus, in community, and institutional
settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

200A.title: Early Development
200A.description: Theory and research on the biological, social, cognitive, and cultural aspects of development from conception to the age of five years.
200A.prereq_text: Graduate standing; basic biology or physiology; one upper division course in psychology or a related field; one upper division or graduate course in developmental psychology (can be concurrent).

240.title: Peer Relationships during Adolescence
240.description: Examines the role of peer relationships in adolescent development including forms and functions at the individual, dyadic and group levels. Ethnicity and cross cultural research will be discussed. Emphasis on methodology, including surveys, peer nominations/sociometrics, experimental, and observational designs.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Supervising instructors lead research discussions with their graduate students. Research papers are reviewed and project proposals are presented and evaluated.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off campus, in community or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor.
292.prereq_text: Consent of faculty (internship sponsor) and satisfactory completion of placement relevant course work, for example: EDU 213, EDU 216; HDE 222, HDE 242; LAW 272, LAW 273.

192.title: Internship in Human Physiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in physiology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed reading, discussion and/or laboratory experience on selected topics.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Senior standing in biology, chemistry, physics, psychology, or engineering.

298.title: Group Study
298.description:
For graduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth.
Lectures and conferences may be involved.

001.title: Human Wrongs/Human Rights
001.description: Introduction to Human Rights and the problems they seek to address. Using key episodes of inhumanity like slavery, genocide, and racism. Examines how international movements for social justice led to the emergence of the international Human Rights system.

130.title: Special Topics in Human Rights
130.description: Thematic study of human rights. Topics may include contemporary or historical issues in the promotion, protection, and violation of human rights; human rights and the arts, religion, literature are possible topical areas.

134.title: Human Rights
134.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the origins, evolution, denial and protection of Human Rights.
134.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have completed RST 090.

002A.title: Global Humanities Forum
002A.description: Introduction to humanities topics and methodologies; analysis of major figures, works, and genres in world arts and literatures, with emphasis on relationships between history, society, and culture.

002B.title: American Humanities Forum
002B.description: Introduction to humanities topics and methodologies; analysis of major figures, works, and genres in American arts and literatures, with emphasis on relationships between history, society, and culture.

015.title: Language & Identity
015.description: Introduction to topics related to the construction of identity through language use, including geographical and social factors affecting language groups. Language ideology affecting linguistic groups, including bilinguals and non-native speakers of English.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.

299.title: Individual Research
299.description: Individual research in the humanities resulting in a formal written research report.

092.title: Hydrologic Science Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in Hydrologic Science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division student.

144.title: Groundwater Hydrology
144.description: Global role of groundwater resources in society; groundwater in the hydrologic cycle; geology of groundwater; global, US, and California geography of groundwater; physical measures of groundwater occurrence and flow; water balance; modeling groundwater flow; principles of well construction; aquifer tests; groundwater quality; contaminant transport and monitoring; groundwater law, water quality regulations, and sustainable management.
144.prereq_text: MAT 012 (can be concurrent) or MAT 019A (can be concurrent) or MAT 021A (can be concurrent) or MAT 016B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

201A.title: Hydrologic Sciences Core Survey
201A.description: Considers the primary sub-disciplines while reviewing the fundamental scientific concepts/processes of the hydrologic sciences research community, and includes a basic writing component.

241.title: Precision Irrigation Systems & Management
241.description: Advanced irrigation science and engineering for agricultural, horticultural, engineering, and hydrology graduate students. Precision irrigation techniques for application of water to meet specific requirements of individual plants or management units and maximum economic benefits of crop production.

242.title: Hydrology & Sustainability of Irrigated Lands
242.description: Impact of irrigated agricultural on groundwater depletion, surface water and groundwater quality, soil salinization, downstream ecosystems, and seawater intrusion. Exploration of efficient resource use, and policies adopted in California to enhance sustainability of irrigated crop production.
242.prereq_text: ABT 110 or ESM 110 or HYD 110 or EBS 145.

245.title: Climate Change Science & Impacts
245.description: Overview of climate change science with a focus on climate change communication. Impacts of climate change on water, agriculture, energy, health, infrastructure, ecosystem services, tribal and indigenous communities. Climate justice, political, societal, and economic dimensions of these issues.

290.title: Seminar in Hydrologic Science
290.description: Seminars and critical review of problems, issues, and research in hydrologic sciences. Oral presentations of research. Topics vary.
290.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing and background in Hydrologic Science.

201.title: Introductory Immunology
201.description: Comprehensive introduction to the principles of immunology.

201L.title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory Rotations
201L.description: Laboratory assignment in two research laboratories. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design. Student writes a project outline and gives oral presentation.

291.title: Introduction to Critical Analysis of Immunology Research Literature
291.description: Introduction to critical reading of primary research papers in Immunology. Guided discussions on recent primary research papers provided to students before each class.
291.prereq_text: IMM 201 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

296.title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
296.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty research topics in Immunology
296.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

141.title: Infectious Diseases of Humans
141.description: Integrates information on biological and molecular nature of the causative organism, modern diagnostics, treatment and prevention strategies, and the role of infectious diseases in contemporary society and throughout human history.
141.prereq_text: Introductory knowledge in biology and chemistry recommended.

192.title: Research Internship in Internal Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in the division of Infectious Diseases. Undergraduates will have an opportunity to acquire research experience in clinical settings.

199.title: Infectious Diseases Research
199.description: Discrete problem requiring reading and actual manual effort in solution will be assigned to each student. Progress and results will be reviewed at intervals with instructor and via seminar presentation.
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; chemistry through organic chemistry (in addition, physical and biochemistry preferred), biology through basic bacteriology (in addition, microbiology and immunology preferred).

299.title: Research in Infectious Diseases
299.description:
Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate
degree.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship in internal medicine and related fields.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Directed group study in medicine and related fields.
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Undergraduate Research in Medicine: Molecular & Cell Biology
099.description: Undergraduate research in medicine, focusing on molecular & cellular biology.

192.title: Internship in Internal Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in internal medicine and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194.title: Practicum in Community Health Clinics
194.description: The undergraduate student, through active participation in the medical aspects of community health clinics, gains knowledge of the organization, administration, and problem-solving capabilities of these primary care facilities.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study in medicine and related fields.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

214.title: Topics in Medical Ethics
214.description: The complex moral, legal and ethical dilemmas that patients, families, and health care providers face in today's clinics.

458Y.title: Climate Change: Implications for Clinical Practice & Population Health
458Y.description: Climate change and its associated environmental and social disruptions are and will increasingly lead to clinical and population health consequences for which clinicians, and health systems, will need to be prepared to best care for their patients and the populations they serve. Draws from the Global Consortium on Climate and Health Education’s set of Core Climate and Health Competencies for Health Professionals and places an emphasis on climate change and clinical practice.

466.title: Medical Spanish for Providers
466.description: Provides ample experience in Spanish patient interviews, supervision of interview styles and Spanish-language skills, discussion of common diagnoses, procedural consent, management/treatment plans, and patient education in Spanish to empower medical students to practice medicine with the nationally growing monolingual Spanish-speaking patient population. Curriculum adapted with permission from the Medical Spanish Taskforce.

469.title: Acting Internship in Medicine Intensive Care Unit (MICU)
469.description: At UCDMC, student functions as acting intern on MICU service under direction of medical resident and staff. Responsibility for patients admitted to MICU.

010.title: Introduction to International Agricultural Development
010.description: Theories, practices and institutions relating to agricultural development; the interaction of changing social, cultural and economic organization through successive stages of economic development; impact of new agricultural technology on underdeveloped regions.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

190.title: Proseminar in International Agricultural Development
190.description: Presentation and discussion of current topics in international agricultural development by visiting lecturers, staff and students.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings. May be taught abroad.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200N.title: Philosophy & Practice of Agricultural Development
200N.description: Introduces key elements of philosophy and practice of agricultural development in less developed countries; major paradigms of development; historical context within which these paradigms operate; various development techniques and initiatives emerging from agricultural production to institutional capacity building and management.
200N.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former IAD 202.

290.title: Seminar in International Agricultural Development
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of advanced topics and issues in international agricultural development.

291.title: Topics in International Agricultural Development
291.description: Selected topics dealing with current issues in agricultural development in lesser developed nations. Variable content.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off or on campus, in community, business or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor and Humphrey Coordinator.
292.prereq_text: Participation in H. Humphrey Fellow Program or consent of instructor.

192.title: International Relations Internship
192.description: Work experience in international relations, with term paper summarizing the practical experience of the student.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

001.title: Elementary Italian
001.description: Introduction to Italian grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001.credit_limit_text: Students who have successfully completed ITA 002 or ITA 003 in the 10th or higher grade in high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed; not open for credit to students who have taken ITA 001A or ITA 001S.

021.title: Intermediate Italian
021.description: Continued development of grammatical structures and vocabulary. Emphasis on reading and writing in Italian.
021.prereq_text: ITA 003 or ITA 003S or ITA 003Y or ITA 032 or ITA 032Y.

105.title: Introduction to Italian Literature
105.description: Introduction to the study of the principal authors, works, and movements of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Early Modern periods in Italy.
105.prereq_text: ITA 009 or ITA 009S or ITA 023 or ITA 023S; or consent of instructor.

150.title: Studies in Italian Cinema
150.description: Introduction to Italian cinema through its genres. Focus on cinema as a reflection or a comment on modern Italian history. Film as an artistic medium and as a form of mass communication.

001.title: Elementary Japanese
001.description:
Introduction to spoken and written Japanese in cultural contexts, with
emphasis on communication.

004.title: Intermediate Japanese
004.description: Intermediate-level training in spoken and written Japanese in cultural context, based on language skills developed in JPN 003.
004.prereq_text: JPN 003 C- or better; or the equivalent language proficiency.

025.title: Japanese Language & Culture (in English)
025.description: Classification and communication of experience in Japanese culture; principles of language use in Japanese society. Speech levels and honorific language, language and gender, minority languages, literacy. Role of Japanese in artificial intelligence and computer science.
025.prereq_text: JPN 001 or LIN 001 or ANT 004 recommended.

101.title: Japanese Literature in Translation: The Early Period
101.description: Study of early Japanese literature from the Nara to the end of the Heian period through a broad survey of the major literary genres such as lyric poetry, court diaries, prose narratives, poem-tales, and classical Chinese writings.

111.title: Modern Japanese: Reading & Discussion
111.description: Readings in modern Japanese short stories, newspaper articles, and essays; conversation practice based on these readings.
111.prereq_text: JPN 006 C- or better; or the equivalent language proficiency.

121.title: Advanced Japanese I
121.description: First of three courses in a series of fourth-year Advanced Japanese which focuses on the levels of formality or politeness in conversation as well as socio-cultural aspects and topics in Japanese society.
121.prereq_text: JPN 113 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

136.title: Readings in Japanese Newspapers
136.description: Fourth-year level reading of newspaper articles and other journalism in Japanese on a wide variety of subjects.
136.prereq_text: JPN 113; or equivalent language proficiency, or consent of instructor.

153.title: Love, Sexuality & the Family in Modern Japanese Literature
153.description: Modern Japanese literature from the late-19th century to the present with a focus on love and sexuality in various forms, particularly as understood through the evolving institution of the Japanese family. Lectures, readings and discussions in English.

155.title: Introduction to Japanese Folklore
155.description: Focus on narrative genres of myth, legend, and folktale, with additional attention paid to festivals, folk art, belief systems, and the development of folklore studies (minzokugaku) as an academic discipline. Examination of the relationship of folklore to ethnic and national identity.

160.title: The Culture of Japanese Food
160.description: Study of Japanese food and the culture of eating and drinking in Japan. Attention to symbolism, historical development, aesthetics, identity and global contexts. Materials examined include critical sources as well as literary texts, art, and films.

192.title: Japanese Internship
192.description: Work experience in Japanese language, with analytical term paper on a topic approved by instructor.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Japanese
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the Program's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Department Chairperson.

001.title: Introduction to Environmental Design
001.description: Introduction to the role of design professionals in contributing to the built environment at a range of scales. Introduction to basic methods used by design professionals to evaluate, design, plan, and manage landscapes and the built environment.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed LDA 001.

021.title: Landscape & Environmental Design Representation I
021.description: Introduction to landscape and environmental design representation techniques. Fundamentals of orthographic drafting, freehand drawing, photography, and basic digital representation.
021.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 021.
021.prereq_text: LED 001 C- or better (can be concurrent) or LDA 001 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

119.title: Landscape & Environmental Design Representation II
119.description: Methods to explore and communicate environmental design intentions through digital media.
119.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 023.
119.prereq_text: LED 021 or LDA 021; or consent of instructor.

140.title: Green Building, Design, & Materials
140.description: Introduction to performance-based foundations of sustainable and regenerative design. Emphasizes engagement with processes, materials, work practices and technologies at a range of site and building scales, using real-world case studies and design projects.
140.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 140.
140.prereq_text: (LED 050 or LDA 050); (LED 070 or LDA 070); or consent of instructor.

150.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
150.description: Basic concepts, principles, and methods of GIS are presented. Data structures, database design, GIS data creation, GPS, and spatial analysis. May be taught abroad.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open to credit for students who have completed ABT 180, PLS 180, ABT 181N.

160.title: Design & Build Studio
160.description: Introduction to the spatial design and construction of small-scale projects. Hands-on approach to learning and understanding materials (including wood, concrete, and stone) and methods in landscape construction, and the application of technical skills (including detailing, cost estimation, and specifications).
160.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 160.
160.prereq_text: LED 070 or LDA 070; or consent of instructor.

161.title: Professional Practice & Construction Documents
161.description: Legal and professional aspects of landscape architecture, including the development of construction documents (drawings and specifications), proposal writing, fee calculations, project management, cost estimation, and insurance.
161.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 161.
161.prereq_text: LED 160 or LDA 160; or consent of instructor.

182.title: Advanced Landscape Architecture Studio I
182.description: Landscape architecture studio featuring advanced studies and applications of creative work, design, technology and/or theory. One day-long field trip required.
182.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 182.
182.prereq_text: LED 171 or LDA 171; or consent of instructor.

001.title: Elementary Latin
001.description: Introduction to basic grammar and vocabulary and development of translation skills with emphasis on Latin to English.
001.credit_limit_text: Students who have successfully completed LAT 002 or LAT 003 in the 10th grade or higher grade in high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

100.title: Readings in Latin Prose
100.description: Review of Latin morphology, grammar, and vocabulary. Readings in prose authors, including Julius Caesar.
100.prereq_text: LAT 003; or equivalent.

135.title: Themes in Latin Literature
135.description: Readings in Latin that trace a theme across times, genres, and authors.
135.prereq_text: LAT 100 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

001.title: Introduction to Linguistics
001.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.

001Y.title: Introduction to Linguistics
001Y.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Students may not take both LIN 001 and LIN 001Y for credit.

002.title: Language, the Mind, & Computers
002.description: Analysis of human language and language processing by humans and machines. How language is represented and processed in the human mind, how computers process language, and similarities and differences between human and computer processing of language. Human-media interaction for language and society.

103A.title: Linguistic Analysis I: Phonetics, Phonology, Morphology
103A.description: Introduction to fundamental methods and concepts used in linguistic analysis, focusing on phonetic, phonological, and morphological phenomena. Emphasizes development of analytical skills and appreciation of structural regularities and differences among languages.
103A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 139.

103B.title: Linguistic Analysis II: Morphology, Syntax, Semantics
103B.description: Introduction to fundamental methods and concepts used in linguistic analysis, focusing on morphological, syntactic, and semantic phenomena. Emphasizes development of analytical skills and appreciation of structural regularities and differences among languages.
103B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 140.

105.title: Topics in Language & Linguistics
105.description: Detailed examination of a major contemporary linguistic theory, a major contemporary issue or related set of issues in linguistics, or the structure of a particular language or language family.

106.title: English Grammar
106.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
106.prereq_text: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or ENG 003 or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or consent of instructor.

141.title: Semantics
141.description: Linguistic study of meanings of words and phrases, meanings expressed by lexical items and compositional structures. Truth-conditional models of semantics, evaluated in context and against social conventions.

173.title: Language Development
173.description: Introduction to research and theoretical perspectives on major domains of language development (infant speech perception and production, pragmatics, phonology, vocabulary, grammar, and extended discourse).

177.title: Computational Linguistics
177.description: Understanding the nature of language through computer modeling of linguistic abilities.  Relationships between human cognition and computer representations of cognitive processing.
177.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 007.
177.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; LIN 001 or LIN 001Y recommended.

197T.title: Tutoring in Linguistics
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing and consent of department chairperson.

200A.title: Foundations of Linguistics I
200A.description: Survey of fundamental issues raised by pre-generative linguistics in the 20th century, with emphasis on issues crucial to applications of linguistics.
200A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 203A.

205A.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
205A.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

205C.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
205C.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

297T.title: English as a Second Language Teaching/Tutoring
297T.description: Teaching classes for ESL graduate students. Aiding the ESL undergraduate composition classes; tutoring foreign graduate student Teaching Assistants in pronunciation. Does not fulfill requirement toward the M.A. degree.
297T.prereq_text: LIN 300 or LIN 301 or LIN 302 (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.

001.title: Thriving at UC Davis
001.description: Adjusting to college life, balancing multiple priorities, and discovering where strengths and interests align. Time management skills, study habits, and communication. Tools to enable success in college and the professional world.

011A.title: Elementary Financial Accounting
011A.description: Basic concepts of accounting; interpreting and using financial statements; understanding accounting principles.

011AY.title: Elementary Financial Accounting
011AY.description: Basic concepts of accounting; interpreting and using financial statements; understanding accounting principles.

011B.title: Elementary Managerial Accounting
011B.description: Theory of product costing. Analyzing the role and impact of accounting information on decision making; planning and performance evaluation.

012Y.title: Navigating Life’s Financial Decisions
012Y.description: Survey of major life financial decisions (e.g., career choice, consumption v. saving, investments, mortgages, insurance) and how decision-making biases (e.g., overconfidence, present bias, limited attention) can lead to suboptimal choice. Draws on research from economics, psychology, and sociology.

092.title: Internship in Business
092.description: Supervised work experience in business. Units for students in lower division standing.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

101.title: Sources & Uses of Accounting Information
101.description: Develops an understanding of the supply and demand of accounting information. Topics include the generation and processing of accounting information, the examination of accounting information by auditors, and the use of accounting information by capital markets and tax authorities.
101.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better; must have C- or better in all prerequisite courses.

103.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
103.description: Begin to develop expertise in the accounting for assets and introduce analysis of financial statements.
103.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better

105.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
105.description: Continue to develop expertise in the preparation of financial statements by studying the accounting for liabilities and stockholders’ equity. Examines the accounting for contracts that can have significant effects on firms’ financial statements.

120.title: Introduction to Information Systems
120.description: Develop an analytical framework to manage and monitor business systems concerned with operational, human, and organizational interactions. Introduction to computer hardware, systems software, and fundamental principles of database management systems. Concepts of data visualization.

140.title: Introduction to Marketing & Data Analytics
140.description: Strategic analysis and solutions to marketing decision problems. Enduring concepts and emerging issues of marketing; analytics tools to address modern marketing challenges.
140.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better).

150.title: Introduction to Management
150.description: Management of firms in a variety of industries, including high technology industries such as software development and biotechnology. 197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

200.title: Preparing for Graduate Student Success
200.description: Introduction to the soft-skills and campus resources needed to succeed in graduate school. Emphasis on the student-mentor relationship and the process of selecting a research mentor.

260.title: Advanced Thermodynamics of Solids
260.description: Thermodynamic principles, formalism and their application to solid materials. Statistical mechanics and the relations between microscopic and macroscopic properties. Prediction of phase diagrams and phase stability, particularly for solids.

262.title: Advanced Topics in Structure of Materials
262.description: Electronic structure and crystal structure of engineering materials on the atomic scale with a detailed discussion of crystallography. Types of bonding, distinction between band structures of metals, semiconductors, and insulators. Symmetry elements, point and space groups, and common crystal structures.
262.prereq_text: EMS 162; EMS 174 recommended; graduate standing in Engineering or consent of instructor.

264.title: Transport Phenomena in Materials Processes
264.description: Thermodynamic driving forces and atomic-scale mechanisms underlying diffusive mass transport and interface motion in materials.  Nucleation, growth and coarsening dynamics of phase transformations.
264.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who previously completed former course EMS 240.

290.title: Materials Science & Engineering Seminar
290.description: Selected topics of current interest in Materials Science & Engineering. Subjects covered vary from year to year and are announced at the beginning of each quarter.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

292.title: Materials Science & Engineering Internship
292.description: Work or lab experience in industry or off-campus lab focusing on Materials Science & Engineering applications at the graduate level.
292.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate level standing.

260.title: Nutrition During Pregnancy
260.description: Overview of the anatomical, physiological and biochemical changes that occur during pregnancy and early development. Discussion and evaluation of nutritional/lifestyle factors associated with pregnancy outcomes and nutrition programs/interventions for pregnant women.
260.prereq_text: Acceptance into Master of Advanced Studies in Maternal & Child Nutrition or Graduate Group in Nutritional Biology; other students by consent of instructor.

262.title: Child & Adolescent Nutrition
262.description: Relationships among nutrition, growth, and development during childhood and adolescence. Nutritional assessment for normal and high risk groups; psychological, social, and economic factors contributing to nutritional status. Nutritional needs and interventions for special groups, including obese children/adolescents, athletes, and eating disordered.

012.title: Precalculus
012.description: Topics selected for their use in calculus, including functions and their graphs, slope, zeroes of polynomials, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions, sketching surfaces and solids.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed any of MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017A, MAT 017B, MAT 017C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C with a C- or better.
012.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry; obtaining required score on the Precalculus Diagnostic Examination also known as the Math Readiness Assessment.

017A.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017A.description: Introduction to differential calculus via applications in biology and medicine. Limits, derivatives of polynomials, trigonometric, and exponential functions, graphing, applications of the derivative to biology and medicine.
017A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016A.
017A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and analytical geometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

017B.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017B.description: Introduction to integral calculus and elementary differential equations via applications to biology and medicine. Fundamental theorem of calculus, techniques of integration including integral tables and numerical methods, improper integrals, elementary first order differential equations, applications in biology and medicine.
017B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016C, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit for students who have completed MAT 016B.
017B.prereq_text: MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better.

017C.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017C.description: Matrix algebra, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, systems of differential equations, and applications to biology and medicine.
017C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016C.

019A.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019A.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities.
019A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016A, 016B, 016C, MAT 017B, MAT 017C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017A.
019A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

019B.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019B.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities.
019B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, 016C, MAT 017C, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017B.
019B.prereq_text: MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better.

019C.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019C.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data-driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities. Multivariable calculus, differential equations, partial derivatives.
019C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016C or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017C.
019C.prereq_text: MAT 019B C- or better or MAT 017B C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better.

021A.title: Calculus
021A.description: Functions, limits, continuity. Slope and derivative. Differentiation of algebraic and transcendental functions. Applications to motion, natural growth, graphing, extrema of a function. Differentials. L'Hopital's rule.
021A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017B, or MAT 017C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016A or MAT 017A.
021A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and analytical geometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

021B.title: Calculus
021B.description: Continuation of MAT 021A. Definition of definite integral, fundamental theorem of calculus, techniques of integration. Application to area, volume, arc length, average of a function, improper integral, surface of revolution.
021B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017B, or MAT 017C.
021B.prereq_text: (MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better) or MAT 017A B or better or MAT 019A B or better.

021C.title: Calculus
021C.description: Continuation of MAT 021B. Sequences, series, tests for convergence, Taylor expansions. Vector algebra, vector calculus, scalar and vector fields. Partial derivatives, total differentials. Applications to maximum and minimum problems in two or more variables. Applications to physical systems.
021C.prereq_text: MAT 016C C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 017B B or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better.

021D.title: Vector Analysis
021D.description: Continuation of MAT 021C. Definite integrals over plane and solid regions in various coordinate systems. Line and surface integrals. Green's theorem, Stoke's theorem, divergence theorem.
021D.prereq_text: (MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better) or MAT 017C B or better.

022A.title: Linear Algebra
022A.description: Matrices and linear transformations, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization, factorization.
022A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 067.
022A.prereq_text: MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better.

022B.title: Differential Equations
022B.prereq_text: (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or BIS 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better).

108.title: Introduction to Abstract Mathematics
108.description: Rigorous treatment of mathematical concepts with emphasis on developing the ability to understand abstract mathematical ideas, to read and write mathematical concepts, and to prove theorems. Designed to serve as preparation for the more rigorous upper division courses.

115A.title: Number Theory
115A.description: Divisibility and related topics, diophantine equations, selected topics from the theory of prime numbers. Designed to serve as preparation for the more rigorous upper division courses.

118A.title: Partial Differential Equations: Elementary Methods
118A.description: Derivation of partial differential equations; separation of variables; equilibrium solutions and Laplace's equation; Fourier series; method of characteristics for the one dimensional wave equation.  Solution of nonhomogeneous equations.
118A.prereq_text: MAT 021D; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

119A.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
119A.description: Scalar and planar autonomous systems; nonlinear systems and linearization; existence and uniqueness of solutions; matrix solution of linear systems; phase plane analysis; stability analysis; bifurcation theory; Liapunov's method; limit cycles; Poincare Bendixon theory.
119A.prereq_text: MAT 021D; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

127A.title: Real Analysis
127A.description: Real numbers, sequences, series, and continuous functions.
127A.prereq_text: (MAT 021C or MAT 021CH); (MAT 067 or MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A); (MAT 108 or MAT 108V).

127B.title: Real Analysis
127B.description: Derivatives, integrals, sequences of functions, and power series.

128A.title: Numerical Analysis
128A.description: Error analysis, approximation, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration.
128A.prereq_text: MAT 021C; (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ENG 006); programming in languages such as MATLAB or Python will be used.

128C.title: Numerical Analysis in Differential Equations
