128C.description: Difference equations, operators, numerical solutions of ordinary and partial differential equations.
128C.prereq_text: (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ENG 006); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B); methods of programming in languages such as MATLAB or Python for numerical analysis will be used.

135A.title: Probability
135A.description: Probability space; discrete probability, combinatorial analysis; independence, conditional probability; random variables, discrete and continuous distributions, probability mass function, joint and marginal density functions; expectation, moments, variance, Chebyshev inequality; sums of random variables, random walk, large number law, central limit theorem.
135A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former MAT 131.

145.title: Combinatorics
145.description: Combinatorial methods using basic graph theory, counting methods, generating functions, and recurrence relations. Designed to serve as preparation for the more rigorous upper division courses.

147.title: Topology
147.description: Basic notions of point-set and combinatorial topology.

150A.title: Modern Algebra
150A.description: Basic concepts of groups, symmetries of the plane. Emphasis on the techniques used in the proof of the ideas (Lemmas, Theorems, etc.) developing these concepts. Precise thinking, proof writing, and the ability to deal with abstraction.
150A.prereq_text: MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, (MAT 108 or MAT 108V)).

165.title: Mathematics & Computers
165.description: Introduction to computational mathematics, symbolic computation, and computer generated/verified proofs in algebra, analysis and geometry. Investigation of rigorous new mathematics developed in conjunction with modern computational questions and the role that computers play in mathematical conjecture and experimentation.
165.prereq_text: (MAT 127A or MAT 108 or MAT 108V or MAT 114 or MAT 115A or MAT 145); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A).

167.title: Applied Linear Algebra
167.description: Applications of linear algebra; LU and QR matrix factorizations, eigenvalue and singular value matrix decompositions.
167.prereq_text: MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A or MAT 067.

168.title: Optimization
168.description: Linear programming, simplex method. Basic properties of unconstrained nonlinear problems, descent methods, conjugate direction method. Constrained minimization. Programming language required.
168.prereq_text: MAT 021C; (((MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A), (MAT 108 or MAT 108V)) or MAT 067).

180.title: Special Topics
180.description: Special topics from various fields of modern, pure, and applied mathematics.  Some recent topics include Knot Theory, General Relativity, and Fuzzy Sets.
180.prereq_text: (MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, MAT 108)), MAT 127A.

185A.title: Complex Analysis
185A.description: Complex number system, analyticity and the Cauchy-Riemann equations, elementary functions, complex integration, power and Laurent series expansions, residue theory.
185A.prereq_text: (MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, MAT 108)), MAT 127B.

192.title: Internship in Applied Mathematics
192.description: Supervised work experience in applied mathematics. Final report.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

194.title: Undergraduate Thesis
194.description: Independent research under supervision of a faculty member. Student will submit written report in thesis form.

197TC.title: Tutoring Mathematics in the Community
197TC.description: Special projects in mathematical education developing techniques for mathematics instruction and tutoring on an individual or small group basis.

201A.title: Analysis
201A.description: Metric and normed spaces. Continuous functions. Topological, Hilbert, and Banach spaces. Fourier series. Spectrum of bounded and compact linear operators. Linear differential operators and Green's functions. Distributions. Fourier transform. Measure theory. Lp and Sobolev spaces. Differential calculus and variational methods.
201A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics, or consent of instructor.

207A.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
207A.description: Ordinary differential equations and dynamical systems. Variational principles. Eigenfunctions, integral equations and Green's functions. Complex analysis and contour integration. Laplace's equation. Diffusion equations. Wave phenomena. Dimensional analysis and scaling. Asymptotic expansions and perturbation theory. Stochastic processes and Brownian motion.
207A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

215A.title: Topology
215A.description: Fundamental group and covering space theory. Homology and cohomology. Manifolds and duality. CW complexes. Fixed point theorems.
215A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

228A.title: Numerical Solution of Differential Equations
228A.description: Numerical solutions of initial-value, eigenvalue and boundary-value problems for ordinary differential equations. Numerical solution of parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations.

235A.title: Probability Theory
235A.description: Measure-theoretic foundations, abstract integration, independence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions, central limit theorems. Weak convergence in metric spaces, Brownian motion, invariance principle. Conditional expectation. Topics selected from: martingales, Markov chains, ergodic theory.
235A.prereq_text: MAT 125B; (MAT 135A or STA 131A); or consent of instructor.

236A.title: Stochastic Dynamics & Applications
236A.description: Stochastic processes, Brownian motion, Stochastic integration, martingales, stochastic differential equations. Diffusions, connections with partial differential equations, mathematical finance.
236A.prereq_text: MAT 201C or (MAT 235B or STA 235B); MAT 235A, MAT 235B, MAT 235C/STA 235A, STA 235B, STA 235C recommended.

245.title: Enumerative Combinatorics
245.description: Introduction to modern combinatorics and its applications. Emphasis on enumerative aspects of combinatorial theory.
245.prereq_text: MAT 145; MAT 150; or the equivalent, or consent of instructor.

250C.title: Algebra
250C.description: Group and rings. Sylow theorems, abelian groups, Jordan-Holder theorem. Rings, unique factorization. Algebras, and modules. Fields and vector spaces over fields. Field extensions. Commutative rings. Representation theory and its applications.
250C.prereq_text: Graduate standing in mathematics or consent of instructor.

258A.title: Numerical Optimization
258A.description: Numerical methods for infinite dimensional optimization problems.  Newton and Quasi-Newton methods, linear and sequential quadratic programming, barrier methods; large-scale optimization; theory of approximations; infinite and semi-infinite programming; applications to optimal control, stochastic optimization and distributed systems.

280.title: Topics in Pure & Applied Mathematics
280.description: Special topics in various fields of pure and applied mathematics. Topics selected based on the mutual interests of students and faculty.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Advanced study in various fields of mathematics, including analysis, applied mathematics, discrete mathematics, geometry, mathematical biology, mathematical physics, optimization, partial differential equations, probability, and topology.

390.title: Teaching Assistantship Training
390.description: Experience in methods of assisting and teaching of mathematics at the university level. Includes discussion of lecturing techniques, running discussion sessions, holding office hours, preparing and grading of examinations, student-teacher interaction, and related topics. Required of departmental teaching assistants.
390.prereq_text: Graduate standing in the Department of Mathematics.

399.title: Individual Study
399.description: Individual study of some aspect of mathematics education or a focused work on a curriculum design project under supervision of a faculty member in mathematics.

210A.title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics & Heat Transfer
210A.description: Development of differential equations governing continuity, momentum and energy transfer. Solutions in laminar flow for exact cases, low and high Reynolds numbers and lubrication theory. Dynamics of inviscid flow.

230.title: Introduction to Neural-Machine-Interfaces & Assisted Human Movement
230.description: Concepts necessary to communicate across disciplines and apply engineering and neuroscientific principals in understanding, quantifying, and restoring impaired human movement.

265.title: Aeroacoustics
265.description: Introduction to acoustics, Fourier transform and sound pressure level, Green’s function, Lighthill’s acoustic analogy and jet noise, tailored Green’s function and acoustic scattering, Ffowcs Williams and Hawkings equation and rotorcraft noise, turbulence for aeroacoustics and leading-edge noise, trailing-edge noise and wind turbine noise, duct acoustics and aircraft engine noise.

278.title: Estimation Theory & Application
278.description: Estimation of the internal states of dynamic systems, fault diagnosis and state-feedback control. Stochastic system model, algorithm design and data analysis. Three basic elements of estimation: model, algorithm and data; with examples taken from applications in energy/mechanical systems.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference
290C.description: Individual and/or group conference on problems, progress, and techniques in mechanical and aeronautical engineering research.

297.title: SEMINAR
297.description: Current topics in engineering including developments in mechanical and aeronautical engineering with presentations by students, faculty, and visitors.

001.title: Mechanical Engineering
001.description: Description of the field of mechanical engineering with examples taken from industrial applications, discussions of the practice with respect to engineering principles, ethics, and responsibilities.

106.title: Thermo-Fluid Dynamics
106.description: Inviscid incompressible flow, compressible flow, ideal gas mixtures, psychrometrics, reacting mixtures and combustion.
106.prereq_text: ENG 103 C- or better; ENG 105 C- or better.

108.title: Measurement Systems
108.description: Experiments to illustrate principles of mechanical systems. Signal analysis; demonstration of basic sensors for mechanical systems; experimental project design; experiments involving voltage measurement; strain gauges, dynamic systems of 1st order.
108.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken BIM 111; 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken EBS 165; 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have completed EME 107B (former version of EME 108).
108.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better; ENG 104 recommended.

109.title: Experimental Methods for Thermal Fluids
109.description: Experiments illustrating principles of thermal-fluid systems and related measurement devices. Statistical design of experiments and uncertainty analysis of data; thermodynamic cycles, combustion, compressible and incompressible flows.
109.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECH 155A; 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECH 155B; 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECI 141L; 1 unit of credit for students who have already completed EME 107A (former version of EME 109).

115.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis & Methods
115.description: Number representation, Taylor expansions, error  and stability analysis, roots of nonlinear equations, sets of linear equations, numerical integration, ordinary differential equations.
115.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken EAD 115.
115.prereq_text: (ENG 006 C- or better or EME 005 C- or better or ECS 030 C- or better or ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better or ECS 036A C- or better or ECH 060 C- or better or ECH 060V C- or better or ECM 006 C- or better); ((MAT 021A C- or better,  MAT 021B C- or better,  MAT 021C C- or better,  MAT 021D C- or better,  (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better),  (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better)),  (PHY 009A C- or better,  PHY 009B C- or better,  PHY 009C C- or better).

150A.title: Mechanical Design
150A.description: Principles of mechanics applied to design. Deformation and stress analysis. Structural integrity under static and fluctuating loads. Projects demonstrate progression from concept to engineering analysis, with emphasis on strength and durability.
150A.prereq_text: (ENG 045 C- or better or ENG 045Y C- or better); ((ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104B C- or better), EME 050 C- or better (can be concurrent)).

165.title: Heat Transfer
165.description: Conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. Computational modeling of heat transfer in engineering. Applications to engineering equipment with the use of digital computers.
165.prereq_text: (ENG 006 C- or better or EME 005 C- or better or ECS 030 C- or better); ENG 103 C- or better; ENG 105 C- or better.

172.title: Automatic Control of Engineering Systems
172.description: Classical feedback control systems; block diagrams; performance specifications; steady state errors; rise and settling times; root locus; PID controllers; Bode and Nyquist plots; stability; phase and gain margins; advanced topics as time allows.
172.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better.

401.title: Introduction to Product Development
401.description: Product development process and design controls embedded within. Clinical/customer needs finding and screening using principles of the Biodesign process and clinical exposure. Establishing a business case through market analysis, intellectual property, and reimbursement considerations. Case studies of medical devices and drug/device combination products illustrate the product life cycle.

meetings.building_name: Aggie Sq Life Long Learn Bldg

411.title: Business Leadership for Engineers I
411.description: Latest technologies and practices in the medical devices industry. Business context within which companies operate in the medical devices industry. Basic psychological and social psychological processes shaping human behavior and application of these processes to the following organizational problems: motivation, job design, commitment, socialization, culture, individual and group decision-making, and team building.

meetings.building_name: Aggie Sq Life Long Learn Bldg

421.title: Engineering Skills I: Computer Aided Design & Simulation
421.description: Essential engineering skills driven by modern computing including computer aided design (CAD), numerical simulation, and coding in Python. Advanced CAD skills focused on design intent and manufacturability, implementation and testing of engineering design concepts using finite element methods. Application of simulation and optimization techniques integrated in CAD software to analyze physical phenomena such as fluid and solid mechanics in medical devices.
421.prereq_text: Introductory CAD course or prior equivalent industry experience required (SolidWorks preferred); engineering math recommended; one or more of the following recommended: transport phenomena, fluid dynamics, mechanics.

431.title: Capstone Project I: Introduction to Clinical Needs & Operations
431.description: Principles of medical device innovation, with exposure to hospital and clinical operations. Needs finding and needs screening based on real-world unmet needs. Identification of potential solutions based on needs refinement and operational constraints to secure topics for capstone projects.

meetings.building_name: Aggie Sq Life Long Learn Bldg

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Group Study in Medical Microbiology and Immunology; primarily for lower division students. Directed reading and discussion on selected topics.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

188B.title: Human Immunology
188B.description: Understand the human immune system, the nomenclature and functional significance of the tissues, cells, proteins and genes, as well as the normal regulatory mechanisms and pathologic outcomes related to the immune response.

192.title: Internship in Medical Microbiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in medical microbiology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

194H.title: Senior Honors Project in Medical Microbiology & Immunology
194H.description: Project in research related to immunology of medically important viruses. Development of a hypothesis-driven project, performance of experimental protocols and preparation of graphical representation of original data. Requires oral and written presentation of research results.

198.title: Group Study in Medical Microbiology
198.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Research in Medical Microbiology
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

291.title: Seminar in Microbiology & Immunology
291.description: Research seminars on current topics in microbiology and immunology.

298.title: Group Study in Medical Microbiology & Immunology
298.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics. Sections 1, 2, 4, 5 are S/U grading only.
298.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to graduate students.

299.title: Research
299.description: Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate degree.
299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to graduate students.

092.title: Internship in Pharmacology
092.description: Supervised work experience in pharmacology and related fields.
092.prereq_text: Lower division student with good academic standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

192.title: Internship in Pharmacology
192.description: Supervised work experience in pharmacology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

205.title: Problem Solving in Pharmacology
205.description: Introduction to a current biomedical problem that would benefit from a developing drug and will develop an experimental strategy for addressing the issue. Develop model systems for testing various classic and recent pharmacological approaches.

192.title: Medical Education Internship for Advanced Undergraduates
192.description:
Participate in projects related to curriculum development in support of curriculum for M.D. degree. Gain work experience and appreciation
for innovative approaches to learning in basic and clinical sciences of medical education.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; competency with computers.

441.title: Combined Ophthalmology & Otolaryngology Clerkship
441.description: Fundamental knowledge of ophthalmology and otolaryngology for the treatment of eye, ear, nose and throat problems at a level of training of general physicians, including when to refer patients to a specialist.
441.prereq_text: Approval by Committee on Student Promotion and Evaluation.

443.title: Global Health ASC
443.description: Aimed at furthering student experience with global health. An important step toward addressing global health is to drive learning toward consistent One Health core competencies in medical education and other health sciences.

489C.title: Clinical Reintroduction Experience
489C.description: Learn and practice basic clinical skills in a supervised clinical setting. Skills include patient interviewing, history, physical examination, diagnostic and clinical reasoning, case presentation, and medical records documentation. Direct observation and individual feedback on clinical skills development is provided.

490.title: Reimagining Education to Advance Central California Health (REACH) Selective
490.description: Third-year REACH students participate in the clinical care of patients at Kaiser Central Valley and associated partners in Central California within specialties of internal medicine, family medicine, pediatrics, surgery, or obstetrics/gynecology. Rotate through outpatient clinics, inpatient wards, and consult services, and may be introduced organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources who care for the same people.

491.title: TEACH-MS Pediatric Advocacy & Community Health Elective
491.description: Through this elective, third- or fourth- year students gain understanding in the importance of community partnerships by directly engaging with community organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources that they may refer their patients to. Students who complete this elective will develop key skills necessary for educating the public and lobbying key decision-makers in government.

496.title: California Oregon Medical Partnership to Address Disparities in Rural Education & Health (COMPADRE) Elective
496.description: Third- or fourth-year students enrolled in COMPADRE participate in the clinical care of patients from rural, underserved, or indigenous communities. Students may rotate through outpatient clinics, inpatient wards, and consult services, and may also be introduced to local community organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources that they may refer their patients to.

020A.title: Intro to Late Antique & Early Medieval Worlds
020A.description: Late antique and early medieval worlds. Social and political structure, prominent philosophies, and literature of societies from the Middle East, Europe, East Asia, South Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

190.title: Senior Thesis
190.description: Preparation of a research paper dealing with a selected aspect of remodern (from Late Antique to Early Modern) culture, under supervision with a designated Supervisor and second reader.
190.prereq_text: Senior standing and major in Medieval & Early Modern Studies.

197T.title: Tutoring in Medieval Studies
197T.description: Tutoring in MST 020A & MST 020B, including leadership in small discussion groups affiliated with the course.
197T.prereq_text: MST 020A; MST 020B; upper division standing; consent of instructor and chairperson of curriculum committee.

102.title: Introductory Microbiology
102.description: Essentials of microbial biology, emphasizing phylogeny, physiology, genetics, ecology, and pathogenesis. Interactions with other microbes, humans, and the biosphere. Uses of microbes in agriculture and biotechnology. May be taught abroad.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MIC 101, MIC 102, or MIC 104.
102.prereq_text: (BIS 001A or BIS 002A or BIO 002); CHE 002B (can be concurrent).

103L.title: Introductory Microbiology Laboratory
103L.description: Introduction to principles and laboratory methods employed in working with microorganisms. Designed for students requiring microbiology for professional school admission. May be taught abroad.
103L.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who completed MIC 101 before spring 2016, or who have completed MIC 102L, or MIC 104L.
103L.prereq_text: (MIC 102 C- or better or MMG 102 C- or better (can be concurrent) or MMG 102V C- or better (can be concurrent)); CHE 002B.

107L.title: General Microbiology Laboratory
107L.description: Principles and laboratory methods employed in working with microorganisms. Designed for students continuing in microbiology, genetics, or biochemistry.
107L.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who completed MIC 101 before spring 2016, or who have completed MIC 103L or MMG 103L; not open to students who have completed MIC 102L or MIC 104L.
107L.prereq_text: (MIC 102 C- or better (can be concurrent) or MMG 102 C- or better (can be concurrent) or MMG 102V C- or better (can be concurrent)); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 129A); consent of instructor.

111.title: Human Microbiology
111.description: Biology of microorganisms that form commensal, mutualistic, and pathogenic relationships with human beings, emphasizing their phylogeny, physiology, genetics, and ecology. Effects on human nutrition, development and physiology. Mechanisms of pathogenesis, immune response evasion, antibiotic action, and antibiotic resistance.
111.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MIC 111.
111.prereq_text: MIC 102 C- or better or MMG 102 C- or better); (BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better.)

115.title: Recombinant DNA Cloning & Analysis
115.description: Cloning and analysis of recombinant DNA, with emphasis on Escherichia coli host-vector systems. DNA- modifying enzymes; vectors and their use; manipulation and expression of insert DNA; polymerase chain reaction; and sequence annotation. Graduate students see MIC 215.
115.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken MIC 115.
115.prereq_text: (BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better); or the equivalent.

275.title: Seminar in DNA Repair & Recombination
275.description: Review and discussion of current research and literature in DNA repair and recombination with presentations by individual students and invited speakers.
275.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in Microbiology or closely related field.

291.title: Selected Topics in Microbiology
291.description: Current progress in microbiology and cellular and molecular biology.

200A.title: Microbial Biology
200A.description: Designed to provide an overview of various aspects of microbiology and microbial processes. Topics will include microbial genetics and genomics, microbial metabolism, signaling, and adaptations.
200A.prereq_text: MIC 102; or equivalent; prior coursework in Microbiology.

201L.title: Advanced Microbiology Laboratory Rotations
201L.description: Two five-week assignments in microbiology research laboratories. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

215.title: Recombinant DNA
215.description: Application of recombinant DNA technology to modern problems in biology, biochemistry, and genetics, emphasizing molecular cloning strategies, genomic analysis, DNA replication, and genome editing.
215.credit_limit_text: 1 unit of credit for students who have previously taken MIC 115 or MMG 115; no credit to students who have taken MIC 215.
215.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V); BIS 103; or the equivalent.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of staff research activities. Designed for advanced graduate students.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Directed reading and discussion on select topics.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research under the guidance of dissertation committee.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of staff research activities. Designed for advanced graduate students.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

002Y.title: World Coffee Cultures
002Y.description: Coffee cultural traditions and practices from around the world. Historical perspectives and analysis of future trends. Corresponding experiments testing distinct cultural influences on the sensory qualities and nutritional aspects of coffee beverages.

131B.title: Modern South Asia Cinema
131B.description: South Asian cinema of last 100 years in the context of cultural, social, and political changes. South Asian history, Independence, Partition, urban life, class, migration, postcolonial identity, diaspora, gender, sexuality, religion, sport, performance, etc
131B.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

150.title: Women & Islamic Discourses
150.description: Introduction to debates/discourses about women and Islam. Transformations in debates/discourses in colonial and postcolonial periods in the Middle East & South Asia. Comparative study of debates/discourses on family, work, law, sexuality, religion, comportment, human rights, and feminist and religious movements.
150.prereq_text: GSW 050 or GSW 050V; or comparable course.

011.title: U.S. Army Leadership & Personal Development
011.description: United States Army, its organization, customs, courtesies, and rank structure. Surveys personal development skills needed for effective leadership such as critical thinking, time management, and health and fitness. Familiarization with the Army ROTC program.

014A.title: Introduction to Military Leadership Skills
014A.description: Personal and organizational leadership skills introduced in leadership laboratory. Extensive supervised leadership experiences conducted in a military environment. Basic military skills necessary to function in a leadership role.
014A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

022A.title: Innovative Team Leadership
022A.description: Leadership values, attributes and theories. Use of basic military skills such as land navigation and squad operations to enhance understanding of the Army.  Types of military briefings.  Practice in interpersonal skills.  Presentation of a briefing.
022A.prereq_text: Lower division standing or consent of instructor.

024A.title: Individual Military Leadership Skills
024A.description: Develop and practice personal military leadership skills in extensive supervised leadership labs.  Cadets perform basic military skills, improve on troop leading procedures and lead subordinates in tactical situations.  Begin with drill and ceremony, land navigation and individual movement techniques.
024A.prereq_text: MSC 014A; MSC 014B; MSC 014C; MSC 022A (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor. MSC 022A required concurrently.

132A.title: Advanced Military Operations
132A.description: Military small unit tactical theory as the basis for leadership development.  Principles of war, contemporary operating environment, Geneva Law of Land Warfare, military offensive and defensive operations.  Emphasis on development of critical thinking, problem solving, and communication skills.
132A.prereq_text: MSC 131; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

134A.title: Adaptive Tactical Leadership
134A.description: Small unit tactical operations serve as the basis for enhancement of leadership performance through tactical application.  Assessment of leadership attributes, skills, and actions through participation in a variety of leadership roles in problem-solving exercises.
134A.prereq_text: MSC 131; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

143.title: U.S. Army Management Systems
143.description: Leadership and management, focusing on four management systems: planning, organizing, leading and controlling. Practical methodologies for assessing management decisions while balancing competing ethical, economic, infrastructure and future growth trade-offs.
143.prereq_text: MSC 142; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

144A.title: Military Training Leadership Skills
144A.description: Enhancement of student leadership performance through practical application.  Small unit military tactical operations as the basis for the student exploration and development.
144A.prereq_text: MSC 141; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

191.title: Special Studies in Military Science
191.description: Intensive examination of one or more special problems in military science. Possible areas of study include leadership dimensions, principles of war, air-land battle imperatives, military strategy, the operational art and professional ethics.
191.prereq_text: MSC 131; MSC 132A; MSC 132B; MSC 141; MSC 142; MSC 143; consent of department chair.

120.title: Molecular Biology & Biochemistry Laboratory Associated Lecture
120.description: Introduction to laboratory methods and procedures employed in studying molecular biology and biochemical processes. Lecture component for MCB 120L.
120.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or consent of instructor.

120L.title: Molecular Biology & Biochemistry Laboratory
120L.description: Introduction to laboratory methods and procedures employed in studying molecular biology and biochemical processes. Designed for students who need experience in use of molecular biology and biochemical techniques as research and analytical tools.
120L.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or consent of instructor; must be taken concurrently with MCB 120.

124.title: Macromolecular Structure & Function
124.description: In-depth investigation into protein and nucleic acid structure and thermodynamics and how these properties influence their biological functions. Key examples of important functional classes of these molecules are examined.
124.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 108.
124.prereq_text: (BIS 102 C- or better or BIS 102 C- or better); (BIS 101 or BIS 101V).

144.title: Mechanisms of Cell Division
144.description: The molecules and mechanisms that allow eukaryotic cells to coordinate cell growth, DNA replication, segregation of chromosomes and cell division.

160L.title: Principles of Genetics Laboratory
160L.description: Laboratory work in basic and molecular genetics including gene mapping, isolation and characterization of mutants in eukaryotic model systems, reverse genetics, gel electrophoresis, recombinant DNA techniques, and PCR.

182.title: Principles of Genomics
182.description: Fundamentals of genomics, including structural genomics, functional genomics, proteomics, and bioinformatics,  focusing on the impact of these disciplines on research in the biological sciences. Social impacts of genomic research.

190C.title: Undergraduate Research Conference
190C.description: Presentation and discussion of current research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: MCB 193 (can be concurrent) or MCB 199 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; upper division standing; MCB 193 or MCB 199 required concurrently.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Technical and/or practical experience on and off campus, supervised by a member of the Section of Molecular and Cellular Biology faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

193.title: Advanced Research
193.description: Research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Discussion and analysis of results and proposed experiments on a weekly basis with faculty sponsor. May include presentation of a seminar to a research group.
193.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; completion of an upper division Molecular & Cellular Biology (MCB) laboratory course.

194.title: Thesis Research
194.description: Continuation of an intensive, individual laboratory research project in biochemistry, genetics, or cell biology culminating with the presentation of the work in a written thesis and in a seminar.
194.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; 6 units of MCB 193 and/or MCB 199 with faculty director; senior standing.

194H.title: Research Honors
194H.description: Honors project. Continuation of an intensive, individual laboratory research project in biochemistry, genetics, or cell biology culminating with the presentation of the work in a written thesis and in a seminar.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; 6 units of MCB 193 and/or MCB 199 with faculty director; senior standing; GPA of at least 3.250.

197T.title: Tutoring in Molecular & Cellular Biology
197T.description: Assisting the instructor in one of the section's regular courses by tutoring individual or small groups of students in a laboratory, in voluntary discussion groups, or other voluntary course activities. May be taught abroad.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing, completion of course to be tutored.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

282.title: Biotechnology Internship
282.description: Research at a biotechnology company or interdisciplinary cross-college lab for a minimum of 3 months as part of the Designated Emphasis in Biotechnology Program.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Presentations and critical discussions of faculty and graduate student research in molecular and cellular biology including biochemistry, genetics, and cell biology.

291.title: Current Progress in Molecular & Cellular Biology
291.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subject of their own research activities.
291.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

390.title: Methods of Teaching
390.description:
Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching biochemistry/genetics/cell biology. Includes analysis of texts and
supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques, preparing for and conducting discussion and laboratory sections, formulating examinations under supervision of instructor. Participating in the teaching program required for Ph.D.

101V.title: Principles of Pharmacology & Toxicology
101V.description: Online course provides training in core concepts of pharmacological and toxicological sciences and prepares to develop higher-order problem solving and critical thinking skills. Designed for advanced undergraduate students with interests in pursuing graduate degrees in pharmacology, toxicology, physiological sciences, and for students with an interest in pursuing D.V.M., M.D., Pharmacy, Dentistry and Nursing professional degrees. Students who pursue careers in environmental sciences, public health management, and epidemiology may also benefit from the subject matter presented in this course.
101V.prereq_text: Consent of instructor;  upper division standing in a science major; chemistry through organic chemistry, general biology, or consent of instructor; good standing with the university; computing capability (use MS Word®, Excel®, PowerPoint®, menu driven software programs, Course LMS); own a computer or have ready access to a computer with broadband Internet access; NPB 101 and BIS 104 recommended.

210L.title: Physiology Laboratory Rotations
210L.description: One mandatory rotation and up-to two voluntary rotations. Students learn techniques and perform experiments related to particular research problems. At the end of the rotations students give a short talk and hand in a research paper.

211A.title: Critical Evaluation of Physiology Research
211A.description: Recent peer-reviewed articles on topics in cell physiology, transport physiology, signal transduction, physiology of excitable cells, and muscle physiology. Critical evaluation of research questions, experimental design, data quality, and interpretation. Development of subject-matter mastery, critical reading, presentation, and discussion skills for physiological research.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of advanced topics and current trends in research.

002A.title: Keyboard Competence, Part 1
002A.description: Training to meet the minimum piano requirements for the major in music. Scales and simple harmonic progressions in twelve keys, both major and minor.

003A.title: Introduction to Music Theory, Part 1
003A.description: Fundamentals of music theory, ear-training, harmony, counterpoint, and analysis directed toward the development of listening and writing techniques. Intended for the general student.

007A.title: Intermediate Theory, Part 1
007A.description: Homophonic music of the Classical era with a focus on analysis of music by Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven. Composition of pieces in the homophonic forms such as minuet and trio, theme and variations, rondo and sonata. Intended for music majors.
007A.prereq_text: (MUS 006B; MUS 017A (can be concurrent)); or consent of instructor; students can place into MUS 007A based on the results of a diagnostic test given at the beginning of fall term.

010.title: Introduction to Musical Literature
010.description: Introduction to composers and major styles of Western music. Lectures, listening sections, and selected readings. For non-majors.

011.title: Musics of the World
011.description: Survey of selected art, folk, and popular music cultures from different parts of the world. Emphasis on understanding relationship of musical style, aesthetic principles, and performance practice to wider cultural contexts.

013.title: Introduction to Musicianship,  Part 1
013.description: Melodic and rhythmic materials of Western music. Includes drills, explanations, sight singing, and listening analysis.
013.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have previously completed MUS 016A.
013.prereq_text: Placement test at start of fall quarter; for more details, see Music Department website.

017A.title: Intermediate Musicianship, Part 1
017A.description: Melodic, rhythmic, and harmonic materials of Western music. Includes sight singing, explanations, drills, melodic/rhythmic/harmonic dictations, and listening analysis.
017A.prereq_text: MUS 007A (can be concurrent); or demonstrate required proficiency level on diagnostic exam.

101A.title: Advanced Theory, Part 1
101A.description: Music of the 20th century from 1930 through 1950 and the various analytical tools pertaining to it. Works of Copland, Sessions, Schoenberg, Bartók, and Stravinsky. Composition of small pieces for piano and voice.

103.title: Workshop in Composition
103.description: Workshop in musical composition for undergraduates who are interested in pursuing serious compositional studies and intending to follow the composition track of the major. Explores the techniques and materials of musical composition.

107A.title: Introduction to Electronic Music
107A.description: Basics of electronic music history, techniques, and composition. Fixed media creation using field recordings. Focus on history, theory and techniques of musique concrète, elektronische musik, and related repertoire.

108A.title: Orchestration
108A.description: Techniques of orchestration from study of basic instrumental techniques to analysis of orchestral scores and scoring for various instrumental combinations.

116.title: Introduction to the Music of The Beatles
116.description: Survey of music of The Beatles, focusing on the songs of Lennon and McCartney. Emphasis on understanding their evolution as musicians, composers and cultural figures. Discussion of their musical influences in wider cultural contexts.

121.title: Topics in Music Scholarship
121.description: Sources and problems of a historical period or musical style selected by the instructor and announced in advance.
121.prereq_text: MUS 006B; MUS 024B; or consent of instructor.

123.title: Music as Culture
123.description: Introduction to the study of music in cross-cultural perspective. Basic theories and frameworks of ethnomusicology; in-depth case studies of three musical traditions from around the world. Intended for music majors.

131A.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual)
131A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131B.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Piano
131B.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131C.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Harpsichord
131C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131D.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Organ
131D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131E.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Violin
131E.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131F.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Viola
131F.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to Music majors only; admission by audition.

131G.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Cello
131G.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131H.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Double Bass
131H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131I.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Flute
131I.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131J.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Oboe
131J.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131K.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Clarinet
131K.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131L.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Bassoon
131L.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131M.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); French Horn
131M.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131N.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Trumpet
131N.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131O.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual);Trombone
131O.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131P.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Tuba
131P.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131Q.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Percussion
131Q.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131R.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Classical Guitar
131R.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131U.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Saxophone

131W.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Harp
131W.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admitted by audition.

140.title: University Jazz Band
140.description: Rehearsal, study, and performance of jazz band music and a full variety of jazz band styles, including swing, be-bob, and contemporary jazz styles.
140.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

141.title: University Symphony
141.description: Open to any student in the University whose proficiency meets the requirements of concert performance. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of music from the orchestral literature.
141.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

142.title: University Chamber Singers
142.description: Rehearsal and performance of works for small choral group.
142.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

143.title: University Concert Band
143.description: Rehearsal and performance of music for band.
143.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

144.title: University Chorus
144.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral music.
144.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

146.title: Chamber Music Ensemble
146.description: Open to any student in the University whose proficiency meets the requirements of concert performance. Study, rehearsal, and performance of ensemble music for strings, winds, voice, piano, harpsichord, and organ.
146.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

149.title: Indonesian Gamelan Ensemble
149.description:
Indonesian music practice. Basic instrumental technique and repertory.
Focus on two styles of Sundanese gamelan (tuned percussion orchestras): 
salendro and degung.

150.title: Brazilian Samba School
150.description: Practice of Brazilian music. Basic instrumental technique and repertory. Focus on the percussion traditions of Rio de Janeiro and Bahia.

153.title: Brazilian Capoeira Ensemble
153.description: Basic instrumental techniques, songs, and dance movements of Capoeira Angola. Protocols of a Capoeira Angola performance and the meanings of Capoeira in Brazil with its connections to Afro-Brazilian culture.

155.title: Percussion Ensemble
155.description: Study and rehearsal of percussion chamber music from the 20th and 21st centuries. Study of standard and extended techniques for a broad range of percussion instruments. Public performance of significant works for percussion ensemble.
155.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

156.title: Mariachi Ensemble
156.description: Rehearsal and performance of traditional and contemporary mariachi repertoire.

157.title: Bluegrass & Old Time String Band
157.description: Performance of bluegrass and Appalachian old time music. Practice of instrumental and vocal techniques and repertory in vernacular American string band idioms.

170A.title: Intro to Recording Techniques
170A.description: Introduction to basic recording equipment, including microphones, cables, pre-amplifiers, mixers, interfaces, and digital audio workstations. Fundamental techniques including gain staging, panning, equalization, compression, and basic mixing.

192.title: Internship in Music
192.description: Internship outside the university related to music.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor or academic advisor.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of music.

194HB.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HB.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of music.

195.title: Senior Project
195.description: Preparation of a senior project in music composition (public presentation of a new work), in music performance (a public recital), or in music history and theory (public presentation of research results).

210B.title: Proseminar in Music: Musicology &Criticism
210B.description: Issues and concepts of music history, including performance practice questions for specific repertoires and periods; principles, aims, and methods of archival study; historical theory; evolution of musical styles; philosophical debates about goals and aims of the discipline in general.

223.title: Topics in Ethnomusicology
223.description: In-depth ethnomusicological studies of selected cultures and their musics; study of historical, theoretical, contextual, and cultural features.

001.title: Introduction to Native American Studies
001.description: Introduction to Native American Studies with emphasis upon basic concepts relating to Native American historical and political development.

005.title: Introduction to Native American Literature
005.description: Focus on the development of writing skills through close readings and analysis of Native American literary texts, with scaffolded writing assignments to develop critical thinking and composition skills.
005.prereq_text: NAS 005A (can be concurrent) or UWP 001A (can be concurrent); or completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005A.title: Writer's Workshop
005A.description: Disciplinary writing support course focuses on the development of writing and revision strategies, exploring ways to understand a writing task, to develop appropriate content for a writing task, to revise content to reflect competence as a communicator.
005A.prereq_text: Has not yet completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); concurrent enrollment in NAS 005 required.

007.title: Indigenous & Minority Languages
007.description: Survey of the status of indigenous, immigrant, and other minority languages in the Americas and around the world. Topics include linguistic diversity, language endangerment & revitalization, heritage language maintenance in immigrant communities, and language change due to transcultural interactions.

034.title: Native American Art Studio
034.description: Studio projects to be influenced by contemporary and traditional Native American arts. Examples of designs and media presented in lectures will be of indigenous origin. Introduction and familiarized with various materials and techniques.

107.title: Learning Native American Languages
107.description: Self-directed study of a Native American language using revitalization strategies. Origins of language endangerment and the importance of language for cultural reclamation.

110A.title: Quechua Language & Society: Beginning Level 1
110A.description: Quechua language and society emphasizing the practical use of the language. Provides some basic Quechua communication skills and with an initial knowledge about contemporary Andean society and the status of Quechua language today.

190.title: Advanced Seminar on Sovereignty & Autonomy
190.description: Advanced course for NAS majors on contemporary theory and practice in Native American and Indigenous Studies.

193.title: Leadership Training in Native American & Indigenous Organizations
193.description: Supervised leadership training in Native American department, campus, and community settings, including the Native American Academic Student Success Center (NAASSC; aka, the Native "Nest").

194HA.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.

194HB.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HB.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.

195.title: Field Experience in Native American Studies
195.description: Field work with governmental and community groups, under supervision of faculty advisor and sponsor. Knowledge acquired in other courses to be applied in field work.
195.prereq_text: NAS 161; senior standing and major in Native American Studies, completion of lower division major requirements.

196.title: Senior Project in Native American Studies
196.description: Guided research project that enables student to apply the theory and research principles from major course work. Final product is to be a major senior project or thesis.
196.prereq_text: NAS 195 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; senior standing and major in Native American Studies.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in Native American Studies
197TC.prereq_text: Consent of major committee; upper division standing with major in Native American Studies.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

200.title: Basic Concepts in Native American Studies
200.description: Analysis of characteristics of the discipline of Native American Studies. Concentration of traditional and contemporary native scholarship and thought as well as theoretical and methodological consequences derived from application of these ideas.

202.title: Advanced Topics in Native American Studies
202.description: Advanced study of selected topics or themes relevant to the field of Native American studies. Topics will be announced at the time of offering.

254.title: Native American Literature
254.description: Introduction to the field of Native American Literature, creative works (fiction, poetry, memoir, personal essay), literary studies.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Planning and results of research programs, proposals, and experiments. Discussion and critical evaluation of original research being conducted by the group. Discussion led by individual research instructors for research group.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Nephrology
192.description: Supervised work experience in nephrology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

010.title: Elementary Human Physiology
010.description: Introduction to physiology for non-science majors. Includes basic cell physiology and survey of major organ systems and how they function in homeostasis and human health.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 101.

091C.title: Research Conference
091C.description: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
091C.prereq_text: NPB 099 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; lower division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 099 required concurrently.

092.title: Internship
092.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
Department of Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.

100.title: Neurobiology
100.description: Brains and nervous systems, neurons and neural circuits. Coordination of movement. Development of nervous systems. Vision, hearing, and feature extraction by the central nervous system. The cell biology of learning and memory. Perception, cognition, and disorders of the brain.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110B, NPB 112, NPB 160, NPB 161 or NPB 162, or NSC 221 or NSC 222.
100.prereq_text: BIS 002A; PHY 009A, PHY 009B or PHY 007A, PHY 007B recommended.

100L.title: Neurobiology Laboratory
100L.description: Experimental basis of neurobiology principles discussed in NPB 100. Topics include neurophysiology, sensory systems, motor systems, cellular neuroscience, cognitive neuroscience, and quantitative data analysis and modeling techniques.
100L.prereq_text: NPB 100 (can be concurrent) or NPB 110B (can be concurrent).

101.title: Systemic Physiology
101.description: Systemic physiology with emphasis on aspects of human physiology. Functions of major organ systems, with the structure of those systems described as a basis for understanding the functions.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110C.
101.prereq_text: (BIO 002 or BIS 002A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH); or consent of instructor; PHY 001B or PHY 007C strongly recommended.

101L.title: Systemic Physiology Laboratory
101L.description: Selected experiments to illustrate functional characteristics of organ systems discussed in NPB 101.
101L.prereq_text: ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C.

102.title: Animal Behavior
102.description: Basic principles of behavioral organization in vertebrate and invertebrate animals. Underlying physiological and ethological mechanisms. The evolution of behavior, with special emphasis on behavior under natural conditions.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 155. (Former NPB 155.)

106.title: Experiments in Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Design & Execution
106.description: Design and execution of experiments in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Choose and design a project in consultation with the sponsoring faculty member.
106.prereq_text: (NPB 110A or NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 102); NPB 199; and consent of instructor.

110A.title: Foundations 1: From Molecules to Individuals
110A.description: Major concepts in cell biology with special emphasis on connections between cell biology and behavior. Includes: cellular metabolism, cellular sensing and signaling, membrane structure-function, molecular switches, electrical and chemical signaling, endocrine signaling, cell cycle and differentiation, cytoskeleton, and integrative examples.
110A.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 3 units for students who have taken BIS 104.
110A.prereq_text: ((BIS 002A, BIS 002B) or (BIO 001, BIO 002)); (CHE 002B or CHE 003A); PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended; BIS 002C recommended.

110B.title: Foundations 2: Neurobiology
110B.description: Core concepts of neurobiology including single-neuron biophysics, synapses and transmitters, neuronal development, motor systems, central pattern generation, neuronal circuits, intracellular signal transduction, sensory processing, multisensory integration, autonomic nervous system, neuromodulation, learning and memory, and higher cognition and disease.
110B.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 2 units for students who have taken NPB 100.
110B.prereq_text: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended.

110C.title: Foundations 3: Physiology
110C.description: Focuses on the structure, function, and interactions of human and other animal organ systems in homeostasis and reproduction, and the response to perturbations of homeostasis; neural and endocrine signaling; skeletal muscle and movement; cardiovascular and respiratory systems; renal, digestive, immune, and reproductive physiology.
110C.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units for students who have taken NPB 101.
110C.prereq_text: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A; PHY 007B and PHY 007C recommended.

113.title: Cardiovascular, Respiratory, & Renal Physiology
113.description: Intense and advanced presentation of concepts in cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal physiology including discussion of acid-base balance.
113.prereq_text: (NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V); CHE 008B, PHY 007B and PHY 007C recommended.

114.title: Gastrointestinal Physiology
114.description: Gastrointestinal anatomy and physiology.  Digestion, secretion, absorption, motility, comparative physiology and pathology.  Strong emphasis on neural and hormonal regulation and on cellular mechanisms of secretion and absorption.
114.prereq_text: (NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V); BIS 105 or BIS 103 recommended, BIS 105 preferred.

117.title: Avian Physiology
117.description: Physiology of the various systems of birds with emphasis on digestion, respiration, excretion, and endocrine systems.
117.prereq_text: ((BIS 002A, BIS 002B) or BIO 001 or BIO 002); CHE 002B.  NPB 101 or NPB 110C strongly recommended.

123.title: Comparative Vertebrate Organology
123.description: Functional anatomy of major organ systems in vertebrates.  Each system examined from cellular to gross level in fish, birds, and mammals. Emphasis on how differentiated cell types are integrated into tissues and organs to perform diverse physiological functions.

130.title: Physiology of the Endocrine Glands
130.description: Advanced presentation of concepts in endocrinology with emphasis on the role of hormones in reproduction, metabolism, and disease.
130.prereq_text: (ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C).

143.title: Neurobiology & Pathophysiology of Mental Illness
143.description: Comparison of the neurobiology and physiology of mental health to the pathophysiology of mental illness. Causative factors of mental illness (e.g., genetic, social, environmental) through a neurobiology and pathophysiology lens (e.g., neurotransmission, neuroimmunology, nervous system malfunction).
143.prereq_text: NPB 100 C- or better; or NPB 110B C- or better; or consent of instructor.

162.title: Neural Mechanisms of Behavior
162.description: Relationship between brain and behavior. Identification and analysis of the relevant neural circuits involved. Examples of systems to be considered are birdsong, locomotion, echolocation.
162.prereq_text: NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110B.

171.title: Physiology of Neuroimmune Interactions
171.description: Explores the complex interactions of the nervous and immune systems, and examine how the systems function together to serve homeostasis, behavior, and disease (such as Alzheimer's, autism, and multiple sclerosis).
171.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (NPB 012 (can be concurrent) or NPB 100 (can be concurrent) or NPB 110B (can be concurrent)); or consent of instructor; completion of PMI 126 or MMI 188 recommended.

190C.title: Research Conference
190C.description: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: NPB 199 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; upper division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 199 required concurrently.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in neurobiology, physiology, & behavior.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Honors
194HA.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HA.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

194HB.title: Neurobiology, Physiology & Behavior: Honors
194HB.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HB.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

194HC.title: Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Honors
194HC.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HC.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

271A.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271A.description: Core concepts and methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity. Behavioral paradigms and measurement approaches in human and animal studies of learning and plasticity, as well as a consideration of the functional, anatomical and neuronal mechanisms underlying brain plasticity.
271A.prereq_text: Graduate Standing or consent of instructor.

199.title: Individual Special Study & Research
199.description: Individual special study in neurophysiology and biomedical engineering is offered to qualified students. Studies on psychophysics, single-unit electrophysiology and instrumentation are offered in Davis.

200LB.title: Laboratory Methods in Neurobiology
200LB.description: Individual research in the laboratory of a faculty member. Research problems emphasize the use of contemporary methods and good experimental design.
200LB.prereq_text: Graduate standing in the Neuroscience Graduate Group.

221.title: Cellular Neurophysiology
221.description: Physiological aspects of cellular and subcellular organization of the nervous system. Neuronal cell biology, the structure and function of ion channels, electrical excitability, signaling cascades, sensory transduction and, mechanisms of synaptic transmission, and the cellular basis of learning and memory.
221.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

226.title: Molecular & Developmental Neurobiology
226.description: Key issues in developmental and molecular neurobiology. Topics include neural induction and patterning, neurogenesis, axon guidance, synapse development and remodeling. Discussion emphasis on critical evaluation of the experiments and methods described in primary seminal research papers and current literature.

271A.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271A.description: Core concepts and methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity. Behavioral paradigms and measurement approaches in human and animal studies of learning and plasticity, as well as a consideration of the functional, anatomical and neuronal mechanisms underlying brain plasticity.
271A.prereq_text: Graduate Standing or consent of instructor.

285.title: Literature in Visual Neuroscience
285.description: Critical presentation and discussion of current literature in visual neuroscience.

290C.title: Research Conference in Neurobiology
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in neurobiology.
290C.prereq_text: NSC 299 required concurrently; graduate standing in Neuroscience or consent of instructor.

295.title: Literature in Neuroengineering
295.description: Critical presentation and discussion of current literature in neuroengineering.

290.title: Master's Seminar
290.description: Subject varies from quarter to quarter. Current knowledge and issues relevant to one of two fields of emphasis: population health or health systems.
290.prereq_text: Current enrollment in the Nursing Science and Health-Care Leadership graduate program or consent of instructor.

293DY.title: Dissertation Seminar
293DY.description: Preparation of final dissertation research. Peer review of presentation plan for dissertation results, IRB application and manuscripts in progress.

293Y.title: Proposal Development Seminar
293Y.description: Reading, critique and synthesis of classic and cutting-edge research in nursing and health care.

010.title: Discoveries & Concepts in Nutrition
010.description: Nutrition as a science; historical development of nutrition concepts; properties of nutrients and foods.
010.credit_limit_text: No credit will be granted to students who have completed NUT 010Y or NUT 010V or an upper division Nutrition (NUT) course.

010V.title: Discoveries & Concepts in Nutrition
010V.description: Nutrition as a science; historical development of nutrition concepts; properties of nutrients and foods.
010V.credit_limit_text: No credit will be granted to students who have completed NUT 010 or NUT 010Y or an upper division Nutrition (NUT) course.

011.title: Current Topics & Controversies in Nutrition
011.description: Exploration of current applications and controversies in nutrition. Read scientific journal articles and write summaries, as well as give brief oral presentations. Topics change to reflect current interests and issues.

104.title: Environmental & Nutritional Factors in Cellular Regulation & Nutritional Toxicants
104.description: Cellular regulation from nutritional/toxicological perspective. Emphasis: role of biofactors on modulation of signal transduction pathways, role of specific organelles in organization/regulation of metabolic transformations, major cofactor functions, principles of pharmacology/toxicology important to understanding nutrient/toxicant metabolism.

106.title: Food Chemistry for Clinical Nutrition
106.description: Chemical and physical principles that influence functional properties, nutrient content, safety, and sensory aspects of food. Emphasis on the application of these concepts in clinical nutrition.
106.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have completed FST 101A and/or FST 101B.
106.prereq_text: CHE 008B C- or better or CHE 118B C- or better or CHE 128B C- or better; concurrent with FST 100A recommended.

113.title: Principles of Epidemiology in Nutrition
113.description: Introduction to epidemiology as it relates to the field of nutrition, including study design, principles of epidemiologic inference, criteria for causality, and interpreting measures of disease risk.
113.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or PLS 120 or STA 100.

116A.title: Clinical Nutrition
116A.description: Biochemical and physiological bases for therapeutic diets. Problems in planning diets for normal and pathological conditions.
116A.prereq_text: (NUT 111AV or NUT 111AY); NUT 111B; NUT 112; NPB 101; or the equivalent to NPB 101.

116AL.title: Clinical Nutrition Practicum
116AL.description: Fundamental principles of planning and evaluating therapeutic diets and patient education for pathological conditions covered in 116A.

117.title: Experimental Nutrition
117.description: Methods of assessing nutritional status. Application of chemical, microbiological, chromatographic and enzymatic techniques to current problems in nutrition.
117.prereq_text: NUT 111AY; NUT 111B; NUT 112; (ABI 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 102); (ABI 103 or BIS 103); MCB 120L or other laboratory course in biochemistry is recommended.

130.title: Experiments in Nutrition: Design & Execution
130.description: Experiments in current nutritional problems. Experimental design: students choose project and, independently or in groups of two-three, design a protocol, complete the project, and report findings.
130.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; NUT 111AV, NUT 111AY, NUT 111B or NUT 114 recommended.

141.title: Comparative Animal Nutrition & Metabolism
141.description: Foundational principles of nutrition, nutrient composition of feed ingredients, digestive systems of domestic and exotic animals, nutrient digestibility and absorption, nutrient metabolism.
141.prereq_text: ABI 103; (NUT 115 or NUT 116A or NUT 116B); or consent of instructor.

190.title: Proseminar in Nutrition
190.description: Discussion of human nutrition problems. Each term will involve a different emphasis among experimental, clinical, and dietetic problems of community, national and international scope.

190C.title: Nutrition Research Conference
190C.description: Introduction to research findings and methods in nutrition. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Nutrition or related biological science.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in practical application of nutrition, supervised by a faculty member.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; one upper division course in nutrition.

197T.title: Tutoring in Nutrition
197T.description: Tutoring of students in nutrition courses, assistance with discussion groups or laboratory sections, weekly conference with instructor in charge of course: written evaluations.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; Nutrition Science, Clinical Nutrition or related major.

230.title: Experiments in Nutrition: Design & Execution
230.description: Student-selected projects to enhance laboratory skills. Independently, or in groups of two-three students, design a protocol, carry out the project, analyze the results and report the findings.
230.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; NUT 201, NUT 202, NUT 203, NUT 204, or the equivalent recommended.

290.title: Beginning Nutrition Seminar
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of topics in nutrition with emphasis on literature review and evaluation in this field. Oral presentations on relevant topics.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description:
Major professors lead research discussions with their graduate students.
Research papers are reviewed and project proposals presented and evaluated. Format will combine seminar and discussion style.

291.title: Advanced Nutrition Seminar
291.description: Advanced topics in nutrition research. Multiple sections may be taken concurrently for credit.

297T.title: Supervised Teaching in Nutrition
297T.description: Practical experience in teaching nutrition at the university level; curriculum design and evaluation; preparation and presentation of material. Assistance in laboratories, discussion sections, and evaluation of student work.
297T.prereq_text: Graduate standing in nutrition or consent of instructor.

210A.title: Advanced Nutrition I: Nutrition & Metabolism, Macronutrients
210A.description: Advanced general nutritional concepts. Integrating nutrition with biological systems, population nutrition issues, and research approaches. Advanced concepts on lipid and protein metabolism.
210A.prereq_text: Admission to the Nutritional Biology Graduate Group or consent of instructor.

194.title: Shifa Clinic Student Volunteer
194.description: Attend clinic every third Sunday performing duties of receptionist, intake, translation, monitor. Students attend a meeting immediately after end of clinic.  There is a mandatory Monday meeting with Clinic co-directors. Students are expected to participate on various committees.
194.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; applications will be available for students; selection of students will be made by selection committee of medical students coordinators and the instructor of record.

290.title: Current Topics in Research
290.description: Selected topics in reproductive biology.

192.title: Research Internship
192.description: Supervised work experience in ophthalmology research. Research staff in Ophthalmology have programs in cell biology, electron microscopy, biochemistry, immunology and visual psychophysics.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

465.title: Advanced Subspecialty Ophthalmology
465.description: Participation in disciplines of neuro-ophthalmology/pediatric ophthalmology, diseases of the cornea and external eye, glaucoma and retina.
465.prereq_text: IMD 430; consent of instructor; medical students in third or fourth year.

099.title: Special Studies for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

192.title: Internship in Human Pathology
192.description: Supervised work experience in pathology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

199.title: Special Study in Pathology for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study in Pathology for advanced undergraduates.

290C.title: Research Group Conferences
290C.description: Focused around the mechanisms of function of the central nervous system under normal and pathogenic conditions. Seminars lead by various speakers from UC Davis and other Institutions, both domestic and international.

298.title: Advanced Group Study
298.description: Group Study provides the opportunity for a faculty member to work with students in a focused manner.

405.title: Brain Cutting Conference
405.description: Current specimens are sectioned, discussed, and clinical correlations proposed.
405.prereq_text: Third- and fourth-year medical students or consent of instructor.

129Y.title: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces
129Y.description: Introduction to fundamentals, challenges, and opportunities in One Health  using local and global health case studies. Animal, human, and environmental health problems, along with tools and transdisciplinary approaches, will be introduced to foster innovative thinking that addresses complex issues.

214.title: Biology of Arthropod-Borne Pathogens
214.description: Overview of the biology of major vector borne pathogens across the world

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Topics in pathology, microbiology or immunology.

199.title: Special Study in Pediatric Research
199.prereq_text: Undergraduate student with consent of instructor based upon adequate preparation as determined by instructor.

299.title: Pediatric Research
