299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate students who are candidates for a degree in some area of biology or behavioral sciences.

200.title: Methods & Materials in Theatre Research
200.description: Essential research tools in theatre and related fields; bibliographies, primary sources; methods of evaluating and presenting evidence; delineating research areas in the field.

259.title: Topics in Contemporary Theatre & Performance
259.description: Special topics designed to study in depth aspects of contemporary performance including performance analysis, cultural and historical context, modes of production, theoretical and political entailments, and issues of spectatorship; e.g., "Brecht and After," "British Theater," "Race and Gender in Performance."

270A.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270A.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270A.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

270B.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270B.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project, to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270B.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

270C.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270C.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

290.title: Colloquia in Performance Studies
290.description: Designed to provide cohort identity and faculty exchange. Opportunity to present papers, hear guest   lecturers, and see faculty presentations, gather for organizational and administrative new, exchange of information and make announcements. Must be taken every year that a Performance Studies graduate is registered, prior to taking the Qualifying Examination.
290.prereq_text: Registration in Performance Studies Graduate Group and prior to Qualifying Examination.

299D.title: Dissertation Research
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advancement to Candidacy.

459.title: Approaches to Theatre & Dance
459.description: Work on approaches to theatre, dance, film/video, design and performance, with a focus on methodology and professional development.
459.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advanced graduate students.

001.title: Elementary Persian
001.description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in Persian and to Persian culture.

021.title: Intermediate Persian
021.description: Integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading and writing skills as well as cultural topics in intermediate Persian.

101.title: Advanced Persian: Topics in Modern Persian Culture 1900-Present
101.description: Integrated work on reading, listening, discussion and writing about modern Persian cultural production using fiction and poetry as well as cinema and theory.

201.title: Principles of Pharmacology & Toxicology I
201.description: First of three courses presenting fundamental principles of pharmacology and toxicology. Introductory overview of basic concepts in pharmacology/toxicology, followed by in-depth blocks on fate processes of chemicals in the body, fate processes in tissue selective responses, selective toxicity employed therapeutically.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current topics in pharmacology and toxicology.

001.title: Introduction to Philosophy
001.description: Problems of philosophy through major writings from various periods. Problems are drawn from political, aesthetic, religious, metaphysical, and epistemological concerns of philosophy.

005.title: Critical Reasoning
005.description: Criteria of good reasoning in everyday life and in science. Topics to be covered may include basic principles of deduction and induction; fallacies in reasoning; techniques and aids to reasoning; principles of scientific investigation; aids to clarity.
005.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PHI 006.

010.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
010.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary cognitive scientific approach to the study of mind, drawing concepts and methods from psychology, philosophy, linguistics, artificial intelligence, and other disciplines.

011.title: Asian Philosophy
011.description: Survey of the main philosophical systems of south and east Asia: Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism. Topics include the nature of reality, including God, the universe and the human self, human knowledge, and the proper conduct of human life.

012.title: Introduction to Symbolic Logic
012.description: Syntax and semantics of the symbolic language sentence logic. Symbols of sentence logic. Translation between sentence logic and English. Truth table interpretation of sentence logic. Proof techniques.  Application of truth tables and proof techniques to arguments in English.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken PHI 112, PHI 113, PHI 134, or PHI 135 and passed with a grade of C or better.

013.title: Minds, Brains, & Computers
013.description: Computational theories of the nature of the mind. Mind as a computer process. Possibility of machine intelligence, consciousness, and mentality.
013.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed PHI 013G.

013D.title: Minds, Brains, & Computers, Discussion
013D.description: Small group discussion and preparation of papers related to the content of PHI 013. Computational theories of the nature of the mind. Mind as a computer process. Possibility of machine intelligence, consciousness, and mentality.
013D.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken PHI 013G.
013D.prereq_text: PHI 013 (can be concurrent); Concurrent enrollment in PHI 013 strongly recommended.

030.title: Introduction to Philosophy of Science
030.description: Basic problems in the philosophy of science, common to the physical, biological, and social sciences. Analysis of explanation, confirmation theory, observational and theoretical terms, the nature of theories, operationalism and behaviorism, realism, reduction.

031.title: Appraising Scientific Reasoning
031.description: Introduction to scientific hypotheses and the kinds of reasoning used to justify such hypotheses. Emphasis on adequate justification, criteria, and strategies for distinguishing scientific from pseudoscientific theories. Concrete historical and contemporary cases.

102.title: Theory of Knowledge
102.description: Analysis of the concept of knowledge. The relation between knowledge, belief and truth. Development of foundationalist, coherentist and externalist theories of justified belief. Examination of skepticism.

104.title: The Evolution of Mind
104.description: Interpretation of human thought and behavior through the lens of evolutionary theory. Topics include the nature/nurture debate concerning cognitive and other mental capacities and traits, and the interaction between evolution, learning and development.
104.prereq_text: One previous course in Philosophy recommended.

111.title: Philosophy of Space & Time
111.description: Philosophical problems of space and time. Philosophical implications of space-time theories, such as those of Newton and Einstein. Topics may include the nature of geometry, conventionalism, absolutist versus relationist views of space and time, philosophical impact of relativity theory.
111.prereq_text: One upper division Philosophy course recommended.

112.title: Intermediate Symbolic Logic
112.description: Predicate logic syntax and semantics. Transcription between predicate logic and English. Models, truth-trees, and derivations. Identity, functions, and definite descriptions. Introduction to concepts of metatheory.
112.prereq_text: PHI 012 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

121.title: Bioethics
121.description: In-depth coverage of topics in bioethics including resource allocation, measures of health and disease/disability, public health, and ethical issues related to research on human subjects and emerging technologies.

134.title: Modal Logic
134.description: Survey of the main systems of modal logic, including Lewis systems S4 and S5. Possible worlds semantics and formal proofs. Applications to epistemology, ethics, or temporality.
134.prereq_text: PHI 112 or MAT 108 or MAT 108V; or the equivalent.

137C.title: Philosophy of Language: Semantics & Pragmatics
137C.description: Philosophical issues and positions concerning the meaning and use of language. Topics include the distinction between meaning and implication, the roles of context and convention in language use, speaker meaning versus linguistic meaning and speech act theory.
137C.prereq_text: One course in Philosophy or Linguistics recommended.

175.title: Kant
175.description: Immanuel Kant's Critique of Pure Reason and related writings. Topics include the nature of human cognition, space and time, a priori concepts, substance, causality, human freedom, and the existence of God.

189A.title: Special Topics in Philosophy: History of Philosophy
189A.description: Special topics in History of Philosophy.
189A.prereq_text: One course in the area of the special topic recommended.

189H.title: Special Topics in Philosophy: Philosophy of Mind
189H.description: Special topics in Philosophy of Mind.
189H.prereq_text: One course in the area of the special topic recommended.

194HA.title: Honors Research Project
194HA.description: Completion of honors research project under direction of an instructor. Consult departmental major advisor for list of instructors available in a given quarter.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to students who are members of the honors program in Philosophy.

194HB.title: Research Project
194HB.description: Completion of honors research project under direction of an instructor. Consult departmental major advisor for list of instructors available in a given quarter.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to students who are members of the honors program in Philosophy.

200A.title: Proseminar I
200A.description: Intensive study of core works in a selected area of philosophy. Intensive experience in philosophical writing, discussion, and presentation of written work.

210.title: Philosophy of Science
210.description: Treatment of one or more general topics of current interest in philosophy of science. Topics may include scientific explanation, theories of confirmation, scientific realism, reduction in physics and biology.
210.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

214.title: Ethics
214.description: Topics may include morality and motivation, objectivity in ethics, the relationship between the factual and the moral. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
214.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

275.title: Kant
275.description: Intensive study of a topic in the philosophy of Kant, in such areas as metaphyics, theory of knowledge, ethics.
275.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

001A.title: Principles of Physics
001A.description: Mechanics. Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics with emphasis on applications in applied agricultural and biological sciences and in physical education.
001A.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have received credit for PHY 007B or PHY 009A.

007A.title: General Physics
007A.description: Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics for students majoring in a biological science.
007A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 001B or PHY 009B.
007A.prereq_text: MAT 016B (can be concurrent) or MAT 017B (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B (can be concurrent); completion or concurrent enrollment in MAT 017B or MAT 021B.

007B.title: General Physics
007B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 001A or PHY 009A.

007C.title: General Physics
007C.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 009C or PHY 005C.

009A.title: Classical Physics
009A.description: Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics for physical science and engineering majors. Classical mechanics.
009A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 001A or PHY 007B; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HA.
009A.prereq_text: MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better or MAT 021M C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 017B B or better.

009B.title: Classical Physics
009B.description: Continuation of PHY 009A. Fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, wave phenomena, optics.
009B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007A; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HB, PHY 009HC, or ENG 105.
009B.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); (MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better).

009C.title: Classical Physics
009C.description: Electricity and magnetism including circuits and Maxwell's equations.
009C.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007C; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HD.
009C.prereq_text: PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better; PHY 009B C- or better; MAT 021D C- or better.

009D.title: Modern Physics
009D.description: Introduction to physics concepts developed since 1900. Special relativity, quantum mechanics, atoms, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear and particle physics.
009D.prereq_text: PHY 009B C- or better; PHY 009C C- or better; (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); (MAT 022B (can be concurrent) or MAT 027B (can be concurrent))

009HA.title: Honors Physics
009HA.description: Classical mechanics. Same material as PHY 009A in greater depth. For students in physical sciences, mathematics, and engineering.
009HA.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007B; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009A.
009HA.prereq_text: MAT 021B (can be concurrent); or MAT 021BH (can be concurrent) or MAT 021M (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

009HD.title: Honors Physics
009HD.description: Electricity and magnetism. Continuation of Physics 009HC.
009HD.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009C.
009HD.prereq_text: PHY 009HB C- or better; PHY 009HC C- or better; MAT 021D C- or better.

040.title: Introduction to Computational Physics
040.description: Introduction to programming with examples from numerical analysis and computational physics. Introduction to modern tools used for scientific analysis and computer algebra.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Primary for lower division students.

104A.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods in Physics
104A.description: Introduction to mathematics used in upper division physics courses, including applications of vector spaces, Fourier analysis, and partial differential equations.
104A.prereq_text: (PHY 009C C- or better or PHY 009HD C- or better); MAT 021D C- or better; (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better); PHY 040 (can be concurrent).

104C.title: Intermediate Methods of Mathematical Physics
104C.description: Applications of complex analysis, conditional probability, integral transformations and other advanced topics.
104C.prereq_text: PHY 104A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

112.title: Thermodynamics & Statistical Mechanics
112.description: Introduction to classical and quantum statistical mechanics and their connections with thermodynamics. Theory is developed for the ideal gas model and simple magnetic models and then extended to studies of solids, quantum fluids, and chemical equilibria.
112.prereq_text: (PHY 009B C- or better or PHY 009HB C- or better); (PHY 009D C- or better or PHY 009HC C- or better); PHY 104A C- or better; PHY 115A (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

112L.title: Computational Physics Lab for Statistical Mechanics
112L.description: Applications of computational physics to problems from statistical mechanics.
112L.prereq_text: PHY 040 C- or better; (PHY 045 C- or better or ECS 032C C- or better or ECS 036B C- or better); (PHY 112 (can be concurrent) or CHE 110C (can be concurrent)); or consent of instructor.

115A.title: Foundation of Quantum Mechanics
115A.description: Introduction to the methods of quantum mechanics with applications to atomic, molecular, solid state, nuclear and elementary particle physics.
115A.prereq_text: ((PHY 009C C- or better, PHY 009D C- or better) or (PHY 009HC C- or better, PHY 009HD C- or better)); PHY 104A C- or better; PHY 105A C- or better; or consent of department.

117.title: Physics Instrumentation with Analog & Digital Electronics
117.description: Experimental and theoretical study of important electronic circuits involving analog and digital components. Feedback, amplifiers, oscillators, noise, integrated circuits, digital logic, timers, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters.
117.credit_limit_text: 2 units of credit if student has taken PHY 116A. No credit if student has taken PHY 116B.

122A.title: Advanced Laboratory in Condensed Matter Physics
122A.description: Experimental techniques and measurements in solid-state physics. Three-six experiments performed depending on difficulty. Individual work is stressed. Thorough write-ups of the experiments are required.
122A.prereq_text: PHY 080 C- or better; PHY 110A C- or better; PHY 115A C- or better; PHY 110B C- or better (can be concurrent); PHY 112 C- or better (can be concurrent); PHY 115B recommended (can be concurrent).

152.title: Galactic Structure & the Interstellar Medium
152.description: Structure, contents, and formation of our Milky Way galaxy, viz. its shape and size, the nature of the interstellar medium, stellar populations, rotation curves, mass determination and evidence of dark matter.
152.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); (PHY 009B C- or better or PHY 009HC C- or better); (PHY 009C C- or better or PHY 009HD C- or better); PHY 040 (can be concurrent); PHY 105A (can be concurrent); MAT 022B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

190.title: Careers in Physics
190.description: Overview of important research areas in physics, discussions of research opportunities and internships, strategies for graduate school and industrial careers, the fellowship and assistantship selection process, preparation of resumes, personal statements, and letters of recommendation.

195.title: Senior Thesis
195.description: Open only to Physics and Applied Physics majors with senior standing. Preparation of a senior thesis on a topic selected by the student with approval of the department.

197T.title: Tutoring in Physics & Astronomy
197T.description: Tutoring of students in lower division courses. Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses. Weekly meeting with instructor.

200A.title: Theory of Mechanics & Electromagnetics
200A.description: Theoretical approaches in classical mechanics including the use of generalized coordinates and virtual work; variational calculus; Lagrange equations; symmetries, conservation laws, and Noether theorem; Lagrangian density; Hamilton formalism; canonical transformations; Poisson brackets; and Hamilton-Jacobi equations.
200A.prereq_text: PHY 204A (can be concurrent); PHY 104B; PHY 105B; PHY 110C; or equivalent to PHY 110C; PHY 204A required concurrently.

200B.title: Theory of Mechanics & Electromagnetics
200B.description: Theoretical approaches in electromagnetics including static electromagnetic fields; Maxwell's equations; plane waves in various media; magnetohydrodynamics; diffraction theory; radiating systems; and special relativity.
200B.prereq_text: PHY 104A B or better; PHY 110B B or better; or graduate standing in Physics and Astronomy.

215A.title: Quantum Mechanics
215A.description: Formal development and interpretation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics; its application to atomic, nuclear, molecular, and solid-state problems; brief introduction to relativistic quantum mechanics and the Dirac equation.

230B.title: Quantum Theory of Fields
230B.description: Continuation of 230A, with selected advanced topics, such as S-matrix theory, dispersion relations, axiomatic formulations.

233.title: Advanced Topics in Geometry & Physics
233.description: Modern geometric methods in theoretical physics, with topics ranging from pseudo-Riemannian differential geometry and topology with application to general relativity, black holes, and string theory.
233.prereq_text: PHY 230A, PHY 230B, PHY 230C, & PHY 260 or equivalent strongly recommended.

240B.title: Condensed Matter Physics B
240B.description: Topics in condensed matter physics: transport and optical properties of metals and quantum structures; experimental measurement the Fermi surface and of phonon spectra.

245A.title: High-Energy Physics
245A.description: Phenomenology and systematics of strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions of hadrons and leptons; determination of quantum numbers; quarks and quarkonia; deep inelastic scattering; the quark parton model; experiments at hadron colliders and electron-positron colliders.

252B.title: Techniques of Experimental Physics
252B.description: Introduction to techniques and methods of designing and executing experiments. Problems and examples from nuclear and particle research will be utilized.

265.title: High Energy Astrophysics & Radiative Processes
265.description: Survey covering galactic and extragalactic X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy, radiative processes, and techniques of high-energy astrophysics.
265.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

270.title: Current Topics in Physics Research
270.description: Reading and discussion to help physics graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in their immediate field of research and related areas.
270.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar in Physics
290.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in physics. Topics will vary weekly and will cover a broad spectrum of the active fields of physics research at a level accessible to all physics graduate students.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

291.title: Seminar in Nuclear Physics
291.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in nuclear physics.
291.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

292A.title: Seminar in Elementary Particle Physics
292A.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in elementary particle physics.
292A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

292B.title: High Energy Frontier Initiative & Cosmology Theory Seminar
292B.description: Weekly seminar on current issues in Particle physics and Cosmology.

293.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
293.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in condensed matter physics.
293.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

294.title: Seminar in Cosmology
294.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in Cosmology.
294.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

296.title: Field, Strings, & Gravity Seminar
296.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in the areas of quantum field theory, string theory and gravity.

200A.title: PBGG Core Course Series–Fall quarter
200A.description: The first of three PBGG graduate core courses. Coverage includes (1) plant genes, (2) biotechnology, (3) genomes and gene flow, (4) principles of plant systematics, and (5) the evolution of flowering plants.
200A.prereq_text: Graduate standing; a broad background of undergraduate level coursework in Plant Biology is recommended.

212.title: Physiology of Herbicidal Action
212.description: Study of the fundamental processes involved in the physiological action of herbicides. Detailed consideration of the fate of herbicides in plants.

290A.title: Faculty Seminar
290A.description: Discussion of research area of seminar speakers in Plant Biology Graduate Group Seminar Series.

290B.title: Seminar
290B.description: Seminars presented by visiting scientists on research topics of current interest.

291.title: Graduate Student Seminar in Plant Biology
291.description: Student-given seminars on topics in plant biology, with critiques by instructor and peers. How to give a seminar, including preparation of visual and other teaching aids. Topic determined by instructor in charge.

292.title: Seminars in Plants Biology
292.description: Review of current literature in botanical disciplines. Disciplines and special subjects to be announced quarterly. Present and analyze assigned topics.

297T.title: Tutoring in Plant Biology
297T.description: Offers graduate students, particularly those not serving as teaching assistants, the opportunity to gain teaching experience.

390.title: The Teaching of Plant Biology
390.description: Consideration of the problems of teaching botany, especially of preparing for and conducting discussions, guiding student laboratory work, and the formulation of questions and topics for examinations.
390.prereq_text: Graduate standing; concurrent appointment as a teaching assistant in Plant Biology.

005.title: Foundations in Plant Biology
005.description: Active areas of research in the Plant Biology department. Navigation of the Plant Biology major, campus resources, and career perspectives.

090X.title: Plant Science Seminar
090X.description: Examination of a special topic in a small group setting.
090X.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLS 090X.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Technical and/or professional experience on or off campus. Supervised by a member of the Plant Biology faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

105.title: Developmental Plant Anatomy
105.description: Structural anatomy of vascular plants. Training in basic tissue sectioning, staining, and use of the compound microscope.
105.prereq_text: BIS 002C; or other similar preparation in plant biology.

111.title: Plant Physiology
111.description: Plant cell as a functional unit. The processes of absorption, movement, and utilization of water and minerals. Water loss, translocation, photosynthesis, respiration.
111.prereq_text: (BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C); (CHE 008B (can be concurrent) or CHE 118B (can be concurrent)); PHY 007C (can be concurrent); PLB 105 recommended.

117.title: Plant Ecology
117.description: Study of the interactions between plants, plant populations or vegetation types and their physical and biological environment. Special emphasis on California. Four full-day field trips and brief write-up of class project required.
117.prereq_text: (BIS 002A, BIS 002B, BIS 002C) or (BIO 001 or BIO 002, BIO 003); PLB 111 recommended.

148.title: Introductory Mycology
148.description: Systematics, ecology, evolution, and morphology of fungi. Importance of fungi to humans.
148.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003).

190C.title: Research Conference in Plant Biology
190C.description: Introduction to research methods in plant biology. Design of field or laboratory research projects, survey of appropriate literature, and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Plant Biology or related discipline.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Technical and/or professional experience on or off campus.  Supervised by a member of the Plant Biology Department faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description:
Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior
thesis.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open only to majors of senior standing on honors list.

197T.title: Tutoring in Plant Biology
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

120.title: Introduction to Plant Pathology
120.description: The nature, cause, and control of plant diseases.
120.prereq_text: BIS 002C; or consent of instructor; MIC 102 recommended.

148.title: Introductory Mycology
148.description: Systematics, ecology, evolution, and morphology of fungi. Importance of fungi to humans.
148.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003).

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus, supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: PLP 120; and consent of instructor.

201A.title: Impacts, Mechanisms & Control of Plant Disease
201A.description: Case-studies approach to analysis of plant diseases caused by bacteria, fungi, oomycetes, and viruses, including impacts, etiology, pathogen taxonomy and epidemiology, biochemical and genetic aspects of pathogen-host interactions, virulence and resistance, and approaches to disease control.
201A.prereq_text: PLP 120; graduate student status in the Plant Pathology Graduate Program or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Review and evaluation of current research in plant pathology.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation, evaluation, and critical discussions of research activities in the area of advanced plant pathology; primarily designed for graduate students.

002.title: Botany & Physiology of Cultivated Plants
002.description: Holistic introduction to the underlying botanical and physiological principles of cultivated plants and their response to the environment. Includes concepts behind plant selection, cultivation, and utilization. Laboratories include discussion and interactive demonstrations.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have complete AMR 002. (Former AMR 002.)
002.prereq_text: High school course in biology and chemistry recommended.

003.title: Seminar: Overview of the Plant Sciences Major
003.description: Introduction to topics covered in the core courses and areas of specialization within the Plant Sciences major. Research and internship opportunities and potential career paths in plant breeding, crop management and ecology, horticulture, precision agriculture, crop quality and safety, ecosystem management and restoration, and related fields.

007V.title: Just Coffee: The Biology, Ecology & Socioeconomic Impacts of the World's Favorite Drink
007V.description: Coffee used as a case study to examine biological, ecological and social factors influencing sustainability of farming systems and how food production systems impact human well-being.

012.title: Plants & Society
012.description: Dependence of human societies on plant and plant products. Plants as resources for food, fiber, health, enjoyment and environmental services. Sustainable uses of plants for food production, raw materials, bioenergy, and environmental conservation. Global population growth and future food supplies.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have complete PLB 012. (Former PLB 012.)

013.title: Chocolate, Covered: The Past, Present, & Future of Cacao
013.description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on the crop that gives us chocolate. History, genetics, agronomy, sensory science, and economics of cacao production.

015.title: Introduction to Sustainable Agriculture
015.description: Multidisciplinary introduction to agricultural sustainability with a natural sciences emphasis.  Sustainability concepts and perspectives.  Agricultural evolution, history, resources and functions.  Diverse agricultural systems and practices and their relative sustainability.  Laboratories provide direct experience with selected agricultural practices and systems.

021.title: Application of Computers in Technology
021.description: Concepts of computing and applications using personal computers, spreadsheets, database management, word processing and communications.

021V.title: Application of Computers in Technology
021V.description: Concepts of computing and applications using personal computers, spreadsheets, database management, word processing and communications.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience on or off campus in subject areas pertaining to plant and environmental sciences.  Internship supervised by a faculty member.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; primarily for lower division students.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; primarily for lower division students.

105.title: Concepts in Pest Management
105.description: Introduction to the ecological principles of integrated pest management, biology of different classes of pests and the types of losses they cause, population assessment, evaluation of advantages and disadvantages of different techniques used for pest management, IPM programs.
105.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed AMR 105. (Former AMR 105.)

111.title: Principles of Crop Production
111.description: Principles, practices and technologies of agronomic cropping systems, including crop systematics, physiology, agroecology, equipment, and management. Cropping systems analysis and integration of economic and ecological decision-making considerations involved in crop production.
111.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLS 110A. (Former PLS 110A.)

120.title: Applied Statistics in Agricultural Sciences
120.description: Application of statistical methods to design and analysis of research trials for plant, animal, behavioral, nutritional, and consumer sciences.  Basic concepts and statistical methods are presented in lectures, laboratories emphasize data processing techniques, problem solving, and interpretation in specialized fields.
120.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed AMR 120. (Former AMR 120.)

144.title: Trees & Forests
144.description: Biological structure and function of trees as organisms; understanding of forests as communities and as ecosystems; use of forests by humans; tree phenology, photosynthesis, respiration, soil processes, life histories, dormancy, forest biodiversity, and agroforestry.
144.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 144 or ENH 144 or ERS 144. (Formerly PLB 144, ENH 144, ERS 144.)

152.title: Plant Genetics
152.description: Basic principles of transmission genetics, cytogenetics, population and quantitative genetics, and molecular genetics.  Practical aspects of genetic crosses and analysis of segregating populations.
152.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have completed PLB 152. (Former PLB 152.)
152.prereq_text: BIS 001A or BIS 002A; or consent of instructor.

189L.title: Laboratory Research in Plant Sciences
189L.description: Formulating experimental approaches to current questions in plant science; performance of proposed experiments.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the plant sciences.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in subject areas pertaining to plant and environmental sciences. Internship supervised by a faculty member.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Senior Honors Thesis
194H.description: Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior thesis.
194H.prereq_text: Senior standing; overall GPA of 3.250 or higher and consent of master advisor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Plant Sciences
197T.description: Leading small voluntary discussion or lab groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing, completion of course being tutored or the equivalent.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

206.title: Applied Multivariate Modeling in Agricultural & Environmental Sciences
206.description: Multivariate linear and nonlinear models. Model selection and parameter estimation. Analysis of manipulative and observational agroecological experiments. Discriminant, principal component, and path analyses. Logistic and biased regression. Bootstrapping. Exercises based on actual research by UC Davis students.
206.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have complete AGR 206. (Former AGR 206.)

220.title: Genomics & Biotechnology of Plant Improvement
220.description: Integration of modern biotechnology and classical plant breeding including the impact of structural, comparative and functional genomics on gene discovery, characterization and exploitation. Covers molecular markers, plant transformation, hybrid production, disease resistance, and novel output traits.
220.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed VCR 220. (Former VCR 220.)
220.prereq_text: BIS 101 or BIS 101V; or the equivalent.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Topics of current interest related to Plant Sciences.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Research conference.

297T.title: Tutoring in Plant Sciences
297T.description: Designed for graduate students who desire teaching experience but are not teaching assistants.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing; completion of course to be tutored or the equivalent.

002.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
002.description: Introduction to basic concepts in political analysis and application of them in comparative studies of selected countries. Coverage is given to cultural and other informal dimensions of politics as well as to more formal political and governmental structures.

003.title: International Relations
003.description: International conflict and cooperation, including the Cold War, nuclear weapons, and new techniques for understanding international politics.

007V.title: Introduction to Law & Politics
007V.description: Introduction to the judicial process and constitutional law. Judicial interpretation, rights litigation, key constitutional amendments, and the sociopolitical forces that have prompted constitutional change.

011AV.title: America Decides: Who Will Win This Year's Election?
011AV.description: Current election events against backdrop of research-based exploration of factors influencing elections. Candidate nominations, campaign strategy, campaign finance, media coverage, and voter decision-making.

012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

051.title: Scientific Study of Politics
051.description: Introduction to the basic principles of the scientific study of politics. Research design and empirical analysis of data with applications to different methodological approaches and different substantive areas in political science.

104.title: California State Government & Politics
104.description: California political system. Political culture, constitution, elections and parties, direct democracy, legislature, governor, executive branch, courts, finances, state-local relations and policy issues.

109.title: Public Policy & the Governmental Process
109.description: Processes of formulating public policy, including individual and collective decision making, political exchange, competition, bargaining, coalition formation and the allocation of public goods, resources and opportunities.

114.title: Quantitative Analysis of Political Data
114.description: Logic and methods of analyzing quantitative political data. Topics covered include central tendency, probability, correlation, and non-parametric statistics. Particular emphasis will be placed on understanding the use of statistics in political science research.

116.title: Foundations of Political Thought
116.description: Analysis and evaluation of the seminal works of a major political philosopher or of a major problem in political philosophy.

118A.title: History of Political Theory:  Ancient
118A.description: Critical analyses of classical and medieval political philosophers such as Plato, Aristotle, Cicero and St. Thomas.

118B.title: History of Political Theory: Early Modern
118B.description: Critical analysis of the works of early modern political philosophers such as Machiavelli, Montaigne, Hobbes, Locke and Hume.

121.title: Scientific Study of War
121.description: Analysis of political processes involved in the initiation, conduct and termination of modern interstate warfare.

122.title: International Law
122.description:
Selected topics in international law; territory, sovereign immunity,
responsibility, the peaceful settlement or nonsettlement of international disputes.

123.title: The Politics of Interdependence
123.description: In the past several decades, growing economic interdependence has generated new problems in international relations. Deals with difficulties in managing complex interdependence and its implication on national policies and politics.

131.title: Analysis of U.S. Foreign Policy
131.description: Detailed presentation and examination of the formulation of execution of U.S. foreign policy. Survey of numerous factors influencing policy outcomes and how such determinants vary according to policy issue areas.

140D.title: When Institutions Fail
140D.description: Examination of factors contributing to the success and failure of political institutions.

151.title: Constitutional Politics of the First Amendment & the Right to Privacy.
151.description: Constitutional politics surrounding such issues as the right to free expression, associational rights, the right to free exercise of religious beliefs and the right to privacy.

168.title: Latino Politics
168.description: Political aspects of Latino life in America; examines the political role of Latinos as it has been historically defined by different groups in society and the responses of Latinos to their political environment.

174.title: Political Economy
174.description: Relationship between government, political institutions and the economy. Relationship between capitalism and democracy, economic inequality, electoral accountability, distributive politics, immigration, and climate policy. Empirical research and political responses to economic changes.

192B.title: Internship in Public Affairs
192B.description: Supervised internship and study in political, governmental, or related organizations.
192B.prereq_text: POL 192A; consent of instructor; highest priority assigned to students with Political Science-Public Service major; upper division standing.

193.title: Research in Practical Politics
193.description: Supervised preparation of an extensive paper relating internship experience to concepts, literature, and theory of political science.
193.prereq_text: POL 192A; POL 192B; open only to Political Science-Public Service majors, for whom it is required.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of Instructor; upper division standing.

211.title: Research Methods in Political Science
211.description: Introductory seminar on the foundations of probability theory and mathematical statistics that are critical to empirical investigations in political science.

214A.title: Research in Political Science
214A.description: Research seminar sequence required of all PhD students. Design, execution, and defense of an original piece of research in political science, culminating in a paper of publishable quality.

215.title: Introduction to Modeling Political Behavior
215.description: Introduction to formal and game theoretic analyses of politics. Students will learn basic game theory and modeling skills. We examine the benefits of modeling, and look at examples of formal analysis in a variety of political science sub-fields.

242.title: Seminar in Comparative Politics
242.description: Systematic survey of theories and methods used in the study of comparative politics.
242.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

274.title: Political Economy
274.description: Politics of economic policy as reflected in taxation, spending and regulation; impact of prices, employment, and growth on political demands; government responses to economic conditions; electoral politics and the political business cycle.

290A.title: Research in American Government & Public Policy
290A.description: Special research seminar on problems and issues in the study of American government and public policy.

290B.title: Research in Political Theory
290B.description: Special research seminar on problems and issues in the study of political theory.

290C.title: Research in International Relations
290C.description: Special research seminar on select problems and issues in the study of international relations.

297.title: Internships in Political Science
297.description: Application and evaluation of theoretical concepts through work experience or systematic observation in public and political agencies.
297.prereq_text: Open only to persons who have internships or other positions in governmental agencies, political parties, etc.

201.title: Principles of Population Biology
201.description: Principles of single-species ecology and evolution. Ecological and evolutionary processes shaping population dynamics and genetic and phenotypic variation within species. Modeling, experimental, and molecular approaches to population biology.
201.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken PBG 200A.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis graduate students and faculty.

290C.title: Research Conference in Population Biology
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in population biology.
290C.prereq_text: PBG 299 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor. Graduate standing; PBG 299 required concurrently.

292.title: Topics in Ecology & Evolution
292.description: Seminar presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty and graduate students.

001.title: Elementary Portuguese
001.description: Introduction to Portuguese grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001.credit_limit_text: Students who have successfully completed POR 002 or POR 003 in the 10th or higher grade of high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and Department Chairperson.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Independent study with professor for advanced undergraduate students, or honor thesis students.

201.title: Financial Reporting
201.description: Coverage includes the fundamentals of accounting and reporting economic events and transactions. Emphasizes the preparation of balance sheets, income statements, statements of cash flow, and statements of stockholders’ equity.
201.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGB 200A or MGP 200A or MGT 200A.

211.title: Tax Reporting & Analysis
211.description: Introduction to the taxation of business entities and their related transactions, with an emphasis on the details of tax law and tax reporting requirements. Topics include individual, partnership, and corporate taxation, as well as tax theory.
211.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MGB 264 or MGP 264 or MGT 264.

251.title: Managerial Accounting & Controls
251.description: Analysis of management accounting systems including cost accounting, performance measurement, and compensation and reward systems. Focuses on the production of information useful for managerial decision-making, as well as the design of these systems.
251.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MGB 271 or MGP 271 or MGT 271.

253.title: Accounting Information & Control Systems
253.description: Analysis of information systems used for accounting, recordkeeping, and control. Topics include the regulatory requirements of accounting control systems as well as their implementation and auditing considerations.
253.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGB 271 or MGP 271 or MGT 271.

271.title: Accounting Ethics
271.description: Analysis of accountants' professional responsibilities and ethics. Topics include the behavioral foundations of ethics in a business environment, how those elements affect accountants' integrity, objectivity, and independence. Professional standards related to accountants' conduct are also covered.

298.title: Directed Group Study for Graduate Students
298.description: Directed group study for graduate students.

418.title: Off-Campus Clinical Experience
418.description: Clinical or research elective in off-campus medical school or mental health setting. Arrangements made with advance approval of the instructor and individual in charge of off-campus setting.
418.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; fourth-year medical students.

001.title: General Psychology
001.description: Introduction to empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

001Y.title: General Psychology
001Y.description: Introduction to empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

041.title: Research Methods in Psychology
041.description: Introduction to experimental design, interviews, questionnaires, field and observational methods, reliability, and statistical inference.
041.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 strongly recommended.

100.title: Introduction to Cognitive Psychology
100.description: Introduction to human information processing, mental representation and transformation, imagery, attention, memory, language processing, concept formation, problem solving, and computer simulation.
100.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

101.title: Introduction to Biological Psychology
101.description: Survey and integration of the relationships between behavior and biological processes, including physiology, genes, development, ecology, and evolution.
101.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for those students who have completed NPB 100.

103A.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Data
103A.description: Design and statistical analysis of psychological investigations and the interpretation of quantitative data in psychology.
103A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 103.
103A.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

113.title: Developmental Psychobiology
113.description: The biology of behavioral development; survey and integration of the organismic and environmental processes that regulate the development of behavior.

120.title: Agent-Based Modeling
120.description: Introduction to agent-based computer simulation and analysis with emphasis on learning how to model animals, including humans, to achieve insight into social and group behavior.

126.title: Health Psychology
126.description: Psychological factors influencing health and illness. Topics include stress and coping, personality and health, symptom perception and reporting, heart disease, cancer, compliance, and health maintenance and promotion.
126.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 160.
126.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 101 recommended.

130.title: Human Learning and Memory
130.description: Consideration of major theories of human learning and memory with critical examination of relevant experimental data.
130.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100); or consent of instructor.

131.title: Perception
131.description: Cognitive organizations related to measurable physical energy changes mediated through sensory channels. Perception of objects, space, motion, events.
131.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135).

134.title: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience
134.description: Explorations of how brain secretes mind, via computer simulations that are manipulated and probed to investigate how neurons produce perception, attention, memory, language, and cognitive control.
134.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 100 or PSC 101 or PSC 135 recommended.

135.title: Cognitive Neuroscience: The Biological Foundations of the Mind
135.description: Neuroscientific foundations of higher mental processes including attention, memory, language, higher-level perceptual and motor processes, and consciousness. Emphasis on the neural mechanisms which form the substrates of human cognition and the relationship of mind to brain. May be taught abroad.
135.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); or consent of instructor; PSC 101 or PSC 121 recommended.

136.title: Psychology of Music
136.description: Introduction to the mental and neural representations of musical structures and processes involved in perceiving, remembering, and performing music. Music and emotion.
136.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135 or MUS 006C); or consent of instructor.

140Y.title: Developmental Psychology
140Y.description: Ontogenetic account of human behavior through adolescence with emphasis on motor skills, mental abilities, motivation, and social interaction.
140Y.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B; not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 112. (Former PSC 112.)
140Y.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

141.title: Cognitive Development
141.description: Theories, methods, evidence, and debates in the field of cognitive development, such as nature/nurture, constraints on learning, and the role of plasticity. Topics include attention, memory, concepts about the physical and social world, and language.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HDE 101.
141.prereq_text: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100B or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV.

142.title: Social & Personality Development
142.description: Social and personality development of children, infancy through adolescence. Topics include the development of personality, achievement motivation, self-understanding, sex-role identity, and antisocial behavior. Emphasis on the interface between biological and social factors.
142.prereq_text: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV.

148.title: Developmental Disorders
148.description: Current scientific knowledge of the influences of biological, cognitive, and environmental factors on the emergence of disorders with onset in childhood.  Examples include autism spectrum, ADD/ADHD, dyslexia and dyscalculia.  Emphasis placed on understanding these disorders, their causes and their treatments.
148.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or PSC 141 or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV).

150.title: Relationship Science: Lust, Love, & Evolution
150.description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 051.
150.prereq_text: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V; PSC 041 recommended.

151V.title: Social Psychology
151V.description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
151V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 145.
151V.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 041 recommended.

152.title: Social Cognition
152.description: Examines how social factors influence how we attend to, encode, and process information and how these mental processes affect subsequent judgments and behavior.
152.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

157.title: Stereotyping, Prejudice, & Stigma
157.description: Social psychological underpinnings of stereotyping, prejudice, and stigma from sociocultural, motivational, and cognitive perspectives. Topics include: origins, maintenance, change, effects on person perception and memory, and the automaticity/controllability of stereotyping and prejudice.
157.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

162.title: Introduction to Personality Psychology
162.description: Scientific study of personality. Methods of personality research. Overview of current research and theory in the field of personality psychology.
162.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 147.
162.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

168.title: Mental Health, Mental Illness, & Problems in Living
168.description: Overview of psychological disorders and psychological conditions that lead to problems in daily living, with consideration of causes, classification systems, and treatment.
168.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

169.title: The Science of Multi-Cultural Psychology
169.description: Effects of culture and ethnicity on psychological processes, such as social cognition, emotion, motivation, personality, self-concept, and interpersonal behavior (i.e., how culture makes who you are). Individuals' construction of multicultural identity and experiences.
169.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

182.title: Methods in Laboratory Research
182.description: Training in specific lab-based research methods coupled with hands-on experience in a research lab. Students assessed on their ability report and interpret research findings. Content varies from quarter to quarter.

185.title: History of Psychology
185.description: Development of psychological thought and research in context of history of philosophy and science.
185.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 120. (Former PSC 120.)
185.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); upper division standing or consent of instructor.

190.title: Seminar in Psychology
190.description: Intensive treatment of a special topic or problem of psychological interest.
190.prereq_text: Junior or senior standing; major in Psychology or consent of instructor.

192.title: Fieldwork in Psychology
192.description: Supervised internship off and on campus, in community and institutional settings. Maximum of 6 units may be used towards satisfaction of upper division major requirement.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Psychology.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed research. Supervised reading, research and writing leading to submission of a Senior Honors thesis under the direction of faculty sponsor.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Psychology and qualifications for admission into college honors program; at least one course from PSC 180A, PSC 180B, PSC 180C or PSC 199 strongly recommended.

200.title: Proseminar in Psychology
200.description: Introduces matriculating graduate students to research activities of departmental faculty.
200.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

202.title: Research Seminar
202.description: Presentation of graduate research to program faculty and graduate students.

204A.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Experiments
204A.description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing using standard parametric and correlational approaches. Analysis of variance, factorial and repeated measures, and tests of trends.
204A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 206.
204A.prereq_text: STA 102; or equivalent; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

218A.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
218A.description: Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.
218A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division undergraduate introduction to the biology of behavior, such as PSC 101, PSC 122, PSC 123, NPB 102, NPB 150, NPB 152, WFC 141, ENT 104, or ANS 105.

263.title: Topics in Cognitive Psychology
263.description: Selected topics in language processing, memory, perception, problem solving, and thinking, with an emphasis on the common underlying cognitive processes.
263.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

270.title: Topics in Personality & Social Psychology
270.description: Critical study of a selected area of personality or social psychology.
270.prereq_text: Graduate student standing or consent of instructor.

271A.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271A.description: Core concepts and methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity. Behavioral paradigms and measurement approaches in human and animal studies of learning and plasticity, as well as a consideration of the functional, anatomical and neuronal mechanisms underlying brain plasticity.
271A.prereq_text: Graduate Standing or consent of instructor.

289A.title: Current Research in Psychology
289A.description: Contemporary theory and empirical research in specialized topics in psychology. Topics include developmental attachment, social neuroscience, mental health, emotion, sexual orientation and identity.
289A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar devoted to a highly specific research topic in any area of basic psychology. Special topic selected for a quarter will vary depending on interests of instructor and students.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

391.title: Teaching of Psychology Practicum
391.description: Supervised teaching in undergraduate classrooms. Techniques for delivering content through lectures, discussions, or labs; course administration; communications; assessment of student learning; solving ethical problems; instructional technology.

101.title: Introduction to Public Health
101.description: Provide basic concepts and controversies in public health, basic science of public health, social and behavioral factors in health and disease, environmental and occupational health issues, the relationship of public health to the medical care system and health care reform.

113.title: Health Disparities in the U.S.
113.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of health disparities research.

120.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
120.description: Introduction to concepts of health informatics and the impacts of the field on healthcare, research and public health.
120.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

190.title: Topics in Public Health
190.description: Seminar on key issues and current topics in public health.

244.title: Introduction to Medical Statistics
244.description: Introduction to statistical methods and software in clinical, laboratory, and population medicine. Graphical and tabular presentation of data; probability, binomial, Poisson, normal, t-, F-, and Chi-square distributions; one and two sample t-test; elementary nonparametric methods; simple linear regression; and correlation.
244.prereq_text: SPH 281; or ability to read a dataset such as a .csv file into SAS and to do data steps (label variables, format values, create new variables) and create summary measures (frequencies and means) in SAS.

299.title: Research in Community & International Health
299.description: Work with faculty member in areas of research interest, including but not limited to injury control, international health, health policy, occupational and environmental health, health promotion and wellness, women's health, and health demographics.

192.title: Internship in Pulmonary Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in pulmonary medicine.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

299.title: Pulmonary Disease Research
299.description: Pulmonary disease research activity with focus in inhalation toxicity, oxidants or lung biochemistry, and cell and molecular biology.
299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; by arrangement only.

001.title: Elementary Punjabi
001.description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.

001V.title: Elementary Punjabi
001V.description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.

021.title: Intermediate Punjabi
021.description: Integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in formal and informal contexts in Intermediate Punjabi. Continuation of fluency acquisition through grammar, vocabulary, and meaningful verbal and written expressions in Punjabi. Short readings and essays in Punjabi literature and culture.

211.title: Introduction to Radiation Oncology Physics
211.description: Introduction to radiation oncology physics. Overview of treatment methodologies. Medical physics equipment. Treatment machine dosimetry, including calibration. Machine quality assurance. Patient dosimetry. Treatment planning. Simulation and treatment. Treatment quality assurance, including calculation checks and chart checks. Brachytherapy.
211.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; restricted to physics and engineering graduate students and senior undergraduate physics majors.

299.title: Independent Study & Research
299.description: Research under supervision of Radiation Oncology faculty. Work must be appropriate to fulfill the requirements for the Ph.D. degree.
299.prereq_text: Enrollment with a graduate group for Ph.D. candidacy and consent of group advisor and sponsor.

473.title: Advanced Clinical Clerkship in Neuroradiology
473.description: Work with Neuroradiologists in image interpretation of CT, MRI, and fluoroscopy. Opportunity to participate in assessment of Neurointerventional patients, and to observe Neurointerventional procedures. Daily conferences in Neuroimaging, General Radiology, Health Physics, and Radiology Safety. Assigned readings.
473.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 3 units for two weeks; 6 units for four weeks.
473.prereq_text: Fourth-year medical student with interest in Diagnostic Radiology, Neuroradiology, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Psychiatry, Psychology, or related field; satisfactory completion of RDI 461, or the equivalent, is strongly encouraged.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

299.title: Research: Special Study for Graduate Students

001B.title: Death & Afterlife
001B.description: Introduction to comparative religion, focusing on the theme of death and the afterlife in different religious traditions.
001B.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken RST 003B.

011.title: Ethical Eating
011.description: Introduction to the complex and varied ethical, religious, and cultural meanings that food has had across the centuries and globe.

060.title: Introduction to Islam
060.description: Introduction to topics central to the Islamic tradition. Muhammad, the Qur'an, Islamic law, theology, philosophy, cosmology, worship, and mysticism. Race and gender in Islam, Islamic revival, and varying experiences of Islam in different historical and cultural settings.

103.title: Medieval & Byzantine Christianity
103.description: Christianity in Europe and the Near East from the year 600 to 1450. Focus on the development of Catholic and Orthodox traditions in ritual, art, and thought, with attention to interactions between regional groups, and Christian interaction with Islam.

144.title: History of the Bible
144.description: History of the formation of the Christian biblical canon, with emphasis on differences between Christian traditions; survey of translations and adaptations of biblical narrative in Christianity, Judaism, and Islam, as well as in contemporary culture.

171.title: Buddhist Art
171.description: A historical survey of Buddhist art in relation to the development of Buddhist doctrine and philosophy.

099.title: Directed Research Immunology
099.description: Independent research will be encouraged in basic immunology, including the role of the cellular immune system in oncogenesis.

192.title: Internship in Rheumatology-Allergy
192.description: Supervised work experience in rheumatology-allergy.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

199.title: Directed Research in Immunology
199.description: Independent research will be encouraged in basic immunology, including the role of the cellular immune system in oncogenesis.

298.title: Topics in Rheumatology & Clinical Immunology
298.description: Library and/or laboratory work as required.

299.title: Research in Autoimmune Disease
299.description:
Independent research will be encouraged in both animal models of human disease (including congenitally athymic [nude], asplenic, and New Zealand mice) and the cellular immune system of patients with systemic
lupus erythematosus, Sjögrens syndrome, polymyositis and drug hypersensitivity.

001.title: Elementary Russian
001.description: Introduction to Russian grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

004.title: Intermediate Russian
004.description: Grammar review and conversational practice in Russian.

101A.title: Advanced Russian
101A.description: Topics in Russian. Grammar for the advanced student. Reading and discussion of journalistic texts and classic and contemporary literature. Conversation exercises utilizing literary and colloquial variants of current Russian speech.

105.title: Advanced Russian Conversation
105.description: Intensive conversational practice and discussion based on current events and contemporary texts.

141.title: Tolstoy (in English)
141.description: Study of Leo Tolstoy's literary evolution and moral quest. Readings include his Confession, a major novel such as War and Peace or Anna Karenina, and representative shorter fiction.

002.title: Feeding the World: Influences on the Global Food Supply
002.description: Scientific principles and dynamic interactions involved in food production, food processing, nutrition, and agribusiness.  Physical, biological and social science issues influencing the availability and safety of the food supply worldwide.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken SAS 002V.

004Y.title: Water In Popular Culture
004Y.description: Analysis of the social construction of modern popular culture and its handling of the environment, focusing on water, as revealed through a survey of Hollywood and independent films.

012.title: Plants & Society
012.description: Dependence of human societies on plant and plant products. Plants as resources for food, fiber, health, enjoyment and environmental services. Sustainable uses of plants for food production, raw materials, bioenergy, and environmental conservation. Global population growth and future food supplies.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 012. (Former PLB 012.)

013.title: Disease & Society
013.description: Introduction to the concept of disease, the societal and personal impacts of past, present and future diseases, and the science behind disease discoveries, causes, evolution, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

090X.title: Lower Division Seminar
090X.description: Examination of a special topic in Science & Society through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, or special activities such as fieldwork, laboratory work, etc.
090X.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

092.title: Internship in Science & Society
092.description: Supervised internship on and off campus, in the community, or in institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

097T.title: Tutoring in Science & Society
097T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate Science & Society courses. Assisting with leading discussion groups under supervision of instructor(s) and teaching assistants. Acting as liaison between the students and course instructor(s) to foster effective communication and interaction.
097T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing; completion of course being tutored.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

109.title: Environmental Change, Disease & Public Health
109.description: Analysis of environmental changes from pre-history to the present and their influence on disease distribution, virulence and public health. Focus on critical study of many human-driven environmental changes and the accelerated transformation/spread of pathogens under globalization.
109.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HIS 109B.

192.title: Internship in Science & Society
192.description: Supervised internship on or off campus, in the community, or in institutional settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

390.title: Teaching Methods in Science & Society
390.description: Practical experience in methods and problems related to teaching Science & Society courses. Discussion of critical pedagogies specific to teaching of science-societal issues, preparing for and conducting discussion sessions, analyses of texts and supporting material, formulation of assignments, exams.

001.title: Introduction to Science, Technology & Medicine Studies
001.description: History, philosophy, sociology, politics, and cultural studies of science, technology, and medicine. Emphasis on a broad range of perspectives.

002Y.title: Introduction to the History of Science & Technology
002Y.description: Introduction to topics and methods of the history of science and technology. Emphasis on understanding the role of science and technology in the modern world through a long-term historical perspective.

009.title: Beautiful Data
009.description: Data visualizations and the idea of beauty using historical and contemporary examples from around the world. Data visualizations as rhetorical tools, conceptions of beauty, attractiveness, and elegance. Interdisciplinary interpretation of visual data and information.

012.title: Epidemics & Society
012.description: Epidemics in world history and the cultural impacts of contagious diseases. The roles of science, medicine, media, and the arts in shaping social conceptions of health and illness.

032.title: Drugs, Science & Culture
032.description: Drugs, politics, science, society in a cultural perspective: emphasis on roles of science, government and the media in shifting attitudes toward alcohol, marijuana, Prozac and other pharmaceuticals; drug laws, war on drugs and global trade in sugar, opium, cocaine.

040A.title: Media History 1: Gutenberg to Oppenheimer
040A.description: History of media to 1945, with particular focus on mechanically reproduced mass media technologies including the printing press, the newspaper, photography, cinema, radio and early computing technology. Analysis of interrelated cultural and political topics.

050.title: Ancient Science
050.description: Study of science in ancient Greece and Rome; consideration of its social context; concentration on the basic concepts of physics the world of medicine and biology the history of mathematics and the practices of astronomy astrology and meteorology.

101.title: Data & Society
101.description: Basic concepts in data science from a socio-cultural perspective. Identifying data stakeholders and their biases, reading and evaluating data documentation, exploring data through analysis and visualization, identifying knowledge gaps, and assessing data ethics.

102.title: Artificial Intelligence in Society
102.description: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in social context. Implications of AI for scientific, legal, educational, economic, and political systems. History of AI research and development. Debates about privacy, security, authenticity, and public policy in the era of AI, with focus on diversity, social justice, and ethical decision-making. Hands-on exercises and projects using AI that generates text and images.

109.title: Visualization in Science: A Critical Introduction
